conceded

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Easy)
  • Why B is Correct: Observing out-of-place alpine granite boulders led Agassiz to propose the scientific hypothesis (posit) that ancient continental ice sheets had carried them there.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (mitigated) = made less severe; C (refuted) = disproved (reverses Agassiz's own ice-age theory!); D (conceded) = reluctantly admitted an opponent's point.
  • Next-Time Clue: [Observation of puzzling natural clue] + [blank] + that [explanatory scientific model] = posited / hypothesized.

questions.stemHtml:
Archaeologists caution that linking an inland Bronze Age weaving workshop to royal Phoenician purple-dye commerce on the basis of a single crushed Murex snail shell rests on ______ footing: solitary shells were frequently traded inland as ornamental charms, whereas industrial dye vats required tens of thousands of crushed shells.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: compelling
ubiquitous
tenuous
conventional

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Medium)
  • Why C is Correct: After the colon, the passage explains why a single snail shell is terrible proof of industrial dye commerce (single shells were ornaments; dye vats needed tens of thousands). Thus the claim rests on weak, shaky (tenuous) footing.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (compelling) means strongly convincing (opposite!); B (ubiquitous) means everywhere; D (conventional) means standard/traditional.
  • Next-Time Clue: Always treat a colon (:) in Words in Context as an = sign defining the blank!

questions.stemHtml:
During the 1854 London cholera outbreak, municipal health boards overwhelmingly ______ the epidemic to noxious "miasma" vapors rising from Thames mudflats; physician John Snow, by contrast, mapped household mortality street by street to demonstrate that cases clustered around a single sewage-contaminated water pump on Broad Street.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: attributed
extrapolated
delineated
entailed

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: Both logic and grammar lock in attributed: health boards regarded [Effect: the epidemic] as caused by to [Proposed Cause: noxious miasma vapors], contrasting (by contrast) with John Snow tracing the true cause to contaminated pump water.
  • Why Distractors Fail: B (extrapolated) = projected outside a dataset (extrapolated X from Y, not to vapors); C (delineated) = outlined boundaries; D (entailed) = necessarily required (does not take "to").
  • Next-Time Clue: Spot the syntactic frame _____ [Effect X] to [Cause Y] → test attributed / ascribed immediately.

questions.stemHtml:
The following text is an original passage in the style of twentieth-century literary fiction.
Every morning in his San Telmo workshop, Master Luthier Don Esteban handed me brass thickness calipers to measure shaved spruce violin bellies down to a tenth of a millimeter, insisting that careless geometry ruined resonance before varnish ever touched wood. Yet whenever a sea captain brought in an old Genoese instrument warped by forty winters along the Río de la Plata, Don Esteban laid the calipers aside, tapped the maple ribs lightly with his knuckle, and told me no dial could predict how damp river air had mellowed a violin's voice until horsehair met the G-string.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.raw: Don Esteban believes brass calipers are useless tools that apprentices should stop using when building new violins.
choices.html: Don Esteban believes brass calipers are useless tools that apprentices should stop using when building new violins.

choices.raw: Although precise physical measurement is essential in violin craft, evaluating an aged instrument's tonal character ultimately requires direct listening and sensory judgment.
choices.html: Although precise physical measurement is essential in violin craft, evaluating an aged instrument's tonal character ultimately requires direct listening and sensory judgment.

choices.raw: Violins constructed in Genoa deteriorate more rapidly in humid river climates than violins built in Buenos Aires.
choices.html: Violins constructed in Genoa deteriorate more rapidly in humid river climates than violins built in Buenos Aires.

choices.raw: The narrator prefers repairing warped sea captains' violins to shaving new spruce violin bellies.
choices.html: The narrator prefers repairing warped sea captains' violins to shaving new spruce violin bellies.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Central Ideas and Details (Easy/Medium — Literature)
  • Why B is Correct: Captures both halves of the paragraph balanced around Yet: Sentence 1 shows Don Esteban demands tenth-of-a-millimeter caliper precision when building new violins, while Sentence 2 (Yet) shows that judging how forty damp winters shaped an old violin's tone requires setting calipers aside and listening to bow on string.
  • Why Distractors Fail:
    • A (Too Extreme): Contradicts Sentence 1 (every morning he handed the narrator brass calipers and insisted geometry mattered!).
    • C (Alien Comparison + Distortion): "Mellowed a violin's voice" is positive/musical, not rapid deterioration, and Genoese vs. Buenos Aires durability is never compared.
    • D (Invented Narrator Preference): The narrator never states a personal preference between tasks.
  • Next-Time Clue: When a literary paragraph pivots with Yet, the main idea must honor the tension between Sentence 1 AND Sentence 2, never erasing Sentence 1.

questions.stemHtml:
Long framed by older maritime histories as an enterprise driven primarily by European appetite for Asian silks and porcelain, the transpacific Manila Galleon trade after 1571 depended just as fundamentally on fiscal transformation inside Ming China. Under the Single Whip Reform, imperial administrators consolidated dozens of regional grain and labor obligations into a single land tax payable exclusively in silver bullion—creating sustained monetary demand in Chinese markets that absorbed over half the silver mined at Potosí in the Andes.

Which choice best states the central claim of the text?

choices.raw: Ming China abandoned silk and porcelain manufacturing after 1571 in order to open domestic silver mines.
choices.html: Ming China abandoned silk and porcelain manufacturing after 1571 in order to open domestic silver mines.

choices.raw: Spanish merchants established the Manila Galleon route to collect land taxes directly from Chinese farmers.
choices.html: Spanish merchants established the Manila Galleon route to collect land taxes directly from Chinese farmers.

choices.raw: Chinese tax reforms mandating silver payments generated crucial demand that helped drive transpacific silver trade, challenging accounts centered solely on European initiative.
choices.html: Chinese tax reforms mandating silver payments generated crucial demand that helped drive transpacific silver trade, challenging accounts centered solely on European initiative.

choices.raw: Silver mined at Potosí was less pure than silver circulated in Ming markets prior to the Single Whip Reform.
choices.html: Silver mined at Potosí was less pure than silver circulated in Ming markets prior to the Single Whip Reform.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Central Ideas and Details (Medium — History)
  • Why C is Correct: Sentence 1 challenges "older maritime histories" that credited European demand alone, arguing the trade "depended just as fundamentally on fiscal transformation inside Ming China"; Sentence 2 explains how the Single Whip silver tax created massive Chinese silver demand.
  • Why Distractors Fail:
    • A (Fabrication): Ming China never abandoned silk or porcelain!
    • B (Absurd Distortion): Spanish merchants traded silver in Manila markets; they did not collect Chinese domestic land taxes.
    • D (Alien Comparison): Silver purity at Potosí vs. earlier Ming silver is never mentioned.
  • Next-Time Clue: Opening participial frames like "Long framed by older histories as X, Phenomenon P depended just as fundamentally on Y" hand you the central claim (Y mattered alongside X, revising X-only accounts) right in Sentence 1!

questions.stemHtml:
Once described in neuroanatomy textbooks merely as passive structural scaffolding supporting neurons, star-shaped glial cells called astrocytes actively regulate interstitial fluid movement through brain tissue during non-REM slow-wave sleep. In controlled experiments on mice, neuroscientists selectively disabled astrocytic aquaporin-4 water channels; although the modified mice slept for the exact same total nightly duration as unmodified control mice, clearance of beta-amyloid metabolic proteins from cortical tissue slowed by sixty percent.

According to the text, what happened when researchers disabled aquaporin-4 water channels in mice?

choices.raw: The mice experienced a sixty percent reduction in nightly non-REM slow-wave sleep duration.
choices.html: The mice experienced a sixty percent reduction in nightly non-REM slow-wave sleep duration.

choices.raw: Neurons took over the waste-clearance duties normally performed by star-shaped astrocytes.
choices.html: Neurons took over the waste-clearance duties normally performed by star-shaped astrocytes.

choices.raw: Beta-amyloid protein production inside cortical neurons ceased completely during wakefulness.
choices.html: Beta-amyloid protein production inside cortical neurons ceased completely during wakefulness.

choices.raw: Metabolic protein clearance from brain tissue dropped sharply even though total sleep time remained unchanged.
choices.html: Metabolic protein clearance from brain tissue dropped sharply even though total sleep time remained unchanged.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Central Ideas and Details (Hard — Neuroscience)
  • Why D is Correct: Matches the exact experimental result in Sentence 2: "although the modified mice slept for the exact same total nightly duration as unmodified control mice, clearance of beta-amyloid metabolic proteins from cortical tissue slowed by sixty percent."
  • Why Distractors Fail:
    • A (Misplaced Number Swap): Transfers "sixty percent" from protein clearance onto sleep duration (which remained exact same!).
    • B (Invented Mechanism): Never stated that neurons took over clearance.
    • C (Confusing Clearance with Production + Extreme): Clearance slowed by 60% during sleep = production ceased completely during wakefulness!
  • Next-Time Clue: Watch out for SAT "Number-Swap Distractors" (Choice A) that attach a genuine passage number (60%) to the wrong noun (sleep duration instead of protein clearance)!

questions.stemHtml:
When severe summer wildfires strip shade-giving fir canopies from mountain streambanks, solar radiation can push shallow creek temperatures above lethal thresholds for juvenile coho salmon. Fluvial ecologists monitoring burned watersheds in Oregon observed, however, that stream reaches impounded by North American beaver dams remained up to 4.5∘C cooler than adjacent undammed reaches: dammed ponds forced surface water downward into gravel beds, displacing cool groundwater back into downstream channels where young salmon congregated.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.raw: To explain a physical mechanism through which one species' habitat modifications buffer another species against post-wildfire heat stress
choices.html: To explain a physical mechanism through which one species' habitat modifications buffer another species against post-wildfire heat stress

choices.raw: To argue that forestry agencies should prioritize extinguishing mountain wildfires over reintroducing North American beavers
choices.html: To argue that forestry agencies should prioritize extinguishing mountain wildfires over reintroducing North American beavers

choices.raw: To compare the dietary preferences of juvenile coho salmon in Oregon with those of salmon in unburned northern watersheds
choices.html: To compare the dietary preferences of juvenile coho salmon in Oregon with those of salmon in unburned northern watersheds

choices.raw: To demonstrate that gravel streambeds absorb more solar radiation than muddy pond bottoms
choices.html: To demonstrate that gravel streambeds absorb more solar radiation than muddy pond bottoms

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Text Structure and Purpose (Easy/Medium — Ecology)
  • Why A is Correct: Abstractly names the exact rhetorical job of the passage: Problem (wildfires strip shade -> lethal creek heat for juvenile coho salmon) → Observed Buffer + Physical Mechanism (beaver dams push water through gravel beds, returning cool groundwater where young salmon congregate). "One species' habitat modifications" = beaver dams; "buffer another species against post-wildfire heat stress" = keep water 4.5∘C cooler for coho salmon!
  • Why Distractors Fail:
    • B (Policy Advocacy Trap): Purely descriptive ecology—forestry policy priorities are never argued.
    • C (Off-Topic): Salmon diets are never mentioned.
    • D (Distortion): Gravel beds cool water via subsurface groundwater exchange, not by absorbing more solar radiation.
  • Next-Time Clue: Translate concrete nouns (beavers, dams, coho salmon) into abstract SAT Purpose categories (one species, habitat modification, another species)!

questions.stemHtml:
Widespread adoption of cloud repositories and high-definition video conferencing led many innovation economists to predict that physical proximity would cease to influence scientific discovery. An audit of forty-two thousand research teams between 2002 and 2023 reveals, however, that coauthors working in the same building filed nearly twice as many breakthrough cross-disciplinary patents as geographically dispersed teams, whereas remote teams outperformed on-site teams primarily in standardized replication and large-scale data cataloging. Sociologists of science suggest that unplanned hallway exchanges prompt researchers to reframe ill-defined questions before formal agendas are even set.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.raw: It summarizes the technological advances that enabled research teams to catalog large datasets remotely after 2002.
choices.html: It summarizes the technological advances that enabled research teams to catalog large datasets remotely after 2002.

choices.raw: It presents empirical findings that challenge the opening prediction while distinguishing between two kinds of scientific output.
choices.html: It presents empirical findings that challenge the opening prediction while distinguishing between two kinds of scientific output.

choices.raw: It offers a sociological explanation for why hallway conversations occur more frequently in university buildings than in corporate labs.
choices.html: It offers a sociological explanation for why hallway conversations occur more frequently in university buildings than in corporate labs.

choices.raw: It concedes that video conferencing has completely replaced in-person collaboration for breakthrough patent filings.
choices.html: It concedes that video conferencing has completely replaced in-person collaboration for breakthrough patent filings.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Text Structure and Purpose — Underlined Sentence Function (Medium/Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Look BEFORE and AFTER:
    • Sentence 1: Prediction that physical proximity wouldn't matter anymore.
    • Sentence 2 (Underlined): Audit of 42,000 teams (empirical findings) + however (challenges opening prediction) + co-located = 2x breakthrough patents, whereas remote = replication & cataloging (distinguishes between two kinds of scientific output).
    • Sentence 3: Sociological explanation (hallway exchanges) for Sentence 2's pattern.
  • Why Distractors Fail:
    • A: Cloud/video technology was Sentence 1, not Sentence 2.
    • C: Sociological hallway explanation is Sentence 3 (and university vs. corporate labs is never compared!).
    • D: Direct opposite of "filed nearly twice as many breakthrough... patents" on-site!
  • Next-Time Clue: Never let an underlined-function trap steal the job of the sentence before it (Trap A) or after it (Trap C)!

questions.stemHtml:
Across several early twentieth-century canvases by Henri Matisse, vibrant cadmium-yellow brushstrokes have gradually faded into chalky beige crusts. Conservators initially attributed this discoloration to prolonged ultraviolet gallery lighting breaking down cadmium sulfide crystals. Yet synchrotron X-ray micro-spectroscopy of unexposed paint edges hidden beneath wooden picture frames revealed identical beige sulfate crusts wherever museum storage humidity exceeded sixty-five percent in the presence of residual synthesis chlorides, prompting museums to pair low-UV LEDs with strict micro-climate dehumidification.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.raw: It praises an artist's pigment choices, criticizes museum curators for neglecting storage rooms, and proposes banning oil-based yellows.
choices.html: It praises an artist's pigment choices, criticizes museum curators for neglecting storage rooms, and proposes banning oil-based yellows.

choices.raw: It contrasts two rival twentieth-century painters, summarizes chemical analyses of their palettes, and concludes both suffered from chloride contamination.
choices.html: It contrasts two rival twentieth-century painters, summarizes chemical analyses of their palettes, and concludes both suffered from chloride contamination.

choices.raw: It introduces an art-conservation puzzle, shows why an initial causal hypothesis proved incomplete, and identifies the chemical condition that guided improved preservation practice.
choices.html: It introduces an art-conservation puzzle, shows why an initial causal hypothesis proved incomplete, and identifies the chemical condition that guided improved preservation practice.

choices.raw: It outlines a chronological history of synchrotron X-ray spectroscopy before illustrating one unexpected failure of the technology.
choices.html: It outlines a chronological history of synchrotron X-ray spectroscopy before illustrating one unexpected failure of the technology.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Text Structure and Purpose — Overall Structure (Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Maps the 3 sentences 1-to-1:
    1. Art-conservation puzzle: Matisse's vibrant cadmium yellows turning into chalky beige crusts.
    2. Initial causal hypothesis: Conservators blamed gallery UV light.
    3. Why incomplete + true chemical driver + improved preservation: Hidden frame-covered paint (zero UV!) formed the exact same crusts when humidity >65% with chlorides, leading museums to combine low-UV LEDs with dehumidification.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A invents scolding curators and banning oil yellows; B invents "two rival painters"; D invents a history of X-ray spectroscopy and a technology failure.
  • Next-Time Clue: Break Overall Structure choices into 3 clauses separated by commas and verify Clause 1 = Beginning, Clause 2 = Middle, Clause 3 = End!

questions.stemHtml:
Text 1
Historically, field travelers encountering whistled speech traditions—such as Silbo Gomero in the Canary Islands—classified them not as full human languages, but as restricted shepherd signal codes capable of transmitting only two or three dozen memorized herding commands across steep volcanic ravines.

Text 2
Acoustic phonetician Julien Meyer recorded Silbo Gomero whistlers conversing across controlled barriers using newly coined sentences containing unfamiliar proper names. By mapping spoken Spanish vowel and consonant formant transitions onto rising and falling whistle pitch contours, listeners accurately transcribed novel sentences they had never heard before, although wind turbulence reduced recognition accuracy at distances exceeding three kilometers.

Based on the texts, how do Meyer's findings in Text 2 relate to the historical classification described in Text 1?

choices.raw: They confirm the historical view that *Silbo Gomero* relies on memorized herding commands rather than Spanish phonetic structures.
choices.html: They confirm the historical view that Silbo Gomero relies on memorized herding commands rather than Spanish phonetic structures.

choices.raw: They suggest *Silbo Gomero* evolved only recently after modern acoustic barriers were installed in the Canary Islands.
choices.html: They suggest Silbo Gomero evolved only recently after modern acoustic barriers were installed in the Canary Islands.

choices.raw: They indicate that wind turbulence prevents *Silbo Gomero* from functioning across steep volcanic ravines of any width.
choices.html: They indicate that wind turbulence prevents Silbo Gomero from functioning across steep volcanic ravines of any width.

choices.raw: They refute the characterization of *Silbo Gomero* as a fixed command code by demonstrating its capacity for open-ended linguistic communication.
choices.html: They refute the characterization of Silbo Gomero as a fixed command code by demonstrating its capacity for open-ended linguistic communication.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Cross-Text Connections (Medium)
  • Why D is Correct: Notice why Day 3's strong verb refute IS justified here!
    • Text 1: Historical travelers claimed Silbo Gomero could transmit only 24–36 memorized herding commands (not open-ended language).
    • Text 2: Meyer proved experimentally that whistlers accurately transmitted newly coined sentences with unfamiliar proper names they had never heard before—directly disproving (refuting) the "fixed memorized command code" claim!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A reverses Text 2; B misreads experimental barriers as evolutionary origin; C exaggerates "exceeding three kilometers" into "ravines of any width."
  • Next-Time Clue: Check when refute IS earned: if Text 1 says "X can ONLY do memorized list L" and Text 2 proves experimentally "X effortlessly does brand-new unmemorized sentences," Text 1's restriction is falsified!

questions.stemHtml:
Text 1
Carbon-offset programs that pay landowners strictly per tree seedling planted frequently backfire ecologically: to maximize rapid payouts, contractors plant dense monocultures of fast-growing non-native eucalyptus that lower local water tables and store less stable soil carbon than diverse native hardwoods. Offset agencies should instead disburse funds only after ten-year ecological audits verify native species survival and soil-carbon accrual.

Text 2
Paying landowners by raw seedling headcount undeniably encourages single-species timber plantations over resilient native ecosystems. Yet withholding all compensation until a ten-year audit concludes would exclude small family farms that cannot afford a decade of uncompensated fencing, weeding, and foregone grazing income; pairing modest annual stewardship stipends with free native-seedling nurseries offers a far more workable reform.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.raw: Reforestation subsidies tied solely to the number of seedlings planted create perverse incentives that work against genuine ecological restoration.
choices.html: Reforestation subsidies tied solely to the number of seedlings planted create perverse incentives that work against genuine ecological restoration.

choices.raw: Delaying all reforestation payments until a ten-year soil-carbon audit concludes is the fairest policy for small family farms.
choices.html: Delaying all reforestation payments until a ten-year soil-carbon audit concludes is the fairest policy for small family farms.

choices.raw: Non-native eucalyptus plantations store substantially more stable soil carbon than mixed native hardwood forests.
choices.html: Non-native eucalyptus plantations store substantially more stable soil carbon than mixed native hardwood forests.

choices.raw: Providing free native seedlings cannot succeed unless seedling-headcount payments are expanded nationwide.
choices.html: Providing free native seedlings cannot succeed unless seedling-headcount payments are expanded nationwide.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Cross-Text Connections — Shared Agreement (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: Look at the opening sentence of both texts:
    • Text 1: "Carbon-offset programs that pay landowners strictly per tree seedling planted frequently backfire ecologically..."
    • Text 2: "Paying landowners by raw seedling headcount undeniably encourages single-species timber plantations over resilient native ecosystems."
    • Although they disagree sharply on the remedy (10-year delayed payout vs. annual stipends + free native nurseries), both authors explicitly agree that per-seedling headcount subsidies create perverse anti-ecological incentives!
  • Why Distractors Fail: B is rejected by Text 2 (excludes small family farms); C contradicts Text 1 (eucalyptus stores less stable carbon); D contradicts both authors' critique of headcount payments.
  • Next-Time Clue: On "both authors would agree" questions, hunt for Text 2's concession sentence ("undeniably," "rightly notes," "while it is true that")—that overlap is 95% of the time the exact correct answer!

questions.stemHtml:
Marine sensory biologists hypothesize that mourning cuttlefish (Sepia plangens) tailor dynamic skin camouflage not merely to match the background texture of the seafloor beneath them, but also to exploit specific visual limitations of whichever predator species is approaching.

Which finding from a controlled aquarium experiment, if true, would most directly support the biologists' hypothesis?

choices.raw: Cuttlefish resting on coarse shell gravel displayed high-contrast mottled skin patterns, whereas cuttlefish resting on fine silt displayed uniform pale skin patterns even when no predators were present.
choices.html: Cuttlefish resting on coarse shell gravel displayed high-contrast mottled skin patterns, whereas cuttlefish resting on fine silt displayed uniform pale skin patterns even when no predators were present.

choices.raw: Cuttlefish darkened their skin patterns within less than half a second after overhead tank lighting was abruptly dimmed.
choices.html: Cuttlefish darkened their skin patterns within less than half a second after overhead tank lighting was abruptly dimmed.

choices.raw: Cuttlefish resting on identical uniform sand displayed polarized arm stripes invisible to color-sighted groupers when approached by groupers, but switched to non-polarized speckled camouflage when approached by polarization-sensitive mantis shrimp.
choices.html: Cuttlefish resting on identical uniform sand displayed polarized arm stripes invisible to color-sighted groupers when approached by groupers, but switched to non-polarized speckled camouflage when approached by polarization-sensitive mantis shrimp.

choices.raw: Mantis shrimp detected stationary plastic prey models faster in clear water than in turbid, algae-rich water.
choices.html: Mantis shrimp detected stationary plastic prey models faster in clear water than in turbid, algae-rich water.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Textual (Medium)
  • Why C is Correct: Apply Lesson 3.2's Two-Half Checklist!
    • Hypothesis: Cuttlefish adjust camouflage (Half 1) not merely to seafloor texture (so hold seafloor constant!), (Half 2) to exploit specific visual limitations of whichever predator approaches.
    • Choice C holds seafloor texture constant ("identical uniform sand") AND shows cuttlefish switching between polarized stripes (invisible to groupers!) vs. non-polarized speckles (when polarization-seeing mantis shrimp approach!).
  • Why Distractors Fail: A only shows seafloor-texture matching without predators (the baseline "not merely..." part!); B tests tank brightness, not predator vision; D doesn't even test cuttlefish!
  • Next-Time Clue: When a hypothesis says "not merely Factor X, but also Factor Y," the winning experiment holds X constant and varies Y!

questions.stemHtml:
In a critical essay on Anna Kovacs's 1898 novel The Harbor Ledger, literary scholar Jin-Woo Park argues that the narrator portrays her father's nightly habit of redrawing coastal navigation charts not as yearning for maritime adventure, but as a psychological refuge offering tidy predictability amid capricious household illness.

Which quotation from The Harbor Ledger most effectively illustrates Park's claim?

choices.raw: *"Three times before his twentieth birthday my father had rounded Cape Horn aboard copper-sheathed tea clippers bound for Falmouth."*
choices.html: "Three times before his twentieth birthday my father had rounded Cape Horn aboard copper-sheathed tea clippers bound for Falmouth."

choices.raw: *"On heavy rag vellum every sunken reef kept its inked margin and every squall obeyed brass dividers—a quiet obedience that my sister's recurring winter fever stubbornly denied our parlor."*
choices.html: "On heavy rag vellum every sunken reef kept its inked margin and every squall obeyed brass dividers—a quiet obedience that my sister's recurring winter fever stubbornly denied our parlor."

choices.raw: *"Merchants from Trieste still praised the accuracy of my father's soundings along the Dalmatian shoals."*
choices.html: "Merchants from Trieste still praised the accuracy of my father's soundings along the Dalmatian shoals."

choices.raw: *"At dawn I unlatched the shutter facing the quay and watched salt fog erase the lighthouse lantern."*
choices.html: "At dawn I unlatched the shutter facing the quay and watched salt fog erase the lighthouse lantern."

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Literary Quotation (Medium/Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Check both halves of Park's literary claim:
    • Half 1 (Tidy predictability on charts): "every sunken reef kept its inked margin and every squall obeyed brass dividers—a quiet obedience..."
    • Half 2 (Refuge amid capricious household illness, NOT adventure yearning): "...that my sister's recurring winter fever stubbornly denied our parlor."
  • Why Distractors Fail: A suggests youthful seafaring adventure (what Park argues against!); C praises commercial accuracy only (misses household illness); D describes harbor fog only.
  • Next-Time Clue: Translate poetic contrast (obeyed brass dividers vs. recurring winter fever stubbornly denied) straight into the critic's two abstract nouns (tidy predictability vs. capricious household illness).

questions.stemHtml:
Performance of Four Solar-Panel Surface Coatings Under Desert Test Conditions

Surface Coating Dry Windborne Dust Removal (%) Morning-Dew Dust Removal (%) Clean-Panel Light Transmission (%)
Uncoated Tempered Glass 12 18 91
Hydrophobic Silica 41 79 93
Nanostructured TiO2​ 38 84 82
Electrostatic Repulsion Film 89 35 90

Photovoltaic engineers testing self-cleaning solar-panel coatings in coastal deserts—where nightly humidity regularly condenses as morning dew—concluded that although nanostructured TiO2​ removes the highest share of dust during morning dew, hydrophobic silica delivers superior overall energy-harvesting suitability for coastal desert arrays.

Which data comparison from the table best supports the engineers' conclusion?

choices.raw: Electrostatic repulsion film removes $89\%$ of dust under dry windborne conditions, compared with only $41\%$ for hydrophobic silica.
choices.html: Electrostatic repulsion film removes 89% of dust under dry windborne conditions, compared with only 41% for hydrophobic silica.

choices.raw: Uncoated tempered glass transmits $91\%$ of incoming light when clean, whereas electrostatic repulsion film transmits $90\%$.
choices.html: Uncoated tempered glass transmits 91% of incoming light when clean, whereas electrostatic repulsion film transmits 90%.

choices.raw: Hydrophobic silica removes $41\%$ of dry dust, exceeding nanostructured $\text{TiO}_2$'s dry dust removal of $38\%$.
choices.html: Hydrophobic silica removes 41% of dry dust, exceeding nanostructured TiO2​'s dry dust removal of 38%.

choices.raw: Nanostructured $\text{TiO}_2$'s small advantage over hydrophobic silica in morning-dew dust removal ($84\%$ vs. $79\%$) comes at the cost of a sharp drop in light transmission ($82\%$ vs. $93\%$, well below even uncoated glass at $91\%$).
choices.html: Nanostructured TiO2​'s small advantage over hydrophobic silica in morning-dew dust removal (84% vs. 79%) comes at the cost of a sharp drop in light transmission (82% vs. 93%, well below even uncoated glass at 91%).

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Quantitative (Medium/Hard)
  • Why D is Correct: Box the engineers' full thesis: Although nanostructured TiO2​ cleans best in morning dew, hydrophobic silica is better overall for energy harvesting in dew-prone coastal deserts. Why would a solar panel that cleans slightly less dew dust (79% vs. 84%) harvest more solar energy? Because Clean-Panel Light Transmission for TiO2​ plunges to 82%, whereas hydrophobic silica transmits 93% of sunlight (even beating uncoated glass at 91%)! Choice D cites both exact pairs of numbers (84% vs. 79% dew cleaning AND 82% vs. 93% light transmission).
  • Why Distractors Fail: A argues against hydrophobic silica using dry-wind conditions (irrelevant/opposing to coastal dew conclusion); B ignores both target coatings; C cites dry wind (41% vs. 38%) rather than explaining why TiO2​'s 84% morning-dew lead loses out on energy harvesting.
  • Next-Time Clue: When an "although X beats Y on Metric 1, Y wins overall" claim appears above a 3-column table, look immediately at Column 3 to see where X collapses and Y excels!

questions.stemHtml:
Radiocarbon-Dated Neolithic Hearths and Surveyed Excavation Area in the Drina Basin

Elevation Zone Period I Hearths (4000–3500 BCE) Period I Area Surveyed (km2) Period II Hearths (3500–3000 BCE) Period II Area Surveyed (km2)
Valley Floor (<500 m) 42 12 19 4
Mid-Slope (500–1,500 m) 18 10 21 10
Alpine Ridge (>1,500 m) 6 8 8 8

Because twentieth-century hydroelectric reservoirs submerged two-thirds of the accessible Period II floodplain strata in the Drina Basin, archaeologists caution that comparing raw hearth counts across eras creates a false impression that Neolithic settlers abandoned the valley floor after 3500 BCE; when normalized for surveyed area, valley-floor settlement intensity actually increased in Period II.

Which calculation from the table directly substantiates the archaeologists' claim?

choices.raw: Valley-floor hearths declined in raw count from $42$ to $19$, yet surveyed valley-floor area shrank from $12\text{ km}^2$ to $4\text{ km}^2$—meaning hearth density rose from $3.5\text{ hearths/km}^2$ in Period I to $4.75\text{ hearths/km}^2$ in Period II.
choices.html: Valley-floor hearths declined in raw count from 42 to 19, yet surveyed valley-floor area shrank from 12 km2 to 4 km2—meaning hearth density rose from 3.5 hearths/km2 in Period I to 4.75 hearths/km2 in Period II.

choices.raw: Mid-slope hearths increased from $18$ in Period I to $21$ in Period II across a constant surveyed area of $10\text{ km}^2$.
choices.html: Mid-slope hearths increased from 18 in Period I to 21 in Period II across a constant surveyed area of 10 km2.

choices.raw: In Period II, raw hearth counts on the mid-slope ($21$) exceeded raw hearth counts on the valley floor ($19$) by $2$ hearths.
choices.html: In Period II, raw hearth counts on the mid-slope (21) exceeded raw hearth counts on the valley floor (19) by 2 hearths.

choices.raw: Alpine ridge hearths accounted for the smallest surveyed area ($8\text{ km}^2$) in both Period I and Period II.
choices.html: Alpine ridge hearths accounted for the smallest surveyed area (8 km2) in both Period I and Period II.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Quantitative Rate Normalization (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: Box the claim: Raw valley-floor hearth counts appear to drop after 3500 BCE, but hearth density per surveyed km2 actually increased in Period II. Compute the valley-floor densities from Row 1:
    • Period I: 12 km242 hearths​=3.5 hearths/km2.
    • Period II: 4 km219 hearths​=4.75 hearths/km2. Choice A is both arithmetically true and logically proves every word of the claim!
  • Why Distractors Fail: B cites Mid-Slope instead of Valley Floor; C compares raw un-normalized Period II counts (repeating the exact fallacy the archaeologists warn against!); D cites Alpine Ridge area only.
  • Next-Time Clue: Whenever a prompt says "when normalized for [area / population / hours]," divide Count ÷ Denominator before reading the choices!

questions.stemHtml:
Transportation researchers mailed complimentary thirty-day municipal bus passes to two randomized groups of car-owning adults in Lyon: Group A had moved to a new neighborhood within the preceding three weeks, whereas Group B had resided at the same address for at least five years. GPS travel diaries showed Group A increased weekly bus trips by 48% during the trial month compared with control newcomers, while Group B increased weekly bus trips by only 6% compared with long-term controls, even though both groups lived within 300 meters of high-frequency stops and rated bus reliability equally high—indicating that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: long-term residents in Lyon live farther from employment centers than newly arrived residents do.
choices.html: long-term residents in Lyon live farther from employment centers than newly arrived residents do.

choices.raw: entrenched daily commuting habits among long-term residents dampen the impact of temporary fare subsidies even when transit proximity and perceived reliability are favorable.
choices.html: entrenched daily commuting habits among long-term residents dampen the impact of temporary fare subsidies even when transit proximity and perceived reliability are favorable.

choices.raw: complimentary thirty-day bus passes permanently eliminate automobile ownership among newly relocated households.
choices.html: complimentary thirty-day bus passes permanently eliminate automobile ownership among newly relocated households.

choices.raw: Group B participants rated bus reliability highly only because they rarely boarded crowded morning buses.
choices.html: Group B participants rated bus reliability highly only because they rarely boarded crowded morning buses.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Inferences (Medium)
  • Why B is Correct: Combine the experimental premises:
    • P1: Both newcomers (Group A) and 5-year residents (Group B) owned cars, got identical free 30-day bus passes, lived ≤300 m from frequent stops, and rated reliability equally high.
    • P2: Yet newcomers boosted bus rides by +48%, whereas long-term residents boosted rides by only +6%!
    • Deduction: Since stop distance and perceived reliability were equal, established routine/habit among settled residents blunts temporary free-fare incentives (Choice B).
  • Why Distractors Fail: A invents commute distance to job centers; C uses extreme "permanently eliminate automobile ownership" from a 30-day trial; D invents a speculation about morning crowding.
  • Next-Time Clue: In controlled experiments where Variables X and Y are held equal (even though both groups lived within 300 m and rated reliability equally high), the inference must trace the outcome gap to the one variable that differed (recent move vs. 5-year settled routine)!

questions.stemHtml:
Rootless parasitic dodder seedlings (Cuscuta pentagona) must locate and coil around a compatible host plant within days of germination by sensing airborne chemical volatiles: untreated seedlings grow consistently toward volatile blends emitted by tomato stems (rich in α-pinene) and grow away from volatile blends emitted by winter wheat (rich in (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate). In dual-chamber bioassays, dodder seedlings grew vigorously toward purified α-pinene alone, yet showed zero directional growth toward healthy tomato stems coated with trace (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate, implying that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: winter wheat stems emit higher concentrations of $\alpha$-pinene than untreated tomato stems do.
choices.html: winter wheat stems emit higher concentrations of α-pinene than untreated tomato stems do.

choices.raw: dodder seedlings cannot detect $\alpha$-pinene unless several other tomato stem compounds are simultaneously present.
choices.html: dodder seedlings cannot detect α-pinene unless several other tomato stem compounds are simultaneously present.

choices.raw: dodder's avoidance of winter wheat is driven at least in part by active chemical repellency from $(Z)$-3-hexenyl acetate capable of overriding attractive host cues, rather than solely by an absence of attractants.
choices.html: dodder's avoidance of winter wheat is driven at least in part by active chemical repellency from (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate capable of overriding attractive host cues, rather than solely by an absence of attractants.

choices.raw: coating winter wheat stems with purified $\alpha$-pinene would prevent wheat from synthesizing $(Z)$-3-hexenyl acetate.
choices.html: coating winter wheat stems with purified α-pinene would prevent wheat from synthesizing (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Inferences (Hard — Chemical Ecology)
  • Why C is Correct: Combine the bioassay puzzle pieces carefully:
    • P1: Dodder grows toward tomato volatiles (α-pinene) and away from wheat volatiles ((Z)-3-hexenyl acetate).
    • P2: Dodder grows vigorously toward purified α-pinene alone (proving α-pinene suffices to attract it).
    • P3: When a real, healthy tomato stem (full of attractive α-pinene!) is dabbed with trace (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate, dodder stops growing toward the tomato completely!
    • Deduction: Wheat avoidance isn't just "wheat lacks α-pinene"—(Z)-3-hexenyl acetate actively repels / overrides attractive tomato signals (Choice C, hedged carefully with "at least in part").
  • Why Distractors Fail: A contradicts P1; B directly contradicts P2 (grew vigorously toward purified α-pinene alone!); D invents internal wheat biosynthesis shutdown.
  • Next-Time Clue: Notice how Choice B fails by contradicting a single clause (purified α-pinene alone)—checking premises one by one eliminates hard science traps cleanly.

questions.stemHtml:
Demographic historians have routinely estimated adult literacy in eighteenth-century rural Normandy by tabulating the percentage of brides and grooms who signed parish marriage registers rather than marking a cross. Curriculum records from rural parish schools, however, show that children were taught to read printed catechisms and almanacs between ages six and nine, whereas quill penmanship—which required costly rag paper, iron ink, and higher tuition—was taught only after age ten, when most peasant daughters had already been withdrawn for seasonal dairy and textile labor. Together, these records suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: rural grooms in eighteenth-century Normandy learned quill penmanship before they learned to read printed almanacs.
choices.html: rural grooms in eighteenth-century Normandy learned quill penmanship before they learned to read printed almanacs.

choices.raw: marriage-register signature counts systematically underestimate the share of eighteenth-century Norman villagers—and especially rural women—who could read printed text.
choices.html: marriage-register signature counts systematically underestimate the share of eighteenth-century Norman villagers—and especially rural women—who could read printed text.

choices.raw: parish schools in urban French ports charged higher penmanship tuition than rural schools in Normandy did.
choices.html: parish schools in urban French ports charged higher penmanship tuition than rural schools in Normandy did.

choices.raw: printed catechisms were rarer than rag writing paper in eighteenth-century Norman farm households.
choices.html: printed catechisms were rarer than rag writing paper in eighteenth-century Norman farm households.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Inferences (Hard — Quantitative History)
  • Why B is Correct: Combine the historical premises:
    • P1: Historians count marriage-register signatures to estimate how many villagers were literate (could read).
    • P2: Rural schools taught reading at ages 6–9, but taught quill writing/signing only after age 10!
    • P3: Most peasant daughters left school before age 10 for farm/textile work (after learning to read, BEFORE learning to sign their names!).
    • Deduction: Many villagers—and disproportionately rural women—could read printed text even though they marked a cross on marriage registers, so signature counts systematically underestimate reading literacy (Choice B)!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A reverses ages 6–9 (reading) vs. 10+ (quill writing); C introduces an Alien Comparison (urban French ports never mentioned!); D compares household book vs. paper rarity beyond the text.
  • Next-Time Clue: Whenever Historians use Proxy Metric M (signatures) to measure Trait T (reading) and archival facts show people acquired T without acquiring M, conclude: M underestimates T!

lessons.title: Lesson 3.4: Priority Advanced Math I — Quadratics, Function Transformations, Polynomial Identities & Radical Equations
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 3.4: Priority Advanced Math I — Quadratics, Function Transformations, Polynomial Identities & Radical Equations
lessons.html:
A. Quadratic Master Toolkit (Faster Than Brute-Force Expanding!)

For ax2+bx+c=0 (a=0):

  1. Sum & Product of Solutions (Vieta's Shortcuts — 3-Second Lifesavers!):
    Sum of solutions (r1​+r2​)=−ab​,Product of solutions (r1​⋅r2​)=ac​
    (Warning: First glance at D=b2−4ac≥0 if the question specifies "real solutions"!)
  2. Function Graph Transformations (g(x)=f(x−h)+k):
    • Inside parentheses (x−h) moves HORIZONTALLY OPPOSITE the sign!
      f(x−5) shifts the graph RIGHT 5 units (every feature's x-coordinate increases by +5: vertex (−2,−9)→(3,−9)!).
      f(x+5) shifts the graph LEFT 5 units.
    • Outside parentheses (+k) moves VERTICALLY WITH the sign!
      +4 shifts UP 4 units; −4 shifts DOWN 4 units.
  3. Polynomial Identity / Coefficient Matching ("true for all values of x"): Whenever (ax+3)(2x−b)=10x2−29x−21 holds for all x, match like powers on both sides:
    • x2 terms: 2a=10⟹a=5.
    • Constant terms: −3b=−21⟹b=7.
    • Always check the middle x term (-35x + 6x = -29x ✓) to catch sign traps!

B. Rational Common Denominators & Radical Extraneous Roots

  • Adding Algebraic Fractions: Never add denominators! x−3A​+x+3B​=(x−3)(x+3)A(x+3)+B(x−3)​=x2−9A(x+3)+B(x−3)​. (Or graph the original expression and choices A–D in Desmos to match curves instantly!)
  • #1 Radical Equation Trap (Extraneous Solutions):
    In mathematics, the radical symbol expression​ denotes the principal (non-negative) square root (9​=+3, never −3!). Squaring both sides of 4x+21​=x destroys negative-sign information and invents fake answers where x<0!
    Non-Negotiable Rule: ALWAYS plug every candidate root back into the original un-squared radical equation (or graph y = sqrt(4x + 21) and y = x in Desmos—Desmos ONLY draws the true principal root!).

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 3.4

  • CC-D3-M1: Without using the quadratic formula, find the sum and product of the solutions to 3x2−21x+11=0.
  • CC-D3-M2: Quadratic p(x) has vertex (4,−7). What is the vertex of q(x)=p(x+6)−2?
  • CC-D3-M3: Why is x=−4 NOT a valid solution to 5x+36​=x, even though (−4)2=5(−4)+36=16?

outline.text: A. Quadratic Master Toolkit (Faster Than Brute-Force Expanding!)
B. Rational Common Denominators & Radical Extraneous Roots
Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 3.4

checks.promptHtml: Without using the quadratic formula, find the sum and product of the solutions to 3x2−21x+11=0.
checks.answerHtml:
For 3x2−21x+11=0 (a=3,b=−21,c=11; check D=(−21)2−4(3)(11)=441−132=309>0):

  • Sum of solutions: −ab​=−3−21​=7.
  • Product of solutions: ac​=311​.

checks.promptHtml: Quadratic p(x) has vertex (4,−7). What is the vertex of q(x)=p(x+6)−2?
checks.answerHtml: Inside p(x+6) shifts LEFT 6 units (4−6=−2); outside −2 shifts DOWN 2 units (−7−2=−9). New vertex: (−2,−9).

checks.promptHtml: Why is x=−4 NOT a valid solution to 5x+36​=x, even though (−4)2=5(−4)+36=16?
checks.answerHtml: Because the radical symbol x​ denotes the principal (non-negative) square root! Substituting x=−4 into the original un-squared equation gives LHS=5(−4)+36​=16​=+4, whereas RHS=−4. Since +4=−4, x=−4 is an extraneous solution created when squaring erased the negative sign.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.5: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis — Squared Units, Percent Wording, Residuals, Conditional Probability & Study Design
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 3.5: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis — Squared Units, Percent Wording, Residuals, Conditional Probability & Study Design
lessons.html:
Problem-Solving and Data Analysis (~15% of SAT Math) is the most English-heavy Math domain—international students rarely miss the arithmetic, but lose points to five English-to-Math translation traps:

1. Squared & Cubed Unit Conversions (1 km2=1,000 m2!)

Always square the linear conversion factor when converting area (and cube it for volume!):

1 km=1,000 m⟹1 km2=(1,000 m)2=1,000,000 m2
1 foot=12 inches⟹1 ft2=144 in2,1 ft3=1,728 in3

2. English Percent Wording Precision

  • "A is what percent of B?" ⟹BA​×100%.
  • "A is what percent GREATER THAN B?" ⟹BA−B​×100% *(Denominator is ALWAYS the noun right after "than" or "of"!)*.
  • Reverse Percent ("After a 20% discount, price is "): Never add 20% of ! Set 0.80P=640⟹P=0.80640​=800.

3. Scatterplots & Residuals

  • Line of Best Fit (y^​): Smooth model prediction; Data dots (y): Actual observed measurements.
  • Residual=Actual y−Predicted y^​ (dots above the line have positive residuals; dots below have negative residuals).

4. Two-Way Table Conditional Probability (Denominator Restriction!)

Read the phrase right after "selected at random from..." or "given that...":

  • "If one item is selected at random from those with Lead-Free Glaze, what is the probability it is Porcelain?"
    ⟹Denominator=Total Lead-Free Glaze ONLY (ignore the grand total of the whole table!).

5. Margin of Error & Causation vs. Association

  • Population Interval from Sample % ± Margin of Error: Multiply (p% - MoE) and (p% + MoE) by the total target population N (not sample size n!).
  • Cause-and-Effect ("causes / leads to"): Requires random assignment of treatments (controlled experiment). Surveys with random sampling only establish correlation/association within the sampled population.

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 3.5

  • CC-D3-M4: Store X sold 90 bikes and Store Y sold 75 bikes. Store X sold what percent more bikes than Store Y?
  • CC-D3-M5: How many square centimeters (1 m=100 cm) are in 2.5 square meters?
  • CC-D3-M6: In a table of 500 voters (200 Rural, 300 Urban), 110 Rural voters support Proposal K. If one Rural voter is chosen at random, what is the denominator of the probability fraction?
