Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 4.4

checks.promptHtml: For what value(s) of k does x2+kx+25=0 have exactly one real solution? (Careful—check BOTH positive and negative k!)
checks.answerHtml: Set discriminant D=b2−4ac=0: k2−4(1)(25)=k2−100=0⟹k2=100⟹k=10 or k=−10.

checks.promptHtml: Simplify x4x5​​ into the form xp (x>0).
checks.answerHtml: x1x5/4​=x45​−44​=x41​.

checks.promptHtml: If M(t)=1,000(0.81)t/2 models mass after t years, by what percent does the mass decrease each year?
checks.answerHtml: Rewrite M(t)=1,000((0.81)1/2)t=1,000(0.90)t. Multiplying by 0.90=1−0.10 each year means a 10% decrease per year (NOT 19% or 9.5%!).

lessons.title: Lesson 4.5: Strategic 5-Second Math Triage (Desmos vs. Manual vs. Bailout) + High-Yield Geometry & Trigonometry
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 4.5: Strategic 5-Second Math Triage (Desmos vs. Manual vs. Bailout) + High-Yield Geometry & Trigonometry
lessons.html:
A. The 5-Second Strategic Decision Matrix

Before writing a single equation on Q12–Q22 of Math, spend 5 seconds choosing the fastest weapon:

Problem Signature Fastest Weapon (Target Time) Exact Execution
Nonlinear system, absolute-value equation, or circle intersection Desmos Graph (15–25 sec) Type both equations directly (x and y); click intersection points!
Equivalent rational identity x−cP(x)​=Q(x)+x−cR​ with unknown constants Desmos Regression ~ (15–25 sec) Define x_1 = [1, 2, 4, 5] (avoiding vertical asymptote x=c!) and type LHS ~ RHS using x_1!
Single clean quadratic D=0, Vieta's −b/a, or trig ratio Manual Formula (20–35 sec) Faster on paper than typing symbols!
3D word problem or abstract geometry constant stalling past 90 seconds Mark & Bailout (90 sec cap) Flag immediately, bank Q18–Q22 solvable items first, return with remaining clock!

B. Four High-Yield Geometry & Trigonometry Pillars (~15% of SAT Math)

  1. Circle Equations (Completing the Square + Desmos Shortcut):
    Standard form: (x−h)2+(y−k)2=r2, with center (h,k) and radius r.
    To convert x2+y2+Ax+By=C: add (2A​)2+(2B​)2 to both sides!
    (Desmos 10-sec backup: type x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y - 11 = 0 directly—Desmos plots the exact circle; click topmost and bottommost points to read diameter 2r and midpoint center!)
  2. Right-Triangle Complementary Angle Theorem (3-Second Free Point!):
    In right △ABC with ∠C=90∘, acute angles satisfy A+B=90∘, so sinA=cosB and cosA=sinB ALWAYS! Also remember Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25.
  3. Circles — Radian Arc Length & Sector Area:
    Full circle =2π radians =360∘. For central angle θ (in radians):
    Fraction of Circle=2πθ​,Arc Length s=rθ,Sector Area A=21​r2θ
  4. Similar 2D & 3D Figures (Scale Factor Power Rule!):
    If all linear dimensions of similar figures scale by factor s:
    • Perimeters / Heights / Radii scale by s1
    • All Areas (base area, lateral area, total surface area) scale by s2
    • Volumes scale by s3 (e.g., if Volume scales by 27=33, linear factor s=3, so Surface Area scales by 32=9, NOT 27!)

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 4.5

  • CC-D4-M4: In a right triangle, sin(28∘)=0.4695. What is cos(62∘)?
  • CC-D4-M5: Find the center and radius of x2+y2+10x−4y=7.
  • CC-D4-M6: Pyramid B is similar to Pyramid A with linear scale factor 4. Pyramid B's surface area is how many times Pyramid A's, and its volume is how many times Pyramid A's?

outline.text: A. The 5-Second Strategic Decision Matrix
B. Four High-Yield Geometry & Trigonometry Pillars (~15% of SAT Math)
Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 4.5

checks.promptHtml: In a right triangle, sin(28∘)=0.4695. What is cos(62∘)?
checks.answerHtml: Since 28∘+62∘=90∘, cos(62∘)=sin(28∘)=0.4695.

checks.promptHtml: Find the center and radius of x2+y2+10x−4y=7.
checks.answerHtml: Complete the square: (x2+10x+25)+(y2−4y+4)=7+25+4=36⟹(x+5)2+(y−2)2=62. Center: (−5,2); Radius: 6.

checks.promptHtml: Pyramid B is similar to Pyramid A with linear scale factor 4. Pyramid B's surface area is how many times Pyramid A's, and its volume is how many times Pyramid A's?
checks.answerHtml: Surface area scales by s2=42=16 times; volume scales by s3=43=64 times.

mathPractice.introHtml:
Explicit Origin Notice: All 16 problems below (MATH-D4-Q1 through MATH-D4-Q16) are original SAT-style practice questions (Q1–Q8: Hard Advanced Math II; Q9–Q16: Geometry, Trigonometry & Strategic Desmos Decision Problems; 10 Multiple-Choice + 6 SPR).
Timed Mastery & 5-Second Triage Target: Set a strict timer for 25 minutes. Before solving each item, write [M] (Manual) or [D] (Desmos) in the margin in 5 seconds, and enforce the 90-second mark-and-return rule! Do not view Section 8 until finished.

questions.stemHtml:
3x2−12x+k=0
In the given equation, k is a constant. If the equation has exactly one real solution, what is the value of k?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Manual Discriminant (18 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: For 3x2−12x+k=0 (a=3,b=−12,c=k), exactly one real solution occurs when D=b2−4ac=0:
    (−12)2−4(3)(k)=0⟹144−12k=0⟹12k=144⟹k=12
  • Desmos Check: Graph y = 3x^2 - 12x + k with slider k = 12 → vertex sits right on the x-axis at (2, 0)!
  • Trap Alert: Writing −122=−144 without parentheses around (−12)2.

questions.stemHtml: For all x>0, which expression is equivalent to x​x23x4​​?

choices.html: x611​
x613​
x617​
x27​

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Manual Exponent Laws (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Convert both radicals using nxm​=xm/n (Power over Root):
    x21​x2⋅x34​​=x2+34​−21​=x612​+68​−63​=x617​
  • Desmos Check (x=64): Type (64^2 * 64^(4/3)) / sqrt(64) → 131072. Test 64^(17/6) → 131072 ✓!
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (11/6) flips 3x4​ upside down as x3/4 or subtracts instead of adding; Trap D (7/2 = 21/6) adds +21​ instead of subtracting −21​ for the denominator!

questions.stemHtml: A laboratory bioreactor is inoculated with 450 microalgae cells. Under constant illumination, the number of microalgae cells in the bioreactor doubles every 12 hours. Which function N models the total number of microalgae cells in the bioreactor t days after inoculation? (1 day=24 hours)

choices.html: N(t)=450(2)12t​
N(t)=450(2)2t
N(t)=450(2)12t
N(t)=900(2)2t

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Concrete Time-Point Plug-In (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Watch the unit switch from hours (every 12 hours) to days (t days, where 1 day=24 hours)!
    • At t=0 days: N(0)=450.
    • At t=1 day (24 hours=two 12-hour doublings!): 45012 hr​90024 hr​1,800.
    • Test t=1 in the choices:
  • A: 450(2)1/12≈477 ✗
  • B: 450(2)2(1)=450×4=1,800 ✓!
  • C: 450(2)12 (huge!) ✗
  • D: 900(2)2=3,600 (wrong initial value N(0)=900!) ✗

questions.stemHtml:
f(x)=2x2−5
g(x)=3x−4
For the functions f and g defined above, what is the value of f(g(3))?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Inside-Out Evaluation (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Inner function first: g(3)=3(3)−4=9−4=5.
    2. Outer function second: f(g(3))=f(5)=2(5)2−5=2(25)−5=50−5=45.
  • Trap Alert: Computing g(f(3)) backwards (f(3)=13⟹g(13)=35 — wrong order!) or squaring (2×5)2=100 instead of 2(52)=50.

questions.stemHtml:
yy​=x2−6x+14=2x−c​
In the system of equations above, c is a constant. If the system has exactly one real solution (x,y), what is the value of c?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Tie (25 seconds either way!)
  • Algebraic Discriminant Solution:
    1. Set y=y and collect all terms on one side:
      x2−6x+14=2x−c⟹x2−8x+(14+c)=0
    2. For exactly one real solution, set D=b2−4ac=0:
      (−8)2−4(1)(14+c)=0⟹64−56−4c=0⟹8−4c=0⟹c=2
  • Desmos Slider Method: Graph y = x^2 - 6x + 14 and y = 2x - c with slider c. At c = 2, the line y = 2x - 2 touches the parabola at a single tangent point (4, 6)!

questions.stemHtml:
2x2−10x+c=0
In the given equation, c is a constant and the equation has two real solutions, r and s. If r2+s2=19, what is the value of c?

choices.html: 3
6
12
31

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Vieta's Sum-of-Squares Identity (30 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: For 2x2−10x+c=0:
    1. Sum of roots: r+s=−2−10​=5.
    2. Product of roots: rs=2c​.
    3. Substitute into r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs:
      19=(5)2−2(2c​)⟹19=25−c⟹c=6
    4. Quick discriminant sanity check: D=(−10)2−4(2)(6)=100−48=52>0 ✓ (real roots confirmed!).
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (12) forgets to divide c by a=2 in rs=c/a (solving 25−2c=19⟹c=3, Choice A, or doubling 6→12)!

questions.stemHtml:
V(t)=800(1.21)2t​
The function V models the value, in dollars, of a rare botanical lithograph t years after an archive acquired it. According to the model, by what percent does the value of the lithograph increase each year?

choices.html: 10%
10.5%
21%
42%

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Rewrite Base Exponent (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Isolate t in the exponent using (am)n=amn:
    V(t)=800(1.21)2t​=800((1.21)21​)t=800(1.21​)t=800(1.10)t
    Since 1.10=1+0.10, the value increases by 10% each year!
  • Concrete Check: V(0)=800; V(1)=800(1.21)0.5=880. Percent increase in 1 year =800880−800​=80080​=10% ✓!
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (21%) is the 2-year growth rate; Trap B (10.5%) divides 21%÷2 linearly instead of taking the square root 1.21​=1.10!

questions.stemHtml:
yx+y​=x2−3x−4=11​
If (x1​,y1​) and (x2​,y2​) are the two real solutions to the system of equations above and x1​>0, what is the value of x1​?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [D] Desmos Intersection (12 seconds!)
  • Desmos Fastest Path: Type y = x^2 - 3x - 4 on Line 1 and x + y = 11 on Line 2 → click the two intersections at (-3, 14) and (5, 6). Since x1​>0, enter 5!
  • Manual Algebra: Substitute y=11−x: 11−x=x2−3x−4⟹x2−2x−15=0⟹(x−5)(x+3)=0⟹x1​=5.
  • Trap Alert: Entering 6 (the y-coordinate at (5,6) instead of x1​!).

questions.stemHtml: In right triangle ABC, the measure of ∠C is 90∘. If sinA=419​, what is the value of cosB?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Complementary Angle Theorem (5 seconds!)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: In right △ABC with ∠C=90∘, acute angles A and B satisfy A+B=90∘, so cosB=sinA=9/41 (4 characters—type 9/41 directly into the SPR box rather than rounding a long decimal!).

questions.stemHtml:
x2+y2−8x+6y−11=0
In the xy-plane, the graph of the given equation is a circle. What is the length of the radius of this circle?
questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Tie (20 seconds)
  • Completing the Square:
    (x2−8x+16)+(y2+6y+9)=11+16+9=36⟹(x−4)2+(y+3)2=62⟹r=6
  • Desmos 10-Second Visual Check: Type x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y - 11 = 0. Click topmost point (4, 3) and bottommost point (4, -9): vertical diameter =3−(−9)=12⟹ radius =12÷2=6!
  • Trap Alert: Entering 36 (r2 instead of r!).

questions.stemHtml: In right triangle PQR, ∠Q is a right angle, tanP=125​, and the length of hypotenuse PR is 39. What is the length of side QR (the leg opposite ∠P)?

choices.html: 13
15
36
37.5

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Scaled Pythagorean Triple (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: In right △PQR (∠Q=90∘):
    tanP=adjacent (PQ)opposite (QR)​=125​
    Let QR=5k and PQ=12k. By the 5-12-13 right triangle ratio, hypotenuse PR=13k=39⟹k=3. Therefore, QR=5(3)=15!
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (36) solves for adjacent leg PQ=12(3)=36 instead of opposite leg QR; Trap D (37.5) sets 39QR​=125​ (confusing tanP with sinP!).

questions.stemHtml: In a circle with radius 12 centimeters, central angle ∠AOB has a measure of 65π​ radians. What is the area, in square centimeters, of sector AOB?

choices.html: 10π
30π
60π
120π

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Sector Area Formula (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Use Asector​=21​r2θ (or fraction 2πθ​⋅πr2):
    Asector​=21​(12)2(65π​)=72×65π​=12×5π=60π
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (10\pi) computes arc length rθ=12(65π​)=10π; Trap D (120\pi) forgets the 21​ in 21​r2θ!

questions.stemHtml: Right circular cylinder A and right circular cylinder B are similar. The volume of cylinder B is 27 times the volume of cylinder A. If the lateral surface area of cylinder A is 14π square centimeters, what is the lateral surface area, in square centimeters, of cylinder B?

choices.html: 42π
84π
98π
126π

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Scale Factor Power Rule (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Volume ratio gives linear scale factor s:
      VA​VB​​=s3=27⟹s=327​=3
    2. Every surface area (including lateral area!) scales by s2:
      AreaA​AreaB​​=s2=32=9⟹AreaB​=9×14π=126π
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (42\pi) multiplies by s=3 instead of s2=9; multiplying 27×14π=378π confuses volume scaling with area scaling!

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, line segment AB is a diameter of a circle. If the coordinates of point A are (−3,7) and the coordinates of point B are (5,−1), which equation represents this circle?

choices.html: (x−1)2+(y−3)2=32
(x−1)2+(y−3)2=128
(x+1)2+(y+3)2=32
(x−4)2+(y+4)2=32

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Midpoint + Plug-In (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Center (h,k)= midpoint of diameter A(−3,7) and B(5,−1):
      (h,k)=(2−3+5​, 27+(−1)​)=(1,3)
      (Eliminates C and D immediately!)
    2. Plug endpoint B(5,−1) into (x−1)2+(y−3)2=r2:
      r2=(5−1)2+(−1−3)2=42+(−4)2=16+16=32⟹Choice A!
  • Trap Alert: Trap B (128) uses full diameter squared d2=82+(−8)2=128 instead of radius squared r2=32!

questions.stemHtml:
x−34x2−9x+7​=4x+a+x−3b​
The equation above is true for all x=3, where a and b are constants. What is the value of a+b?

choices.html: 7
13
19
25

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [D] Desmos Regression ~ (15 seconds!)
  • Desmos 15-Second Regression Method:
    • Line 1: x_1 = [1, 2, 4, 5] (avoid x=3!)
    • Line 2: (4x_1^2 - 9x_1 + 7)/(x_1 - 3) ~ 4x_1 + a + b/(x_1 - 3)
    • Desmos displays a = 3 and b = 16 with R² = 1 ⟹a+b=3+16=19!
  • Manual Algebraic Identity Method: Multiply both sides by (x−3):
    4x2−9x+7=(4x+a)(x−3)+b=4x2+(a−12)x+(−3a+b)
    • Match x coefficient: a−12=−9⟹a=3.
    • Match constant (or plug x=3 into 4x2−9x+7): b=4(9)−9(3)+7=16.
    • Sum: a+b=3+16=19.

questions.skill: Right Circular Cone Volume & Slant Height
questions.stemHtml: A right circular cone has a volume of 96π cubic centimeters and a circular base with a diameter of 12 centimeters. What is the slant height, in centimeters, of the cone?

choices.html: 8
10
213​
237​

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Second Triage: [M] Reference Formula + Pythagorean Triple (30 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Diameter Trap Check: Diameter =12 cm⟹ radius r=6 cm!
    2. Find vertical height h from cone volume V=31​πr2h:
      96π=31​π(6)2h=12πh⟹h=1296​=8 cm
    3. Slant height ℓ is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by radius r=6 and vertical height h=8 (6-8-10 Pythagorean triple!):
      ℓ=r2+h2​=62+82​=100​=10 cm
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (8) stops at vertical height h=8 instead of slant height ℓ; Trap D (2\sqrt{37}) uses diameter 12 as the radius (h=2⟹122+22​=148​=237​)!

subSections.title: A. Lesson Short Comprehension Checks — Answer Key
subSections.titleHtml: A. Lesson Short Comprehension Checks — Answer Key
subSections.html:
Reading & Writing Checks (CC-D4-RW1 to CC-D4-RW7)

  • CC-D4-RW1: Select Choice C (preclude) immediately with 100% confidence! Because you verified that Choices A (substantiate), B (bolster), and D (concede) all violate "make impossible," they have a 0% chance of being right. Never pick a known wrong word out of familiarity bias, and never eliminate an unknown word just because it is unfamiliar.
  • CC-D4-RW2: Stopped, halted, or prevented chloride corrosion from progressing further (secondary academic verb meaning of arrest, NOT police action!).
  • CC-D4-RW3: Contrast (However, / By contrast,) — Sentence 1 highlights 2,000-year Roman concrete durability (+), while Sentence 2 contrasts 50-year modern concrete cracking (-). Consequently, fails because Roman durability did not cause modern piers to crack!
  • CC-D4-RW4: That is, restates the exact same idea from Sentence 1 in clearer or more specific words (Sentence 2 = Sentence 1), whereas Moreover, introduces a brand-new, additional supporting point (Sentence 2 = Extra Point #2).
  • CC-D4-RW5: Because an audience unfamiliar with the architect has no idea who "her" is or what "her earlier bridges in Zurich" refers to! For an unfamiliar audience, the correct choice must introduce her full name/identity explicitly rather than presupposing prior knowledge.
  • CC-D4-RW6: Cancel both negatives (far from + trivial): "The archival gap is very important / significant."
  • CC-D4-RW7: Dangling modifier! A treatise (book) was not celebrated for calculating comet orbits—astronomer Edmond Halley was! Fix: "Celebrated for calculating comet orbits accurately, Edmond Halley predicted in his 1705 treatise that a bright periodic comet would return in 1758."

Math Checks (CC-D4-M1 to CC-D4-M6)

  • CC-D4-M1: Set discriminant D=b2−4ac=0: k2−4(1)(25)=k2−100=0⟹k2=100⟹k=10 or k=−10.
  • CC-D4-M2: x1x5/4​=x45​−44​=x41​.
  • CC-D4-M3: Rewrite M(t)=1,000((0.81)1/2)t=1,000(0.90)t. Multiplying by 0.90=1−0.10 each year means a 10% decrease per year (NOT 19% or 9.5%!).
  • CC-D4-M4: Since 28∘+62∘=90∘, cos(62∘)=sin(28∘)=0.4695.
  • CC-D4-M5: Complete the square: (x2+10x+25)+(y2−4y+4)=7+25+4=36⟹(x+5)2+(y−2)2=62. Center: (−5,2); Radius: 6.
  • CC-D4-M6: Surface area scales by s2=42=16 times; volume scales by s3=43=64 times.

subSections.title: B. Vocabulary Retrieval & Exercises (4A & 4C) — Answer Key
subSections.titleHtml: B. Vocabulary Retrieval & Exercises (4A & 4C) — Answer Key
subSections.html:
Section 4A: Cumulative Days 1–3 Mixed Vocabulary Quiz (SR-D4-Q1 to SR-D4-Q15)

  • SR-D4-Q1: corroborated (confirmed independently across two ice/bog archives).
  • SR-D4-Q2: underscored ("Rather than weakening" rules out undermined; frog die-off emphasized the warning).
  • SR-D4-Q3: ambiguous (broken verb suffix leaves two valid competing translations).
  • SR-D4-Q4: concede (admit an initial drawback before pivoting with yet to long-term clean power).
  • SR-D4-Q5: disparate (tree rings, grain prices, and tax rolls are fundamentally different kinds of archives).
  • SR-D4-Q6: mitigate (lessen/cushion flood severity without eliminating typhoons).
  • SR-D4-Q7: notwithstanding (postposed "despite harsh Arctic darkness").
  • SR-D4-Q8: entails (necessarily requires 24-hour HEPA filtration).
  • SR-D4-Q9: caveat (methodological caution/limitation after the colon).
  • SR-D4-Q10: attribute (matches attribute [dry summers] to [royal impiety]).
  • SR-D4-Q11: tenuous (weak/flimsy support from one blurry sonar ping).
  • SR-D4-Q12: Any two of substantiate, corroborate, or bolster.
  • SR-D4-Q13: empirical (based on observation/experiment).
  • SR-D4-Q14: tentative.
  • SR-D4-Q15: ubiquitous.

Exercise 4C-1: Medium/Hard Words in Context (VOC-D4-Q1 to VOC-D4-Q4)

  • VOC-D4-Q1 → B (circumvent): Setting up stalls just outside the city moat allowed non-citizen painters to work around / bypass (circumvent) Antwerp's guild ban. Notice how known Day 1/4 words A (corroborate), C (proliferate), and D (substantiate) all fail "get around a rule"!
  • VOC-D4-Q2 → A (equivocal): Although contrasts early leaky-crystal dates with newer unequivocal (crystal-clear) dates—so early results were inconclusive / uncertain (equivocal). B (pragmatic), C (ubiquitous), and D (compelling — opposite of leaky uncertainty!) all fail the Although ... unequivocal contrast.
  • VOC-D4-Q3 → C (ostensibly): Classic surface-vs.-reality frame! On paper / supposedly (ostensibly) the ordinance promoted sanitation, yet councilors selectively used it to crush pushcart competitors of their own indoor arcades. A (unequivocally) misses the hypocrisy; B (pragmatically) and D (conversely) fail the framed as X, yet in reality Y logic.
  • VOC-D4-Q4 → D (preclude): Human cultivation of sweet potatoes does not rule out / make impossible (preclude) natural ocean-current floating, even though linguistic evidence favors human voyages. A (engender), B (ameliorate), and C (underscore) all make the sentence illogical.

Exercise 4C-2: Role Mapping (VOC-D4-Q5 to VOC-D4-Q8)

  • VOC-D4-Q5: (d) Two-Way Mutual Exchange (reciprocity = borrow in spring ↔ return seeds in autumn).
  • VOC-D4-Q6: (a) Compact Mid-Sentence Concession (albeit = lower energy density -, although with lower cost/fire risk +).
  • VOC-D4-Q7: (c) Rapid Multiplication (proliferated = coastal dead zones multiplied rapidly worldwide).
  • VOC-D4-Q8: (b) Surface Excuse vs. Hidden Reality (ostensibly = outwardly open to all, though actually restricted to six big publishers).

Exercise 4C-3: Academic Sentence Completion (VOC-D4-Q9 to VOC-D4-Q13)

  • VOC-D4-Q9: ameliorate (improve/relieve storm-surge soil salinization).
  • VOC-D4-Q10: pragmatic (practical, fast, realistic 6-month bus-lane solution).
  • VOC-D4-Q11: engender (give rise to / spark household anxiety).
  • VOC-D4-Q12: precludes (makes year-round unescorted shipping impossible).
  • VOC-D4-Q13: albeit (compact concession phrase "albeit with narrow frequency range...").

Exercise 4C-4: Lookalike & Polysemy Trap Drill (VOC-D4-Q14 to VOC-D4-Q18)

  • VOC-D4-Q14: preclude — prelude is a noun meaning musical/literary introduction; spiders lacking wings does not rule out (preclude) wind dispersal!
  • VOC-D4-Q15: engender — open-source code generates/sparks (engenders) replication rather than putting it in danger (endangers)!
  • VOC-D4-Q16: equivocal — 3 warming cores vs. 3 cooling cores makes the regional trend inconclusive/mixed (equivocal), not "equal in value" (equivalent).
  • VOC-D4-Q17: (b) halts/stops — polyethylene glycol stops/prevents cellular collapse during drying.
  • VOC-D4-Q18: First blank = exacerbate (paving worsens runoff); Second blank = ameliorate (marshes improve/reduce flooding).

Exercise 4C-5: Closed-Notes Rapid Retrieval Quiz (VOC-D4-Q19 to VOC-D4-Q28)

(Grade for accurate core meaning in your own simple English words)

  • VOC-D4-Q19 (albeit): Although; even though (compact qualifying phrase).
  • VOC-D4-Q20 (circumvent): Find a clever way around an obstacle or rule.
  • VOC-D4-Q21 (preclude): Make impossible in advance; rule out completely.
  • VOC-D4-Q22 (proliferate): Multiply, spread, or increase rapidly in number.
  • VOC-D4-Q23 (engender): Cause, generate, or give rise to a state/feeling.
  • VOC-D4-Q24 (equivocal): Unclear, inconclusive, or open to two interpretations.
  • VOC-D4-Q25 (pragmatic): Practical and realistic rather than idealistic.
  • VOC-D4-Q26 (ostensibly): Supposedly on the surface (hiding a different reality).
  • VOC-D4-Q27 (ameliorate): Make a bad or harmful condition better.
  • VOC-D4-Q28 (reciprocity): Two-way mutual give-and-take benefiting both sides.

subSections.title: C. Reading & Writing Practice Questions (RW-D4-Q1 to RW-D4-Q20) — Detailed Explanations
subSections.titleHtml: C. Reading & Writing Practice Questions (RW-D4-Q1 to RW-D4-Q20) — Detailed Explanations
subSections.html:
RW-D4-Q1 → Correct Answer: B (pragmatic)

  • Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Medium)
  • Why B is Correct: After the colon, cities rejected aesthetically uniform single-species planting in favor of a practical, risk-smart (pragmatic) 10% genus cap so no single pest could wipe out street shade again.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (tentative) = hesitant/unconfirmed (mandating a strict 10% cap is decisive, not tentative!); C (tenuous) = flimsy; D (conventional) = traditional (contradicts abandoning the old single-species habit).
  • Next-Time Clue: Contrasting "picturesque ideal" against "workable risk-reduction rule" points straight to pragmatic.

RW-D4-Q2 → Correct Answer: C (arrests)

  • Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context — Secondary Polysemy (Medium/Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Whereas sets up a direct opposite against "absorbs sunlight and accelerates ablation [melting]"! Thick debris insulates the ice and halts / checks / slows down (arrests) seasonal melt rates.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (engenders = causes) and B (proliferates = multiplies) move in the wrong direction (increasing melt); D (asserts = declares) makes zero physical sense.
  • Next-Time Clue: Whenever ordinary verbs (arrest, check, harbor, yield, afford) appear on Hard WIC, test their formal scientific verb definitions before crossing them out!

RW-D4-Q3 → Correct Answer: A (ostensibly)

  • Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: ...built as philanthropic model villages...; economic historians note, however, that tying cottage leases directly to weekly loom quotas prevented families from striking... Classic surface humanitarian claim vs. coercive economic reality → ostensibly!
  • Why Distractors Fail: B (unequivocally) = without a doubt (contradicts however); C (pragmatically) misses the pretense/reality contrast; D (empirically) = by experiment (nonsensical modifier for "built as philanthropic villages").
  • Next-Time Clue: [Noble stated purpose] + ; however, [self-serving coercive mechanism] = ostensibly / purportedly / nominally.

RW-D4-Q4 → Correct Answer: B (equivocal)

  • Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context (Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Because hydrophones cannot distinguish 10 whales × 1 call from 1 whale × 10 calls, acoustic tallies alone yield ambiguous, inconclusive (equivocal) population estimates unless paired with visual boat counts.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (compelling) means convincingly clear (opposite!); C (ubiquitous) means everywhere; D (reciprocal) means mutual two-way exchange.
  • Next-Time Clue: "Without revealing whether Case X or Case Y occurred" = two indistinguishable interpretations = ambiguous / equivocal.

RW-D4-Q5 → Correct Answer: C (circumvented)

  • Skill & Domain: Craft and Structure · Words in Context — Elimination Practice (Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Even if you forgot circumvented, run Lesson 4.1's Unknown-Option Protocol on the three Days 1–3 words: merchants faced a guild ban on direct cocoon purchases and used upfront orchard loans labeled as debt repayments to get around those controls. Does that mean A (corroborated = confirmed)? No! B (underscored = emphasized)? No! D (conceded = reluctantly admitted)? No! C (circumvented = bypassed) wins both by direct meaning and 100% elimination!

RW-D4-Q6 → Correct Answer: B (instead,)

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Transitions (Medium)
  • Why B is Correct: Sentence 2 Clause 1 states what the underground orchid never does (never emerges above leaf litter to photosynthesize); Clause 2 states what it does in place of photosynthesizing (remains completely dependent on its fungus for life). [Negative: never does X]; instead, [does Y] is a textbook replacement bridge!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (nevertheless,) would mean "despite never photosynthesizing, it still depends on fungi" (illogical—not photosynthesizing is why it depends on fungi, not an obstacle to depending on them!); C (for example,) and D (conversely,) misread the negative-to-replacement structure.
  • Next-Time Clue: Spot [Subject does NOT do X]; _____, [Subject does alternative Y] → test instead, / rather, first!

RW-D4-Q7 → Correct Answer: A (Moreover,)

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Transitions (Medium)
  • Why A is Correct:
    • Idea 1: Fathy favored mud brick for thermal regulation (+ Advantage #1).
    • Idea 2: Mud brick could be made locally at tiny cost (+ Advantage #2). Adding a second distinct advantage supporting the same thesis requires Moreover,!
  • Why Distractors Fail: B (However,) and D (Regardless,) signal contrast (+ vs. -); C (Consequently,) falsely claims thermal warmth caused canal silt to be cheap!

RW-D4-Q8 → Correct Answer: B (in other words,)

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Transitions (Medium/Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Compare the clause right before the semicolon with the clause right after:
    • Before ;: Grasses already covered floodplains 21 million years ago (compared with antelopes at 10 million years ago in Sentence 1).
    • After ;: Abundant grass habitats preceded grazing mammal dentition by more than 10 million years (21−10=11>10). Clause 2 translates the raw million-year numbers into their exact plain-language takeaway → in other words,!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (nonetheless,) and C (by contrast,) wrongly pit 21 Ma against "preceded by >10 Ma" (the contrast already happened between Sentence 1 and Sentence 2's opening!); D (likewise,) requires a second parallel species/region.

RW-D4-Q9 → Correct Answer: C (Accordingly,)

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Transitions (Hard)
  • Why C is Correct:
    • Idea 1 (Cause): Coriolis deflection bends air masses in each hemisphere (driving storm spin).
    • Idea 2 (Physical Consequence): Hurricanes never cross the equator, where Coriolis deflection drops to zero. Accordingly, (= therefore / as a logical result) links physical law to meteorological consequence.
  • Why Distractors Fail: Trap A (Fittingly,) is a classic Hard SAT trap! Fittingly, is ONLY used when something's name or fate poetically matches an earlier detail (e.g., "Named after Vulcan, the Roman god of fire... Fittingly, it spews lava"). Coriolis's French surname has no poetic pun about the equator! B (Even so,) and D (Alternatively,) violate cause-and-effect.

RW-D4-Q10 → Correct Answer: D (conversely,)

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Transitions (Hard)
  • Why D is Correct: Symmetrical two-part opposite on the same glass object:
    • Part 1 (Bulbous head): Withstands direct steel hammer blows without cracking.
    • Part 2 (Hair-thin tail): Snapping 1 mm shatters the entire drop into powder instantly! Conversely, marks that dramatic opposite behavior at the opposite end of the drop.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (therefore,) claims surviving hammer blows causes tail shattering; B (similarly,) and C (indeed,) signal sameness/reinforcement rather than opposite vulnerability.

RW-D4-Q11 → Correct Answer: B

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis (Medium)
  • Why B is Correct: Check all 3 Goal Constraints (explain how kintsugi differs [1] visually and [2] philosophically from [3] conventional invisible ceramic repair):
    • [3] Contrast with invisible repair: "Rather than hiding fractures with clear adhesives,"
    • [1] Visual difference: "highlights mend lines in gold- or silver-dusted urushi lacquer,"
    • [2] Philosophical difference: "honoring breakage and repair as visible parts of a vessel's history."
  • Why Distractors Fail: A discusses polymer heat resistance (wrong bullet!); C is vague meta-commentary with zero specifics; D omits both the philosophical meaning and the contrast with invisible repair.

RW-D4-Q12 → Correct Answer: C

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis (Medium/Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Goal asks for the specific procedure used to sample water without contamination. Choice C states every procedural step in order (stopped just above the water → reduced shaft pressure so lake water rose and froze inside the borehole → later extracted that clean ice).
  • Why Distractors Fail: A explains why the lake is liquid, not how it was sampled; B states only the goal (avoiding contamination), omitting how they achieved it; D states only that they succeeded, omitting the pressure-freeze mechanism.

RW-D4-Q13 → Correct Answer: C

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis (Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Goal requires (1) emphasizing the magnitude of P. oceanica's carbon storage (2) by comparing it directly with another seagrass species. Choice C contrasts Zostera marina (140 metric tons/ha) directly against Posidonia oceanica (over 1,000 metric tons/ha)!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A compares seagrasses to seaweeds and mentions anchor damage without storage numbers; B states P. oceanica's 1,000 t/ha without comparing it to another seagrass (Half-Goal Trap!); D groups them together vaguely without numbers or contrast.

RW-D4-Q14 → Correct Answer: C

  • Skill & Domain: Expression of Ideas · Rhetorical Synthesis (Hard)
  • Why C is Correct: Goal requires (1) introducing Dr. Gladys West's core achievement (algorithms modeling the geoid for GPS accuracy) (2) to a general audience unfamiliar with the term geoid (so geoid MUST be defined!). Choice C seamlessly embeds an appositive definition (modeled the geoid—Earth's irregular gravitational shape—with the precision needed to make modern GPS accurate).
  • Why Distractors Fail: Trap A leaves the geoid completely undefined (failing the "unfamiliar audience" constraint!); B defines geoid without mentioning Dr. Gladys West at all; D reverses cause/effect and omits both geoid and GPS.

RW-D4-Q15 → Correct Answer: B

  • Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Quantitative (Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Box every piece of the hypothesis: Whereas other chaparral shrubs germinate mainly from heat alone OR smoke alone, Adenostoma fasciculatum requires BOTH cues together (synergistic dual-cue dormancy). To prove synergy (neither cue works well alone, both together surge), you must cite:
    1. Single-cue specialists for contrast (Ceanothus =76% heat alone; Salvia =68% smoke alone), AND
    2. Adenostoma staying low under both single cues (14% heat alone AND 18% smoke alone) before jumping to 84% when combined! Choice B supplies the complete proof.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A cites only the 84% combined column (without single-cue numbers, Adenostoma might have hit 82% with heat alone!); C cites untreated controls only; D omits Adenostoma's smoke-only rate (18%), failing to rule out that smoke water alone caused the 84% germination!

RW-D4-Q16 → Correct Answer: B

  • Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Inferences (Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Combine the exact arithmetic + welfare premises after however, because:
    • P1: Thermostat rebound offsets 1/4 (25%) of projected fuel savings, leaving 3/4 (75%) of the energy savings intact ⟹ "diminishes—but far from eliminates—net energy savings."
    • P2: Warmer winter indoor temperatures "simultaneously improv[e] household thermal comfort" ⟹ "delivers measurable welfare gains to residents."
  • Why Distractors Fail: A confuses a 1/4 partial offset with >100% "backfire" (using more energy than before); C speculates beyond the text; D blames lab testing error rather than household thermostat behavior.

RW-D4-Q17 → Correct Answer: A

  • Skill & Domain: Information and Ideas · Command of Evidence — Textual Reconciliation (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: Use Day 1's verb reconcile! How can both of these statements be true at once?
    • Fact 1 (New Protein Correction): The charred campfire eggshells came from small brush-turkeys, NOT giant Genyornis.
    • Hypothesis 2: Early human foraging still contributed to Genyornis extinction. Choice A bridges the exact gap: humans harvested giant Genyornis eggs by cutting perforation holes to drain them raw without charring them in campfires—explaining both why Genyornis disappeared from human egg predation AND why campfire-charred fragments belonged to brush-turkeys!
  • Why Distractors Fail: B explains why brush-turkeys survived, not how humans affected Genyornis; C argues for climate rather than human foraging; D discusses protein preservation by moisture, not campfire species identity.

RW-D4-Q18 → Correct Answer: D

  • Skill & Domain: Standard English Conventions · Form, Structure, and Sense — Hard Dangling Modifier (Hard)
  • Why D is Correct: Ask "What was distilled from steam-heated leaves of the Malagasy Ravensara aromatica tree?" The volatile essential oil! Notice how Choices A (agronomists), B (cacao beans), and C (experiments) are all passive/active disguises that place the wrong noun immediately after the comma! Only D (the volatile essential oil) places the true distilled substance right after the comma.

RW-D4-Q19 → Correct Answer: B (Dubrovnik, Croatia;)

  • Skill & Domain: Standard English Conventions · Boundaries — Semicolon Super-Commas (Hard)
  • Why B is Correct: Look at the rest of the three-harbor list after the blank: ...Venice, Italy; and Marseille, France. Because list items contain internal commas (City, Country and the appositive Ragusa, present-day Dubrovnik, Croatia), semicolons must separate the three major list items, while a comma separates Dubrovnik from Croatia:
    1. Ragusa, present-day Dubrovnik, Croatia;
    2. Venice, Italy;
    3. and Marseille, France.
  • Why Distractors Fail: A uses a comma instead of a semicolon to end Item 1 (breaking parallel list hierarchy with ; and); C and D wrongly split Dubrovnik from its own country Croatia with a semicolon!

RW-D4-Q20 → Correct Answer: A (decomposition—lie)

  • Skill & Domain: Standard English Conventions · Form, Structure, and Sense + Boundaries (Hard)
  • Why A is Correct: Solves two simultaneous Hard grammar checks:
    1. Paired Dash Rule: The non-essential clause opened with an em-dash (Jutland—where sphagnum moss...), so it must close with a matching em-dash (decomposition—)—immediately eliminating C (comma) and D (semicolon)!
    2. Inverted Subject-Verb Agreement: Strip the opening participial phrase (Preserved within the anoxic peat bogs of Jutland [—...—]), and flip the inverted verb: [more than two dozen Iron Age wool cloaks...] **lie** preserved within the anoxic peat bogs! Plural subject cloaks requires plural verb lie (eliminating singular lies in B).

subSections.title: D. Math Practice Questions (MATH-D4-Q1 to MATH-D4-Q16) — Strategic Triage, Step-by-Step & Desmos Explanations
subSections.titleHtml: D. Math Practice Questions (MATH-D4-Q1 to MATH-D4-Q16) — Strategic Triage, Step-by-Step & Desmos Explanations
subSections.html:
MATH-D4-Q1 → Correct Answer (SPR): 12

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Manual Discriminant (18 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: For 3x2−12x+k=0 (a=3,b=−12,c=k), exactly one real solution occurs when D=b2−4ac=0:
    (−12)2−4(3)(k)=0⟹144−12k=0⟹12k=144⟹k=12
  • Desmos Check: Graph y = 3x^2 - 12x + k with slider k = 12 → vertex sits right on the x-axis at (2, 0)!
  • Trap Alert: Writing −122=−144 without parentheses around (−12)2.

MATH-D4-Q2 → Correct Answer: C (x^(17/6))

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Manual Exponent Laws (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Convert both radicals using nxm​=xm/n (Power over Root):
    x21​x2⋅x34​​=x2+34​−21​=x612​+68​−63​=x617​
  • Desmos Check (x=64): Type (64^2 * 64^(4/3)) / sqrt(64) → 131072. Test 64^(17/6) → 131072 ✓!
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (11/6) flips 3x4​ upside down as x3/4 or subtracts instead of adding; Trap D (7/2 = 21/6) adds +21​ instead of subtracting −21​ for the denominator!

MATH-D4-Q3 → Correct Answer: B (N(t) = 450(2)^(2t))

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Concrete Time-Point Plug-In (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Watch the unit switch from hours (every 12 hours) to days (t days, where 1 day=24 hours)!
    • At t=0 days: N(0)=450.
    • At t=1 day (24 hours=two 12-hour doublings!): 45012 hr​90024 hr​1,800.
    • Test t=1 in the choices:
      • A: 450(2)1/12≈477 ✗
      • B: 450(2)2(1)=450×4=1,800 ✓!
      • C: 450(2)12 (huge!) ✗
      • D: 900(2)2=3,600 (wrong initial value N(0)=900!) ✗

MATH-D4-Q4 → Correct Answer (SPR): 45

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Inside-Out Evaluation (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Inner function first: g(3)=3(3)−4=9−4=5.
    2. Outer function second: f(g(3))=f(5)=2(5)2−5=2(25)−5=50−5=45.
  • Trap Alert: Computing g(f(3)) backwards (f(3)=13⟹g(13)=35 — wrong order!) or squaring (2×5)2=100 instead of 2(52)=50.

MATH-D4-Q5 → Correct Answer (SPR): 2

  • 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Tie (25 seconds either way!)
  • Algebraic Discriminant Solution:
    1. Set y=y and collect all terms on one side:
      x2−6x+14=2x−c⟹x2−8x+(14+c)=0
    2. For exactly one real solution, set D=b2−4ac=0:
      (−8)2−4(1)(14+c)=0⟹64−56−4c=0⟹8−4c=0⟹c=2
  • Desmos Slider Method: Graph y = x^2 - 6x + 14 and y = 2x - c with slider c. At c = 2, the line y = 2x - 2 touches the parabola at a single tangent point (4, 6)!

MATH-D4-Q6 → Correct Answer: B (6)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Vieta's Sum-of-Squares Identity (30 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: For 2x2−10x+c=0:
    1. Sum of roots: r+s=−2−10​=5.
    2. Product of roots: rs=2c​.
    3. Substitute into r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs:
      19=(5)2−2(2c​)⟹19=25−c⟹c=6
    4. Quick discriminant sanity check: D=(−10)2−4(2)(6)=100−48=52>0 ✓ (real roots confirmed!).
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (12) forgets to divide c by a=2 in rs=c/a (solving 25−2c=19⟹c=3, Choice A, or doubling 6→12)!

MATH-D4-Q7 → Correct Answer: A (10%)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Rewrite Base Exponent (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Isolate t in the exponent using (am)n=amn:
    V(t)=800(1.21)2t​=800((1.21)21​)t=800(1.21​)t=800(1.10)t
    Since 1.10=1+0.10, the value increases by 10% each year!
  • Concrete Check: V(0)=800; V(1)=800(1.21)0.5=880. Percent increase in 1 year =800880−800​=80080​=10% ✓!
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (21%) is the 2-year growth rate; Trap B (10.5%) divides 21%÷2 linearly instead of taking the square root 1.21​=1.10!

MATH-D4-Q8 → Correct Answer (SPR): 5

  • 5-Second Triage: [D] Desmos Intersection (12 seconds!)
  • Desmos Fastest Path: Type y = x^2 - 3x - 4 on Line 1 and x + y = 11 on Line 2 → click the two intersections at (-3, 14) and (5, 6). Since x1​>0, enter 5!
  • Manual Algebra: Substitute y=11−x: 11−x=x2−3x−4⟹x2−2x−15=0⟹(x−5)(x+3)=0⟹x1​=5.
  • Trap Alert: Entering 6 (the y-coordinate at (5,6) instead of x1​!).

MATH-D4-Q9 → Correct Answer (SPR): 9/41

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Complementary Angle Theorem (5 seconds!)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: In right △ABC with ∠C=90∘, acute angles A and B satisfy A+B=90∘, so cosB=sinA=9/41 (4 characters—type 9/41 directly into the SPR box rather than rounding a long decimal!).

MATH-D4-Q10 → Correct Answer (SPR): 6

  • 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Tie (20 seconds)
  • Completing the Square:
    (x2−8x+16)+(y2+6y+9)=11+16+9=36⟹(x−4)2+(y+3)2=62⟹r=6
  • Desmos 10-Second Visual Check: Type x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y - 11 = 0. Click topmost point (4, 3) and bottommost point (4, -9): vertical diameter =3−(−9)=12⟹ radius =12÷2=6!
  • Trap Alert: Entering 36 (r2 instead of r!).

MATH-D4-Q11 → Correct Answer: B (15)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Scaled Pythagorean Triple (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: In right △PQR (∠Q=90∘):
    tanP=adjacent (PQ)opposite (QR)​=125​
    Let QR=5k and PQ=12k. By the 5-12-13 right triangle ratio, hypotenuse PR=13k=39⟹k=3. Therefore, QR=5(3)=15!
  • Trap Alert: Trap C (36) solves for adjacent leg PQ=12(3)=36 instead of opposite leg QR; Trap D (37.5) sets 39QR​=125​ (confusing tanP with sinP!).

MATH-D4-Q12 → Correct Answer: C (60\pi)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Sector Area Formula (20 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution: Use Asector​=21​r2θ (or fraction 2πθ​⋅πr2):
    Asector​=21​(12)2(65π​)=72×65π​=12×5π=60π
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (10\pi) computes arc length rθ=12(65π​)=10π; Trap D (120\pi) forgets the 21​ in 21​r2θ!

MATH-D4-Q13 → Correct Answer: D (126\pi)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Scale Factor Power Rule (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Volume ratio gives linear scale factor s:
      VA​VB​​=s3=27⟹s=327​=3
    2. Every surface area (including lateral area!) scales by s2:
      AreaA​AreaB​​=s2=32=9⟹AreaB​=9×14π=126π
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (42\pi) multiplies by s=3 instead of s2=9; multiplying 27×14π=378π confuses volume scaling with area scaling!

MATH-D4-Q14 → Correct Answer: A ((x - 1)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 32)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M / D] Midpoint + Plug-In (25 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Center (h,k)= midpoint of diameter A(−3,7) and B(5,−1):
      (h,k)=(2−3+5​, 27+(−1)​)=(1,3)
      (Eliminates C and D immediately!)
    2. Plug endpoint B(5,−1) into (x−1)2+(y−3)2=r2:
      r2=(5−1)2+(−1−3)2=42+(−4)2=16+16=32⟹Choice A!
  • Trap Alert: Trap B (128) uses full diameter squared d2=82+(−8)2=128 instead of radius squared r2=32!

MATH-D4-Q15 → Correct Answer: C (19)

  • 5-Second Triage: [D] Desmos Regression ~ (15 seconds!)
  • Desmos 15-Second Regression Method:
    • Line 1: x_1 = [1, 2, 4, 5] (avoid x=3!)
    • Line 2: (4x_1^2 - 9x_1 + 7)/(x_1 - 3) ~ 4x_1 + a + b/(x_1 - 3)
    • Desmos displays a = 3 and b = 16 with R² = 1 ⟹a+b=3+16=19!
  • Manual Algebraic Identity Method: Multiply both sides by (x−3):
    4x2−9x+7=(4x+a)(x−3)+b=4x2+(a−12)x+(−3a+b)
    • Match x coefficient: a−12=−9⟹a=3.
    • Match constant (or plug x=3 into 4x2−9x+7): b=4(9)−9(3)+7=16.
    • Sum: a+b=3+16=19.

MATH-D4-Q16 → Correct Answer: B (10)

  • 5-Second Triage: [M] Reference Formula + Pythagorean Triple (30 seconds)
  • Step-by-Step Solution:
    1. Diameter Trap Check: Diameter =12 cm⟹ radius r=6 cm!
    2. Find vertical height h from cone volume V=31​πr2h:
      96π=31​π(6)2h=12πh⟹h=1296​=8 cm
    3. Slant height ℓ is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by radius r=6 and vertical height h=8 (6-8-10 Pythagorean triple!):
      ℓ=r2+h2​=62+82​=100​=10 cm
  • Trap Alert: Trap A (8) stops at vertical height h=8 instead of slant height ℓ; Trap D (2\sqrt{37}) uses diameter 12 as the radius (h=2⟹122+22​=148​=237​)!

errorLab.beforeKeyHtml:
Part A: Morning Days 1–3 Cumulative Audit Check (09:00–09:20 — 5 Minutes)

Verify you solved both cumulative check items cleanly without notes:

  1. Day 3 Radical + Target Check: Solve 6x+16​=x and state the value of 2x−1. → x2−6x−16=(x−8)(x+2)=0; reject extraneous x=−2; valid x=8⟹2(8)−1=15!
  2. Day 3 Lookalike + Structure Check: Does "Recent glacial core chemistry underscores Dr. Lin's monsoon hypothesis" mean the data weaken or strongly emphasize her hypothesis? → Strongly emphasize (+)!

Part B: Classify Five Day 4 Hard-Tier Student Mistakes (EL-D4-CASE-1 to EL-D4-CASE-5)

Assign (1) Primary Error Code (E1–E10), (2) Vocabulary/Language Label (V1–V7, if R&W), and (3) a 1-sentence Prevention Rule:
errorLab.caseKeyHtml:
• EL-D4-CASE-1: E1 / E2 + V1 / V4 (Familiarity Bias on Unknown Choices) — Prevention Rule: Never pick a known word that fails your context prediction; if all 3 known choices are logically false, select the remaining unknown word confidently.
  • EL-D4-CASE-2: E1 / E4 + V4 (Superficial Cue Association on Transitions) — Prevention Rule: Only choose Fittingly, when Idea 2 poetically echoes a name/meaning; here Coriolis physics caused the equatorial storm-free zone (Accordingly,).
  • EL-D4-CASE-3: E4 (Missed Audience Constraint in Rhetorical Synthesis) — Prevention Rule: Box every constraint in "The student wants to..." FIRST—"unfamiliar with [Term T]" mandates an explicit definition of Term T!
  • EL-D4-CASE-4: E1 (Concept gap — linear division instead of root extraction on exponential base) — Prevention Rule: Use exponent laws (1.21)t/2=(1.21​)t=(1.10)t (and verify V(1)/V(0) in Desmos!).
  • EL-D4-CASE-5: E9 (Wrong strategy — skipped 15-sec Desmos Regression) + E8 (Timing problem — violated 90-sec Bailout, causing downstream rushing error E4 on Q16) — Prevention Rule: Use Desmos ~ regression on rational constant identities in 15 seconds, and NEVER exceed 90 seconds on one problem before banking remaining items!
errorLab.afterKeyHtml:
Part C: Personal Day 4 Error-Log & Pacing Readiness Check (10 Minutes)

Log all today's misses in SAT-Error-Log-and-Daily-Reflections.md and write down your Top 5 Personal Trap Rules at the top of a clean sheet of scratch paper—you will read that exact 5-line cue card at 09:00 tomorrow before Day 5's full timed 27-Q R&W and 22-Q Math module simulations!

cases.answerHtml: E1 / E4 + V4 (Superficial Cue Association on Transitions) — Prevention Rule: Only choose Fittingly, when Idea 2 poetically echoes a name/meaning; here Coriolis physics caused the equatorial storm-free zone (Accordingly,).

cases.promptHtml: Reading all 4 bullets slowly first, Hanna liked Choice A ("...programmed IBM 7030 Stretch computers to refine the geoid, laying the computational foundation for modern GPS accuracy") because every fact matched the bullets, overlooking "unfamiliar with the term geoid" in the question stem.

mastery.introHtml: Complete all 10 synthesis questions below closed-notes in 9 minutes:

masteryItems.promptHtml: Fill both blanks: "The tariff was ______ introduced to protect infant domestic workshops, yet ______ port merchants quickly bypassed it through duty-free transshipment warehouses." (Use ostensibly and pragmatic.)
masteryItems.answerHtml: First blank = ostensibly; Second blank = pragmatic.

masteryItems.promptHtml: In plain English, what does "High elevation does not preclude amphibian breeding" mean?
masteryItems.answerHtml: High elevation does NOT rule out / does NOT prevent amphibians from breeding (amphibians CAN still breed at high elevation).

masteryItems.promptHtml: What does arrest mean in "Rapid pasteurization arrests lactic-acid fermentation in bottled cider"?
masteryItems.answerHtml: Stops / halts fermentation.

masteryItems.promptHtml: Fill the transition: "Sea cucumbers lack rigid calcareous shells; ______ they stiffen or soften dermal collagen fibers within seconds when threatened."
masteryItems.answerHtml: instead, (or rather, — states what sea cucumbers do in place of having rigid shells).

masteryItems.promptHtml: If a synthesis goal specifies "to an audience already familiar with the Harlem Renaissance," do you need to include a background definition of what the Harlem Renaissance was?
masteryItems.answerHtml: No! For a familiar audience, skip background definitions and focus directly on the specific new comparison/claim requested.

masteryItems.promptHtml: For what value of c does 2x2+8x+c=0 have exactly one real solution?
masteryItems.answerHtml: D=82−4(2)(c)=64−8c=0⟹c=8.

masteryItems.promptHtml: Write 5x3​⋅5x7​ as a power of x (x>0).
masteryItems.answerHtml: x3/5⋅x7/5=x10/5=x2.

masteryItems.promptHtml: A fungal colony triples every 8 hours. Starting from 100 spores, write the model S(d) for the spore count after d days (1 day=24 hours).
masteryItems.answerHtml: 24÷8=3 triplings per day ⟹S(d)=100(3)3d.

masteryItems.promptHtml: In right △XYZ with ∠Z=90∘, if cosX=1715​, what is sinY?
masteryItems.answerHtml: Since X+Y=90∘, sinY=cosX=1715​.

masteryItems.promptHtml: Cone B is similar to Cone A, and Cone B's radius is 5 times Cone A's radius. Cone B's volume is how many times Cone A's volume?
masteryItems.answerHtml: Volume scales by s3=53=125 times.

mastery.keyHtml:
1. First blank = ostensibly; Second blank = pragmatic.
  2. High elevation does NOT rule out / does NOT prevent amphibians from breeding (amphibians CAN still breed at high elevation).
  3. Stops / halts fermentation.
  4. instead, (or rather, — states what sea cucumbers do in place of having rigid shells).
  5. No! For a familiar audience, skip background definitions and focus directly on the specific new comparison/claim requested.
  6. D=82−4(2)(c)=64−8c=0⟹c=8.
  7. x3/5⋅x7/5=x10/5=x2.
  8. 24÷8=3 triplings per day ⟹S(d)=100(3)3d.
  9. Since X+Y=90∘, sinY=cosX=1715​.
  10. Volume scales by s3=53=125 times.
mastery.matrixTitle: Day 4 Quantitative Advancement & Revisit Decision Matrix
mastery.matrixHtml:
Component Target Threshold to Advance Cleanly to Day 5 Mandatory Action If Below Threshold
Days 1–3 Mixed Vocab Quiz (SR-D4-Q1..15) >= 12 / 15 (80%+) Add every missed word to Day 5's "48-Second Timed Vocab Sprint" deck tonight.
Day 4 Vocab Recall (Exercise 4C-5) >= 8 / 10 (80%+) Re-drill albeit, circumvent, preclude, equivocal, ostensibly, and ameliorate aloud using 3-Layer examples.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: Digital SAT Adaptive Reality & the Split-Order 32-Minute R&W Pacing Plan
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 5.1: Digital SAT Adaptive Reality & the Split-Order 32-Minute R&W Pacing Plan
lessons.html:
A. How Digital SAT Adaptation Actually Works (Zero Myths)

  1. Stage-Adaptive, NEVER Question-by-Question: Within Module 1, the questions are fixed in advance—missing Q4 does not change Q5. Adaptation happens once at the boundary between Module 1 and Module 2 based on your overall Module 1 performance.
  2. Why Module 1 Easy/Medium Precision Is Sacred: Module 1 mixes Easy, Medium, and Hard items. Scoring cleanly across Easy and Medium items routes you into Harder Module 2, unlocking the 650–800 scaled score range. Careless rushing errors in Module 1 that drop you into Easier Module 2 cap your maximum possible score below ~600–630 even if you get every Module 2 item right!
  3. Psychological Reframe for Harder Module 2: When Module 2 feels noticeably denser in vocabulary and multi-step logic, celebrate for 2 seconds—that proves you earned Upper-Tier Routing! You do not need 27/27 on Harder Module 2 to break 680–700+; banking 22–24/27 cleanly by flagging the 2–3 most abstract time-sinks puts you squarely in elite territory.

B. The Official 27-Question R&W Module Map & Split-Order Checkpoints

Every Digital SAT Reading & Writing module follows the exact same 4-block domain order:

Question Numbers SAT Domain & Skills Cognitive Demand for International Students Target Pace
Q1–Q5 Words in Context Short texts; high vocabulary precision ~45–50 sec/Q (4 min)
Q6–Q14 Structure, Purpose, Cross-Text, Central Ideas, Evidence & Inferences Slowest, heaviest English prose & tables! ~90–100 sec/Q (14–15 min)
Q15–Q21 (sometimes starts at Q14 or Q16) Standard English Conventions (Boundaries & Form, Structure, Sense) Mechanical rule scan — fastest points on exam! ~35–40 sec/Q (4.5 min)
Q22–Q27 Transitions & Rhetorical Synthesis Formulaic logic & Goal-First reading — ultra-fast! ~40–45 sec/Q (4.5 min)

Your Split-Order Execution Script (32:00 Countdown Clock):

  1. At 32:00 (Start): Click the question navigator at the bottom of Bluebook and jump directly to Q15 (or whichever item first asks "conforms to the conventions of Standard English").
  2. Pass 1 (Q15 → Q27): Sweep straight through Grammar, Transitions, and Rhetorical Synthesis.
    • Clock Checkpoint #1 (at Q27): Timer must show >= 22:00 remaining! (You just banked nearly half the module in <=10 minutes while your eyes were fresh!)
  3. Pass 2 (Jump to Q1 → Q10): Solve Words in Context, Structure/Purpose, Cross-Text, and Central Ideas.
    • Clock Checkpoint #2 (at Q10): Timer must show >= 11:00 remaining!
  4. Pass 3 (Q11 → Q14 + Flagged Items): Spend a calm 2 minutes per question on heavy Command of Evidence and Inferences, enforcing the 75-second bailout on any single monster item so 02:00 remains to verify flagged items!

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 5.1 (Check answers in Section 8)

  • CC-D5-RW1: Why does starting at Q15 (Standard English Conventions) protect an international student's score better than solving Q1 through Q27 strictly in numerical order?
  • CC-D5-RW2: When you finish Q27 at the end of Pass 1 and prepare to jump back to Q1, at least how many minutes should remain on the 32:00 countdown clock?
  • CC-D5-RW3: If Harder Module 2 Q12 is a brutal quantitative genetics passage and you are still torn between Choice B and Choice D at 01:15 elapsed, what exact three clicks do you execute immediately?

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: Anti-Freeze Protocol Under Countdown Pressure & the 35-Second Grammar Speed Scan
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 5.2: Anti-Freeze Protocol Under Countdown Pressure & the 35-Second Grammar Speed Scan
lessons.html:
A. Breaking the "Countdown Translation Freeze"

Under a live clock, stress tempts non-native speakers to revert to old habits—silently translating every unknown adjective into their first language or re-reading Line 1 three times without absorbing anything. Use the 10-Second Anchor Reset:

  1. Never stop at an unknown descriptive adjective/noun ("saprophytic basidiomycetes" → read "Mushroom X" and keep moving!).
  2. Read Sentence 1's Subject + Verb (background), jump to the Final Pivot (however, yet, suggesting that), and lock the Author's Claim in 6 plain English words before touching A–D.

B. The 35-Second Grammar Speed Scan (Q15–Q21)

Never read a Standard English Conventions paragraph for plot or science facts! Glance only at how Choices A–D differ first:

  • Choices differ in . / ; / , / — / : → Run Left/Right Independent Clause Test (IC ; IC, IC : explanation, , FANBOYS, paired — ... —, NEVER IC , IC!).
  • Choices differ in verb endings (lies / lie / lying / having lain) → Cross out prepositional phrases, check Finite Verb Requirement, then match Singular vs. Plural Subject + paragraph Tense.
  • Sentence opens with [Participial Phrase], _____ → Place the true logical doer immediately after the comma!

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 5.2

  • CC-D5-RW4: Choices A–D on Q17 are: A) currents, they · B) currents; they · C) currents, and they · D) currents. They. Without even reading the passage, why can you suspect B, C, and D are triple grammatical equivalents (IC ; IC, IC , and IC, IC . IC)—and what would that imply if the first clause is ACTUALLY a dependent clause (Although warm currents...)?
  • CC-D5-RW5: Spot the 5-second cue in Choices A) analyzing · B) having analyzed · C) analyzed · D) to analyze: Which choice is the ONLY finite main verb capable of completing a sentence lacking a main verb?

checks.promptHtml: Choices A–D on Q17 are: A) currents, they · B) currents; they · C) currents, and they · D) currents. They. Without even reading the passage, why can you suspect B, C, and D are triple grammatical equivalents (IC ; IC, IC , and IC, IC . IC)—and what would that imply if the first clause is ACTUALLY a dependent clause (Although warm currents...)?
checks.answerHtml: Because B (; they), C (, and they), and D (. They) all join two independent clauses, they are grammatically equivalent—eliminating all three at once and confirming that Clause 1 is a dependent clause (Although warm currents..., they... → Choice A)!

checks.promptHtml: Spot the 5-second cue in Choices A) analyzing · B) having analyzed · C) analyzed · D) to analyze: Which choice is the ONLY finite main verb capable of completing a sentence lacking a main verb?
checks.answerHtml: Choice C (analyzed) — -ing (analyzing, having analyzed) and to + verb (to analyze) are non-finite verbals that can NEVER serve as the main finite verb of a clause!

subSections.title: B. Day 5 Core Academic Vocabulary: High-Pressure Nuance, Scope & Rhetoric (Words #41–#48)
subSections.titleHtml: B. Day 5 Core Academic Vocabulary: High-Pressure Nuance, Scope & Rhetoric (Words #41–#48)
subSections.html:
Per Part 1's Day 5 design, we encode 8 high-value words today (#41–#48) so cognitive energy stays sharp for both full-length timed modules. Review model entries #41–#48 in Vocabulary-Notebook-and-Spaced-Review.md.

41. ephemeral (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Lasting for only a very short time; fleeting and short-lived.
  • Science & Literature Contexts: Desert rain pools (ephemeral ponds), spring wildflowers, viral social trends, human youth in poetry.
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: fleeting, transient, short-lived, momentary · Ant: enduring, perennial, permanent, perpetual.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Desert fairy shrimp complete their entire life cycle within days inside ephemeral playas that evaporate into cracked salt flats before summer arrives."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Because the ponds dry up completely within days or weeks, they are short-lived (ephemeral).
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Confusing ephemeral ("short-lived") with ethereal ("delicate/heavenly") or perennial ("lasting year after year" — its exact opposite in botany!).
  • Short Application Activity: Contrast: Oak forests are enduring, whereas desert flash-flood puddles are ______. (ephemeral).

42. catalyst (noun) / catalyze (verb)

  • Simple English Definition: Something that sparks, triggers, or dramatically speeds up an important change or reaction.
  • Cross-Domain Reach: Originated in chemistry (a substance speeding a reaction without being consumed), used constantly on SAT History/Social Science ("acted as a catalyst for constitutional reform").
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: spark, stimulus, impetus, spur · Ant: deterrent, impediment, brake.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "The 1755 Lisbon earthquake served as an intellectual catalyst, prompting Enlightenment thinkers across Europe to launch systematic seismic cataloging."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: The disaster triggered and accelerated scientific seismology across Europe.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Confusing catalyst ("spark for change" — often positive or neutral!) with cataclysm / catastrophe ("violent disaster")!
  • Short Application Activity: Convert to verb form: "Cheaper lithium refining ______ rapid electric ferry adoption in Norway." (catalyzed).

43. repudiate (verb)

  • Simple English Definition: To firmly reject, disown, or refuse to accept a doctrine, authority, or past belief.
  • CRITICAL SAT PRECISION (repudiate vs. refute):
    • Refute (Day 3 #25): Prove false with hard empirical evidence/logic.
    • Repudiate: Formally reject / renounce / refuse to endorse (a treaty, a tradition, an artistic school—doesn't have to be an experimental proof!).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: renounce, disavow, reject, disown · Ant: embrace, endorse, ratify, uphold.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "In her 1924 manifesto, the choreographer repudiated rigid classical ballet turnouts in favor of grounded barefoot movement."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: You cannot "prove ballet experimentally false"—she formally rejected and broke away from classical ballet rules (repudiated them).
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Thinking repudiate means "repeat" or "reputation"! Focus on firm rejection.
  • Short Application Activity: Choose refuted or repudiated: "The newly elected parliament ______ the colonial trade monopoly signed by the former monarch." (repudiated — formally rejected a legal treaty!).

44. salient (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Most noticeable, prominent, striking, or important.
  • Related Word Family: salience (n.).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: prominent, conspicuous, striking, key, foremost · Ant: inconspicuous, peripheral, minor, obscure.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Although the two owl species share nearly identical plumage, field ornithologists separate them instantly by one salient acoustic difference: a three-note descending whistle."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Amid identical feathers, the three-note whistle stands out as the most noticeable, unmistakable (salient) feature.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: #1 Science Lookalike Trap: Confusing salient ("most noticeable/important") with saline ("salty," as in saline marsh or saline solution)!
  • Short Application Activity: Pick salient or saline: "Summarizing the report's most ______ policy recommendation, hydrologists warned against pumping ______ groundwater onto citrus roots." (salient / saline).

45. correlate (verb: KOR-uh-layt / noun) / correlation (noun)

  • Simple English Definition: To have a mutual statistical connection in which two things change together (without necessarily proving one causes the other!).
  • Cross-Section SAT Bridge (R&W + Math): Both R&W Inferences and Math Evaluating Statistical Claims test correlation ≠ causation!
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: covary, correspond, parallel, associate · Ant: vary independently, be uncorrelated.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Tree-ring widths across Patagonia correlate closely with Southern Hemisphere summer wind strength, enabling paleoclimatologists to reconstruct past wind belts."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Ring widths and summer wind strength move together in a consistent statistical pattern (correlate).
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Reading "X correlates with Y" as "X causes Y." Keep them strictly distinct!
  • Short Application Activity: If ice-cream sales correlate positively with sunburn clinic visits, does eating ice cream cause sunburns? (No—hot sunny weather causes both!)

46. discern (verb) / discernible (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: To perceive, detect, or distinguish something subtle through careful observation or thought.
  • Common SAT Phrasing: "scarcely discernible" (= barely noticeable), "discern a pattern amidst noise."
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: detect, perceive, distinguish, make out · Ant: overlook, miss, conflate.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Under ordinary room lighting the palimpsest looked blank, but multispectral imaging allowed conservators to discern faint Greek geometric diagrams scraped off the parchment centuries earlier."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Special imaging allowed scholars to detect and make out (discern) faint hidden diagrams invisible to the naked eye.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Confusing discern with concern ("worry"). Think: dis- (apart) + cern (sift/separate) = spot subtle differences clearly!
  • Short Application Activity: What does "produced no discernible change in river pH" mean? (Produced zero detectable / noticeable change in pH.)

47. stringent (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Strict, precise, and rigorously enforced (used for rules, safety standards, or experimental controls).
  • Related Word Family: stringently (adv.), stringency (n.).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: rigorous, strict, exacting, tight · Ant: lax, lenient, loose, permissive.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Because even trace airborne dust ruins EUV lithography wafers, chip foundries enforce stringent gowning and air-lock protocols."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Foundries enforce extremely strict, unbending (stringent) cleanliness rules.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Guessing stringent means "made of string" or "stingy with money." Anchor stringent = strict rules/controls.
  • Short Application Activity: Pair opposites: Loose, careless emissions rules are lax; tight, strictly enforced emissions rules are ______. (stringent).

48. augment (verb)

  • Simple English Definition: To make something larger, stronger, or more effective by adding to it; to supplement.
  • Related Word Family: augmentation (n.), augmented (adj. — augmented reality = real view + added digital layer!).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: supplement, expand, boost, enlarge, amplify · Ant: diminish, curtail, deplete, shrink.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "During dry Andean winters when glacial meltwater drops, Lima's water utility augments reservoir supplies by diverting treated highland lagoon storage."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: When stream flows drop, the utility adds to / supplements (augments) its water supply from highland lagoons.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: #1 Reading Speed Misread: Misreading augment (aug-ment) as argument (ar-gu-ment) when skimming fast! Slow your eyes for 0.5 seconds: no r after a ⟹ augment = add to / increase!
  • Short Application Activity: Connect augmented reality to remember augment forever: what does augmented reality do to your camera view? (Adds extra digital information onto reality!)

Section 4A: Timed Contextual Recall Across Days 1–4 (SR-D5-Q1 to SR-D5-Q14)

  • SR-D5-Q7: tenuous · SR-D5-Q8: ameliorate · SR-D5-Q9: engender · SR-D5-Q10: reciprocity · SR-D5-Q11: underscore · SR-D5-Q12: pragmatic · SR-D5-Q13: reconcile · SR-D5-Q14: scrutinize.

Exercise 4C-1: 48-Second Speed Words in Context (VOC-D5-Q1 to VOC-D5-Q5)

  • VOC-D5-Q1 → B (ephemeral): Unlike perennial [multi-decade] cushions contrasts with germinating, flowering in 10 days, and withering rapidly = short-lived (ephemeral).
  • VOC-D5-Q2 → A (augment): Sundews trap insects to supplement / add to (augment) scarce bog nitrogen.
  • VOC-D5-Q3 → C (discern): Human eyes struggle to detect / perceive (discern) millisecond wingbeat differences without 5,000-fps cameras.
  • VOC-D5-Q4 → B (repudiated): Publicly broke with and renounced (repudiated) austere glass-box functionalism in favor of historical ornament.
  • VOC-D5-Q5 → C (stringent): Strict, rigorous (stringent) double-blind clinical standards exposed weak strains.

Exercise 4C-2: Lookalike & Nuance Discrimination (VOC-D5-Q6 to VOC-D5-Q9)

  • VOC-D5-Q6: salient (most prominent/important archival discovery—contrasted right beside saline = salty lagoons!).
  • VOC-D5-Q7: augment (verb meaning supplement/expand grid capacity; argument is a noun).
  • VOC-D5-Q8: catalyst (spark accelerating trade communication, not a disaster/catastrophe).
  • VOC-D5-Q9: correlate (move together statistically during wildfire smoke spikes).

Exercise 4C-3: Sentence Completion (VOC-D5-Q10 to VOC-D5-Q14)

  • VOC-D5-Q10: discern · VOC-D5-Q11: catalyst · VOC-D5-Q12: stringent · VOC-D5-Q13: ephemeral · VOC-D5-Q14: augment (or augmented).

Exercise 4C-4: Cumulative Sort (VOC-D5-Q15 to VOC-D5-Q16)

  • VOC-D5-Q15: Support / Increase (+): bolster, augment, corroborate · Reject / Block (-): preclude, repudiate · Bypass obstacle: circumvent.
  • VOC-D5-Q16: 1 = ephemeral (fleeting/short-lived), 2 = ubiquitous (present everywhere), 3 = conventional (traditional/established).

Exercise 4C-5: Closed-Notes Rapid Retrieval Quiz (VOC-D5-Q17 to VOC-D5-Q24)

  • VOC-D5-Q17 (ephemeral): Very short-lived; fleeting and temporary.
  • VOC-D5-Q18 (catalyst): Spark or factor accelerating rapid change.
  • VOC-D5-Q19 (repudiate): Firmly reject, disown, or renounce.
  • VOC-D5-Q20 (salient): Most noticeable, prominent, or important.
  • VOC-D5-Q21 (correlate): Vary together in a statistical relationship.
  • VOC-D5-Q22 (discern): Detect, perceive, or distinguish subtle details.
  • VOC-D5-Q23 (stringent): Strict, rigorous, and tightly enforced.
  • VOC-D5-Q24 (augment): Add to, supplement, or make larger.
