STRICT SIMULATION RULES (32:00 Countdown Clock — ZERO PAUSING!):

  1. Set a timer for 32 minutes (32:00). Put your phone out of reach.
  2. Execute Split-Order Pacing:
    • Pass 1 (Start at RW-D5-Q15 → RW-D5-Q27): Complete all 13 Grammar, Transition, and Rhetorical Synthesis items first! Checkpoint at Q27: >= 22:00 left on clock.
    • Pass 2 (Jump to RW-D5-Q1 → RW-D5-Q10): Complete Words in Context, Structure/Purpose, Cross-Text, and Central Ideas. Checkpoint at Q10: >= 11:00 left on clock.
    • Pass 3 (RW-D5-Q11 → RW-D5-Q14 + Flagged Review): Complete Evidence & Inferences + review any marked items.
  3. Every item below is an original SAT-style practice question matching official Digital SAT module proportions (5 WIC · 3 Structure/Cross-Text · 6 Info & Ideas · 7 SEC · 6 Transitions/Synthesis = 27 Qs). Do not view Section 8 until the 32:00 horn sounds!

questions.stemHtml:
To determine whether graylag geese learn migration routes genetically or culturally, ethologists raised incubator-hatched goslings alongside ultralight aircraft pilots; the young birds readily followed the planes southward in autumn and ______ that exact human-guided flyway on their own the following spring.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: repudiated
retraced
precluded
mitigated

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Goslings followed ultralight planes south in autumn and flew back along that exact same path (retraced it) on their own in spring. A (repudiated) = rejected; C (precluded) = ruled out; D (mitigated) = softened harm.

questions.stemHtml:
Because unbaked clay cuneiform tablets from third-millennium-BCE Mesopotamia survived predominantly when palace archives burned down—firing soft mud into brick-hard ceramic—archaeologists note that surviving administrative texts ______ crisis years far more heavily than peaceful decades.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: represent
ameliorate
circumvent
arrest

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Because palace fires baked soft mud tablets hard, surviving tablets depict / reflect (represent) crisis years disproportionately compared with quiet decades. B (ameliorate), C (circumvent), and D (arrest) make no sense with "crisis years far more heavily."

questions.stemHtml:
Whereas macro-scale satellite sensors easily map multi-kilometer kelp canopy losses along California headlands, autonomous underwater cameras are needed to ______ juvenile bull-kelp recruitment occurring beneath turbid nearshore surf.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: engender
catalyze
discern
concede

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Whereas contrasts satellites easily mapping surface canopies against underwater cameras needed to detect / make out (discern) tiny young kelp beneath murky surf. A (engender) & B (catalyze) mean cause/spark (cameras observe kelp, they don't grow it!); D (concede) = admit.

questions.stemHtml:
Critics of nineteenth-century laissez-faire grain policy argued that municipal export bans during harvest shortfalls were ______ emergency stabilizers rather than ideological attacks on commerce, lifted as soon as winter wheat barges arrived.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: equivocal
ubiquitous
perennial
pragmatic

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Rather than ideological attacks on commerce + lifted as soon as winter wheat barges arrived defines a practical, temporary real-world fix (pragmatic stabilizers). A (equivocal) = ambiguous; B (ubiquitous) = everywhere; C (perennial) = permanent/year-after-year (contradicts lifting them promptly!).

questions.stemHtml:
Although bioluminescent flash patterns among Caribbean ostracod crustaceans appear chaotic to casual night divers, high-speed stereoscopic video reveals ______ species-specific pulse intervals: males of Photeros annecohenae space upward light dots exactly 1.4 seconds apart, and females ignore signals deviating by even two-tenths of a second.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: stringent
ephemeral
tenuous
ostensible

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: After the colon, males space flashes exactly 1.4 s apart and females reject deviations of even 0.2 s—an exacting, ultra-strict (stringent) timing rule! B (ephemeral) = short-lived (distractor playing on flashes of light, missing the colon's strict timing precision!); C (tenuous) = weak; D (ostensible) = pretended.

questions.stemHtml:
In traditional Japanese satoyama woodland management, villagers coppiced chestnut and oak groves on fifteen-year rotations for charcoal fuel—periodically opening sunlit forest floors where spring violets and endangered Luehdorfia butterflies thrived. As rural households switched to imported kerosene and propane after 1960, uncut canopies closed into dark shade, prompting modern conservationists to organize volunteer coppicing brigades solely to restore lost understory biodiversity.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.raw: To argue that rural Japanese households should abandon propane heating and return to domestic charcoal production
choices.html: To argue that rural Japanese households should abandon propane heating and return to domestic charcoal production

choices.raw: To trace how the decline of a traditional fuel-harvesting practice unintentionally altered woodland habitats and inspired targeted ecological restoration
choices.html: To trace how the decline of a traditional fuel-harvesting practice unintentionally altered woodland habitats and inspired targeted ecological restoration

choices.raw: To compare the caloric heat output of coppiced oak charcoal with that of imported kerosene
choices.html: To compare the caloric heat output of coppiced oak charcoal with that of imported kerosene

choices.raw: To explain why *Luehdorfia* butterflies feed exclusively on chestnut leaves rather than spring violets
choices.html: To explain why Luehdorfia butterflies feed exclusively on chestnut leaves rather than spring violets

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Sentence 1 explains how rotational charcoal coppicing kept satoyama floors sunny for violets and butterflies; Sentence 2 traces how post-1960 fossil-fuel adoption closed canopies and prompted conservationists to revive coppicing for biodiversity (Choice B). A invents policy advocacy against propane; C & D invent unmentioned comparisons/diets.

questions.stemHtml:
Astronomers measuring how fast stars orbit the outer rims of spiral galaxies expected orbital speeds to drop off sharply beyond the visible disk of stars, just as Neptune orbits the Sun far more slowly than Mercury does. Radio-telescope Doppler maps of neutral hydrogen gas extending far beyond visible galactic edges showed instead that outer gas clouds orbit at nearly flat, constant velocities. To account for the extra gravitational pull keeping those fast outer clouds from flying into intergalactic space, astrophysicists proposed that galaxies sit inside vast invisible halos of dark matter.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.raw: It explains why Mercury orbits the Sun more rapidly than outer gas giants do.
choices.html: It explains why Mercury orbits the Sun more rapidly than outer gas giants do.

choices.raw: It describes an observational anomaly that contradicted classical orbital expectations and motivated the theoretical proposal in the final sentence.
choices.html: It describes an observational anomaly that contradicted classical orbital expectations and motivated the theoretical proposal in the final sentence.

choices.raw: It proves that radio telescopes measure visible starlight more accurately than optical telescopes do.
choices.html: It proves that radio telescopes measure visible starlight more accurately than optical telescopes do.

choices.raw: It questions whether neutral hydrogen gas exists outside spiral galaxies.
choices.html: It questions whether neutral hydrogen gas exists outside spiral galaxies.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Sentence 1 = classical expectation (outer speeds should drop). Sentence 2 (Underlined) = radio-telescope surprise (instead, outer gas orbits at flat constant speeds = observational anomaly). Sentence 3 = dark-matter halo theory proposed to explain Sentence 2! A, C, and D distort surrounding sentences.

questions.stemHtml:
Text 1
Behavioral economists point to automatic retirement-savings enrollment—where new employees contribute four percent of wages by default unless they actively opt out—as a triumph of low-cost policy design, raising participation rates from under fifty percent to above eighty-five percent within six months of implementation.

Text 2
Multi-year payroll audits by Choukhmane and colleagues confirm that automatic enrollment dramatically boosts initial retirement-plan participation. Over three to five years, however, automatically enrolled workers take out significantly larger emergency loans against their retirement balances and accept stagnant four-percent default contribution rates rather than raising contributions to eight or ten percent as active opt-in savers typically do—leaving five-year net wealth accumulation far closer to pre-policy levels than six-month snapshots suggest.

Based on the texts, how would Choukhmane and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the assessment in Text 1?

choices.raw: By disputing Text 1's claim that automatic enrollment raises six-month participation rates above eighty-five percent
choices.html: By disputing Text 1's claim that automatic enrollment raises six-month participation rates above eighty-five percent

choices.raw: By conceding automatic enrollment's strong short-term participation effect while cautioning that extrapolating long-term wealth gains from six-month enrollment rates overlooks offsetting borrower and default-anchoring behaviors
choices.html: By conceding automatic enrollment's strong short-term participation effect while cautioning that extrapolating long-term wealth gains from six-month enrollment rates overlooks offsetting borrower and default-anchoring behaviors

choices.raw: By arguing that employers should forbid workers from opting out of retirement plans under any circumstances
choices.html: By arguing that employers should forbid workers from opting out of retirement plans under any circumstances

choices.raw: By recommending that default contribution rates be lowered from four percent to two percent
choices.html: By recommending that default contribution rates be lowered from four percent to two percent

questions.explanationHtml:
• Why Correct: Look at Text 2's exact 2-step structure (±):
    1. Concession: "confirm that automatic enrollment dramatically boosts initial retirement-plan participation" (rules out A!).
    2. Caveat against extrapolation: Over 3–5 years, higher loans + sticky 4% defaults offset those gains (Choice B, weaving Day 2 concede + Day 3 extrapolate!). C and D invent policy extremes.

questions.stemHtml:
The following text is an original passage in the style of nineteenth-century realist fiction.
Cousin Henrik spoke of his new botanical glasshouse in Uppsala as though he had pardoned winter itself: behind double-glazed Belgian panes and cast-iron steam pipes, Javanese orchids unfurled waxy white throats while sleet rattled harmlessly overhead. Yet whenever old Greta carried coal scuttles down to stoke the cellar boiler at midnight and four again before dawn, Henrik never glanced toward the soot-streaked iron grate beneath the ferns—preferring to believe tropical July lingered in Sweden out of sheer admiration for his Latin plant labels.

Which choice best describes how the narrator characterizes Cousin Henrik?

choices.raw: As a tireless horticultural laborer who personally tends boiler fires throughout freezing nights
choices.html: As a tireless horticultural laborer who personally tends boiler fires throughout freezing nights

choices.raw: As a self-congratulatory collector who takes pride in defying winter while ignoring the grueling domestic labor that sustains his conservatory
choices.html: As a self-congratulatory collector who takes pride in defying winter while ignoring the grueling domestic labor that sustains his conservatory

choices.raw: As an accomplished university botanist whose Latin taxonomy revolutionized Swedish orchid breeding
choices.html: As an accomplished university botanist whose Latin taxonomy revolutionized Swedish orchid breeding

choices.raw: As a thrifty householder anxious to reduce the coal consumption of his Belgian glasshouse
choices.html: As a thrifty householder anxious to reduce the coal consumption of his Belgian glasshouse

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Henrik boasts "as though he had pardoned winter itself" while "never glanc[ing] toward the soot-streaked iron grate" as old Greta hauls coal at midnight and 4 a.m. (Choice B). A swaps Greta's labor onto Henrik; C & D misread ironic details.

questions.stemHtml:
Unlike terrestrial mammals that sleep with both brain hemispheres offline simultaneously, northern fur seals (Callorhinus ursinus) adapt sleep architecture to their surrounding habitat. While resting ashore on subarctic rookery beaches, fur seals spend over seventy percent of sleep time in bilateral slow-wave and REM sleep; when foraging at sea for weeks at a time, however, they switch almost exclusively to unihemispheric slow-wave sleep—keeping one eye open and the contralateral brain hemisphere awake to monitor sharks and keep nostrils above swells.

According to the text, what distinguishes northern fur seals' sleep at sea from their sleep on land?

choices.raw: Fur seals sleep for a greater total number of hours per day at sea than they do on rookery beaches.
choices.html: Fur seals sleep for a greater total number of hours per day at sea than they do on rookery beaches.

choices.raw: At sea, fur seals keep one brain hemisphere alert during slow-wave sleep rather than sleeping with both hemispheres offline as they predominantly do ashore.
choices.html: At sea, fur seals keep one brain hemisphere alert during slow-wave sleep rather than sleeping with both hemispheres offline as they predominantly do ashore.

choices.raw: Fur seals experience rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep only while floating in open ocean swells.
choices.html: Fur seals experience rapid-eye-movement (REM) sleep only while floating in open ocean swells.

choices.raw: Young fur seals must learn unihemispheric sleep by observing adult seals on subarctic beaches.
choices.html: Young fur seals must learn unihemispheric sleep by observing adult seals on subarctic beaches.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Directly matches ashore = >70% bilateral sleep vs. at sea = almost exclusively unihemispheric slow-wave sleep—keeping one eye open and the contralateral brain hemisphere awake (Choice B). A invents total sleep hours; C reverses REM location; D invents social learning.

questions.stemHtml:
Environmental historians studying medieval Venice contend that the Republic's centuries-long survival as a deep-water maritime port depended on massive engineering interventions that deliberately sacrificed brackish marsh habitats along the lagoon's mainland perimeter in order to prevent river silt from turning Venice's defensive water moat into walkable mudflats.

Which historical finding, if true, would most directly substantiate the historians' claim?

choices.raw: Fifteenth-century Venetian senate decrees ordered thousands of laborers to dig colossal diversion canals rerouting the Brenta and Piave rivers completely outside the lagoon, despite fishermen's petitions that cutting off freshwater inflows destroyed reed-marsh eel fisheries.
choices.html: Fifteenth-century Venetian senate decrees ordered thousands of laborers to dig colossal diversion canals rerouting the Brenta and Piave rivers completely outside the lagoon, despite fishermen's petitions that cutting off freshwater inflows destroyed reed-marsh eel fisheries.

choices.raw: Venetian glassmaking furnaces were relocated to the island of Murano in 1291 to reduce timber fire hazards inside dense residential parishes.
choices.html: Venetian glassmaking furnaces were relocated to the island of Murano in 1291 to reduce timber fire hazards inside dense residential parishes.

choices.raw: Merchant galleys departing Venice's Arsenal carried standardized interchangeable rudders and hemp rigging across Mediterranean trade routes.
choices.html: Merchant galleys departing Venice's Arsenal carried standardized interchangeable rudders and hemp rigging across Mediterranean trade routes.

choices.raw: Tide gauges installed along St. Mark's Basin in the late nineteenth century recorded rising winter storm surges during Adriatic sirocco winds.
choices.html: Tide gauges installed along St. Mark's Basin in the late nineteenth century recorded rising winter storm surges during Adriatic sirocco winds.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Satisfies both halves of the historians' claim: (Half 1) massive engineering preventing river silt from filling Venice's lagoon moat (rerouting the Brenta and Piave rivers outside the lagoon), AND (Half 2) deliberately sacrificing perimeter brackish marsh habitats (ignoring fishermen's petitions about destroying reed-marsh eel fisheries). B, C, and D miss river silt and marshes completely.

questions.stemHtml:
Pollination Visits and Seed-Set Success in Alpine Bellflowers (Campanula thyrsoides) by Elevation

Site Elevation (m) Bumblebee Visits per Flower/Hour Hoverfly Visits per Flower/Hour Open-Pollinated Seed Set (%) Bee-Excluded Mesh Seed Set (%) (Hoverflies Only)
1,400 6.2 1.8 88 19
1,900 3.4 4.1 85 31
2,400 0.9 7.6 79 72

Alpine pollination ecologists note that because cold winds above 2,200 m sharply curtail thermoregulating bumblebee flights while cold-tolerant hoverflies become abundant, raw flower-visitation counts often mislead researchers into assuming hoverflies are inefficient pollen transferrers everywhere; at the highest alpine meadows, hoverflies actually account for the vast majority of successful Campanula thyrsoides reproduction.

Which comparison of data from the table best supports the ecologists' claim?

choices.raw: Hoverfly visits per flower per hour rose steadily with elevation, from $1.8$ at $1{,}400\text{ m}$ to $4.1$ at $1{,}900\text{ m}$ and $7.6$ at $2{,}400\text{ m}$.
choices.html: Hoverfly visits per flower per hour rose steadily with elevation, from 1.8 at 1,400 m to 4.1 at 1,900 m and 7.6 at 2,400 m.

choices.raw: Open-pollinated seed set declined slightly from $88\%$ at $1{,}400\text{ m}$ to $79\%$ at $2{,}400\text{ m}$ as bumblebee visits dropped from $6.2$ to $0.9$ per hour.
choices.html: Open-pollinated seed set declined slightly from 88% at 1,400 m to 79% at 2,400 m as bumblebee visits dropped from 6.2 to 0.9 per hour.

choices.raw: Whereas excluding bumblebees at $1{,}400\text{ m}$ caused seed set to plunge from $88\%$ to $19\%$, excluding bumblebees at $2{,}400\text{ m}$ left seed set at $72\%$—nearly matching the $79\%$ open-pollinated rate where both insects had access.
choices.html: Whereas excluding bumblebees at 1,400 m caused seed set to plunge from 88% to 19%, excluding bumblebees at 2,400 m left seed set at 72%—nearly matching the 79% open-pollinated rate where both insects had access.

choices.raw: At $1{,}900\text{ m}$, hoverflies visited flowers more frequently than bumblebees did ($4.1$ vs. $3.4$ visits/hour), yet bee-excluded seed set was $31\%$.
choices.html: At 1,900 m, hoverflies visited flowers more frequently than bumblebees did (4.1 vs. 3.4 visits/hour), yet bee-excluded seed set was 31%.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: To prove hoverflies drive the vast majority of high-alpine seed set despite looking weak lower down, compare Open-Pollinated (Bees + Hoverflies) vs. Bee-Excluded Mesh (Hoverflies Only): at 1,400 m hoverflies alone manage only 19% (vs. 88% open), whereas at 2,400 m hoverflies alone achieve 72% seed set—nearly matching the 79% open-pollinated total! A cites visit counts without proving seed-set success; B omits hoverfly mesh data; D cites mid-elevation 1,900 m only.

questions.stemHtml:
When urban streetlamp networks transitioned from amber high-pressure sodium bulbs to broad-spectrum white LEDs rich in short-wavelength blue light (450–480 nm), nocturnal moth pollination of evening primroses along lit roadsides dropped by sixty-two percent. Field trials replacing white LEDs with shielded phosphor-converted amber LEDs—which emit virtually zero wavelengths below 500 nm while preserving human pedestrian obstacle visibility—restored evening primrose moth visitation to within five percent of unlit meadow baselines, suggesting that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: high-pressure sodium bulbs emit higher proportions of short-wavelength blue light than white LEDs do.
choices.html: high-pressure sodium bulbs emit higher proportions of short-wavelength blue light than white LEDs do.

choices.raw: ecological disruption of nocturnal moth pollination by streetlighting depends strongly on spectral wavelength composition and can be largely mitigated without sacrificing pedestrian safety.
choices.html: ecological disruption of nocturnal moth pollination by streetlighting depends strongly on spectral wavelength composition and can be largely mitigated without sacrificing pedestrian safety.

choices.raw: evening primroses growing in unlit meadows produce sweeter nectar than evening primroses growing beside amber LED streetlights.
choices.html: evening primroses growing in unlit meadows produce sweeter nectar than evening primroses growing beside amber LED streetlights.

choices.raw: shielding white LEDs without altering their blue-light spectrum would restore moth pollination more effectively than phosphor-converted amber LEDs do.
choices.html: shielding white LEDs without altering their blue-light spectrum would restore moth pollination more effectively than phosphor-converted amber LEDs do.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Combine premises: Blue-rich white LEDs cut moth pollination by 62%; switching to blue-free amber LEDs (spectral wavelength change) restored pollination to within 5% of unlit baselines (mitigated disruption) while preserving pedestrian obstacle visibility (Choice B). A reverses sodium vs. LED spectra; C invents nectar sweetness; D contradicts the wavelength finding.

questions.stemHtml:
Radiocarbon dating of bone collagen from Viking Age graves in coastal Norway occasionally yields calendar dates 300 to 400 years older than silver coins minted in known years buried inside the exact same coffins. Geochemists explain this "marine reservoir offset" by noting that deep North Atlantic ocean water contains dissolved ancient carbon depleted in 14C; organisms feeding heavily on marine fish incorporate this older carbon signature into their tissues, whereas terrestrial grazers reflect contemporary atmospheric 14C. Consequently, if an archaeologist calculates an unadjusted bone-collagen radiocarbon date for a coastal individual without measuring dietary nitrogen isotopes to estimate fish intake, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: the silver coins in the coffin will appear several centuries older than the skeleton's true burial date.
choices.html: the silver coins in the coffin will appear several centuries older than the skeleton's true burial date.

choices.raw: the skeleton's estimated burial date is likely to be skewed artificially early in proportion to how heavily that person relied on marine seafood.
choices.html: the skeleton's estimated burial date is likely to be skewed artificially early in proportion to how heavily that person relied on marine seafood.

choices.raw: terrestrial animal bones recovered from the same village will exhibit an identical $300$-to-$400$-year marine reservoir offset.
choices.html: terrestrial animal bones recovered from the same village will exhibit an identical 300-to-400-year marine reservoir offset.

choices.raw: radiocarbon dating cannot accurately date any organic material older than the Viking Age.
choices.html: radiocarbon dating cannot accurately date any organic material older than the Viking Age.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Combine premises: Deep ocean carbon lacks 14C (looks 300–400 years older) → fish-eating Vikings absorb that older marine carbon into bone collagen → unadjusted bone radiocarbon dates make the skeleton look centuries older (buried earlier) than its true burial year, in proportion to marine fish intake (Choice B). A flips skeleton vs. dated coins; C contradicts "terrestrial grazers reflect contemporary atmospheric 14C"; D is an extreme overclaim.

questions.stemHtml:
Constructed in 1902 to carry spring snowmelt across Granada's dry foothills, the brick ______ still irrigates terraced almond orchards more than a century later.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: aqueduct,
aqueduct;
aqueduct
aqueduct—

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Never place a single comma, semicolon, or dash between grammatical subject (the brick aqueduct) and its main verb (still irrigates)!

questions.stemHtml:
Before British crystallographer Dorothy Crowfoot Hodgkin determined the three-dimensional atomic structure of penicillin using X-ray diffraction in 1945, organic chemists ______ for over a decade over whether the molecule contained a strained beta-lactam ring.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: debate
will debate
are debating
had debated

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: "Before Hodgkin determined [past, 1945]" + duration "for over a decade" requires past perfect (had debated) for the earlier ongoing chemical debate.

questions.stemHtml:
Iceland's Hellisheiði geothermal plant does not vent captured carbon dioxide into the ______ engineers dissolve the gas in water and pump it deep into porous basalt bedrock, where calcium and magnesium ions mineralize it into solid carbonate stone within two years.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: atmosphere, instead,
atmosphere; instead,
atmosphere, instead
atmosphere instead

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Left of blank = complete IC (Iceland's Hellisheiði geothermal plant does not vent captured carbon dioxide into the atmosphere). Right of blank = complete IC (engineers dissolve the gas...). Conjunctive adverb instead between two ICs requires IC ; instead, IC (Choice B; A & C are comma splices; D is a fused run-on).

questions.stemHtml:
The intricate geometric tilework adorning Uzbekistan's fifteenth-century Registan madrasas—along with the cobalt-glazed calligraphic friezes crowning their pishtaq ______ master ceramicists' command of kiln temperature gradients.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: portals—exemplifies
portals—exemplify
portals, exemplifies
portals; exemplify

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: (1) Paired Dashes: Must close madrasas—along with... portals— with a matching dash (eliminating C and D). (2) Subject-Verb Agreement: Cross out everything inside the dashes! Singular subject The intricate geometric tilework requires singular verb exemplifies (eliminating plural exemplify in B).

questions.stemHtml:
In 2014, Iranian mathematician ______ became the first woman to win the Fields Medal for her foundational discoveries concerning the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: Maryam Mirzakhani,
Maryam Mirzakhani
, Maryam Mirzakhani,
Maryam Mirzakhani—

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Essential title phrase Iranian mathematician (no the or an) restricts Maryam Mirzakhani → zero commas or dashes!

questions.skill: Form, Structure, and Sense (Possessive Plural + Comparison)
questions.stemHtml:
Acoustic measurements in high-altitude cloud forests indicate that male Andean cock-of-the-rock ______ carry nearly twice as far through dense fern foliage as those of closely related lowland cotingas.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: birds' courtship calls
bird's courtship calls
birds courtship calls'
birds' courtship call

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Check two clues: (1) plural verb carry and plural comparison those of require plural head noun calls (eliminating singular call in D, and C absurdly makes calls' possessive!); (2) general species statement male Andean cock-of-the-rock birds (matching plural lowland cotingas) uses plural possessive birds', though note male ... birds' vs. singular a bird's (no article a before male, confirming plural birds'!).

questions.skill: Form, Structure, and Sense (Finite Verb vs. Participle)
questions.stemHtml:
Whereas ordinary silicate glass shatters when plunged from boiling water into ice, borosilicate laboratory glassware—formulated by German chemist Otto Schott in 1893 by incorporating boron trioxide into molten ______ minimal thermal expansion and withstands abrupt temperature shocks intact.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: silica, exhibiting
silica—exhibiting
silica—exhibits
silica; exhibits

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: (1) Paired Dashes: Close glassware—formulated... silica— with a dash (eliminating A and D). (2) Finite Parallel Verb: Main clause subject borosilicate laboratory glassware needs finite singular verb exhibits (...exhibits minimal thermal expansion and withstands abrupt temperature shocks), whereas exhibiting (B) leaves a fragment before and withstands!

questions.stemHtml:
Sea otters lack the thick insulating blubber layer that keeps seals and whales warm in chilly North Pacific waters. ______ they rely on the densest fur in the mammalian kingdom—up to one million hairs per square inch—to trap a dry blanket of air next to their skin.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.html: Instead,
For instance,
Likewise,
Furthermore,

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: [Sea otters lack blubber.] Instead, [they rely on ultra-dense fur.] Direct replacement after a negative statement.

questions.stemHtml:
In 1928, microbiologist Alexander Fleming noticed that a stray blue-green Penicillium mold colony had dissolved nearby Staphylococcus bacteria on an unwashed culture plate. Isolating pure, shelf-stable penicillin in clinical quantities proved dauntingly difficult for a lone researcher; ______ twelve years passed before Howard Florey, Ernst Chain, and Norman Heatley scaled deep-tank fermentation for wartime hospitals.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.html: by contrast,
consequently,
nevertheless,
similarly,

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Because purifying penicillin was dauntingly difficult for one researcher (cause), twelve years elapsed before industrial scaling (effect → consequently,).

questions.stemHtml:
Many Renaissance civic humanists praised vernacular Tuscan Italian in theory as a vibrant literary medium equal to classical Cicero. ______ when composing diplomatic treaties or university astronomy lectures intended for pan-European readerships, those very same scholars wrote almost exclusively in Neo-Latin.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.html: Accordingly,
Specifically,
In other words,
Even so,

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Humanists praised Italian in theory; despite that (Even so,), those very same scholars wrote major works almost exclusively in Neo-Latin in practice!

questions.stemHtml:
In desert locusts (Schistocerca gregaria), solitary green grasshoppers actively avoid one another across sparse scrubland. Touch-receptor stimulation on their hind femurs when drought crowds insects onto shrinking vegetation patches triggers a rapid serotonin surge; ______ within four hours, formerly shy individuals turn bright yellow-and-black and band together into migratory swarms numbering billions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.html: regardless,
conversely,
as a result,
granted,

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Hind-leg crowding triggers a rapid serotonin surge (physiological cause); as a result, within four hours locusts change color and form swarms (behavioral outcome).

questions.stemHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Stepwells (vavs or baoris) are multi-story subterranean stone water-storage structures built across arid western India between the seventh and nineteenth centuries.
  • Descending flights of carved sandstone steps allowed residents to reach fluctuating groundwater tables during dry nine-month gaps between summer monsoons.
  • Recessed colonnaded pavilions inside the shaft stayed up to 6∘C cooler than surface air, serving as shaded community gathering spaces for women drawing water and passing caravan traders.
  • Rani ki Vav in Patan, Gujarat (11th century), features over 500 principal sandstone sculptures and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

The student wants to highlight how western Indian stepwells served both hydraulic and social functions in arid climates. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.raw: Built in eleventh-century Gujarat, Rani ki Vav contains over $500$ sandstone sculptures and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in $2014$.
choices.html: Built in eleventh-century Gujarat, Rani ki Vav contains over 500 sandstone sculptures and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

choices.raw: Across arid western India, subterranean stone stepwells provided year-round access to receding groundwater between monsoons while offering cool, shaded pavilions where residents and travelers gathered.
choices.html: Across arid western India, subterranean stone stepwells provided year-round access to receding groundwater between monsoons while offering cool, shaded pavilions where residents and travelers gathered.

choices.raw: Descending flights of carved sandstone steps enabled communities in western India to reach fluctuating groundwater tables during dry nine-month intervals.
choices.html: Descending flights of carved sandstone steps enabled communities in western India to reach fluctuating groundwater tables during dry nine-month intervals.

choices.raw: Colonnaded pavilions inside Indian stepwells remained up to $6^\circ\text{C}$ cooler than surface temperatures between the seventh and nineteenth centuries.
choices.html: Colonnaded pavilions inside Indian stepwells remained up to 6∘C cooler than surface temperatures between the seventh and nineteenth centuries.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Goal requires both hydraulic AND social functions: Choice B pairs hydraulic (year-round access to receding groundwater between monsoons) with social (cool, shaded pavilions where residents and travelers gathered). A = UNESCO/sculptures only; C = hydraulic only; D = temperature only.

questions.stemHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Icebergs calving off Greenland glaciers contain microscopic iron-oxide nanoparticles (ferrihydrite) ground from bedrock beneath the ice sheet.
  • Dissolvable iron is a scarce limiting micronutrient for marine phytoplankton across much of the high-latitude North Atlantic.
  • Oceanographer Raisa Bhatia analyzed water samples along 14 Greenland fjord-to-shelf iceberg melt plumes (2021).
  • Samples collected inside melt plumes contained 8.4 nanomoles of bioavailable iron per liter and 3.2 milligrams of chlorophyll-a per cubic meter.
  • Control ocean samples collected 15 km away from melt plumes contained 0.9 nanomoles of bioavailable iron per liter and 0.6 milligrams of chlorophyll-a per cubic meter.

The student wants to use quantitative data from Bhatia's 2021 study to illustrate how Greenland iceberg meltwater stimulates phytoplankton abundance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.raw: Carrying bedrock *ferrihydrite* nanoparticles into iron-limited North Atlantic waters, Greenland iceberg melt plumes in Bhatia's $2021$ study had dramatically higher bioavailable iron ($8.4$ vs. $0.9\text{ nmol/L}$) and phytoplankton chlorophyll-$a$ ($3.2$ vs. $0.6\text{ mg/m}^3$) than distant control waters.
choices.html: Carrying bedrock ferrihydrite nanoparticles into iron-limited North Atlantic waters, Greenland iceberg melt plumes in Bhatia's 2021 study had dramatically higher bioavailable iron (8.4 vs. 0.9 nmol/L) and phytoplankton chlorophyll-a (3.2 vs. 0.6 mg/m3) than distant control waters.

choices.raw: In $2021$, oceanographer Raisa Bhatia measured bioavailable iron and chlorophyll-$a$ across $14$ Greenland iceberg melt plumes and control ocean sites located $15\text{ km}$ away.
choices.html: In 2021, oceanographer Raisa Bhatia measured bioavailable iron and chlorophyll-a across 14 Greenland iceberg melt plumes and control ocean sites located 15 km away.

choices.raw: Because dissolvable iron limits marine phytoplankton in the North Atlantic, Greenland icebergs containing *ferrihydrite* nanoparticles enrich fjord waters when they melt.
choices.html: Because dissolvable iron limits marine phytoplankton in the North Atlantic, Greenland icebergs containing ferrihydrite nanoparticles enrich fjord waters when they melt.

choices.raw: Inside Greenland iceberg melt plumes, bioavailable iron averaged $8.4$ nanomoles per liter, compared with $0.9$ nanomoles per liter in control samples $15\text{ km}$ away.
choices.html: Inside Greenland iceberg melt plumes, bioavailable iron averaged 8.4 nanomoles per liter, compared with 0.9 nanomoles per liter in control samples 15 km away.

questions.explanationHtml: • Why Correct: Goal requires quantitative data from Bhatia's 2021 study showing how iceberg meltwater stimulates phytoplankton abundance. Choice A includes both required quantitative comparisons: higher bioavailable iron (8.4 vs. 0.9 nmol/L) AND resulting higher phytoplankton chlorophyll-a (3.2 vs. 0.6 mg/m3)! B & C include zero data numbers; D omits phytoplankton chlorophyll-a data completely!

lessons.title: Lesson 5.3: The 35-Minute 22-Question Math Pacing Architecture & SPR Entry Firewall
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 5.3: The 35-Minute 22-Question Math Pacing Architecture & SPR Entry Firewall
lessons.html:
A. Official 22-Question Math Clock Checkpoints (35:00 Countdown)

Unlike R&W, Digital SAT Math progresses roughly in order of increasing difficulty from Q1 (Easy) to Q22 (Hardest). Therefore, work Q1 → Q22 in order on Pass 1, enforcing strict checkpoint splits:

Question Block Difficulty Mix Max Time Budget Countdown Clock Remaining Tactical Priority
Q1–Q10 Easy → Low-Med <= 11 minutes >= 24:00 left 100% Accuracy Shield (10/10 target!)—read boxed target phrases twice; never rush Q1–Q10 to "save" 90 seconds if it costs a careless leak!
Q11–Q17 Medium → Med-Hard <= 12 minutes >= 12:00 left Use 5-Second Desmos vs. Manual Triage (~100 sec/Q max; flag immediately if stalling at 1:30).
Q18–Q22 + Review Hard Gatekeepers 12 minutes 00:00 Scan all 5 Hard items quickly! Solve the 3–4 cleanest ones first (Desmos regression / circle / discriminant), leaving the single gnarliest item for the final 3 minutes.

B. Student-Produced Response (SPR) Formatting Firewall (Zero Unforced Grid-In Losses!)

Bluebook's SPR box accepts up to 5 characters for positive answers (0.375, 14/3, 12600) and up to 6 characters for negative answers (-14/3, -0.25):

  1. Leave Fractions Unreduced or Reduced (14/3 > 4.666): Typing an exact fraction (9/41, 7/2) takes zero rounding effort and eliminates truncation slips—provided it fits in 5 characters!
  2. NEVER Enter Mixed Numbers (4 2/3 Is Read as 42/3 = 14!): Always convert 432​ to improper fraction 14/3 or decimal 4.667 (4.666 also accepted).
  3. Never Type %, $, ,, or pi: If a question asks "what is k where area =kπ?", enter 126, never 126pi!

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 5.3 (Check answers in Section 8)

  • CC-D5-M1: When you click from Q10 to Q11 on a 35-minute SAT Math module, at least how many minutes should still be showing on the countdown timer?
  • CC-D5-M2: Your exact algebraic answer to an SPR problem is 383​. Write two valid ways to enter this in Bluebook, and state the one fatal mistake to avoid.
  • CC-D5-M3: Your exact fraction answer is 12115​ (6 characters!). Why won't 115/12 fit in Bluebook's positive SPR box, and what should you type instead?

outline.text: A. Official 22-Question Math Clock Checkpoints (35:00 Countdown)
B. Student-Produced Response (SPR) Formatting Firewall (Zero Unforced Grid-In Losses!)

checks.promptHtml: When you click from Q10 to Q11 on a 35-minute SAT Math module, at least how many minutes should still be showing on the countdown timer?
checks.answerHtml: >= 24:00 remaining (<=11 minutes spent on Q1–Q10).

checks.promptHtml: Your exact algebraic answer to an SPR problem is 383​. Write two valid ways to enter this in Bluebook, and state the one fatal mistake to avoid.
checks.answerHtml: Valid entries: improper fraction 27/8 OR exact decimal 3.375. Fatal mistake to avoid: typing 3 3/8 (Bluebook strips spaces or rejects it—33/8 is completely wrong!).

checks.promptHtml: Your exact fraction answer is 12115​ (6 characters!). Why won't 115/12 fit in Bluebook's positive SPR box, and what should you type instead?
checks.answerHtml: Positive SPR answers allow at most 5 characters (1-1-5-/-1-2 is 6 characters!). Divide 115/12 = 9.58333... in Desmos and enter 9.583!

lessons.title: Lesson 5.4: Harder Second-Module Math Resilience (Q18–Q22) — Smart Skipping & Parametric Constants
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 5.4: Harder Second-Module Math Resilience (Q18–Q22) — Smart Skipping & Parametric Constants
lessons.html:
When you reach Q18–Q22 of Harder Module 2, College Board intentionally plants 1–2 abstract parameter problems designed to trap perfectionists for 4+ minutes. Beat them with two rules:

  1. The 45-Second "Peek & Re-Order" on Q18–Q22:
    Suppose Q19 is a 7-line 3D inscribed-prism word problem with no diagram, while Q21 is a clean right-triangle circle problem and Q22 is a rational constant identity x2+7x+106x+24​=x+2A​+x+5B​ that Desmos regression solves in 15 seconds. If you freeze on Q19 for 4 minutes, you never even see Q21 and Q22! Flag any Q18–Q22 item whose path isn't clear at 0:45, harvest the faster Q20–Q22 points first, then come back with zero stress.
  2. Thales's Inscribed Diameter Rule (High-Frequency Q20–Q22 Favorite):
    Whenever a triangle is inscribed inside a circle and one side of the triangle is a diameter of the circle, the angle opposite that diameter is guaranteed to be a 90∘ right angle—instantly unlocking Pythagoras and SOH-CAH-TOA!

Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 5.4

  • CC-D5-M4: Points P, Q, and R lie on a circle of radius 5, and segment PR passes through the center of the circle. What is the measure of ∠PQR, and what is the length of hypotenuse PR?
  • CC-D5-M5: In Desmos regression (6x_1 + 24)/(x_1^2 + 7x_1 + 10) ~ A/(x_1 + 2) + B/(x_1 + 5), which two numbers must you avoid putting inside your list x_1 = [...]?

outline.text: Short Comprehension Check — Lesson 5.4

checks.promptHtml: Points P, Q, and R lie on a circle of radius 5, and segment PR passes through the center of the circle. What is the measure of ∠PQR, and what is the length of hypotenuse PR?
checks.answerHtml: By Thales's Theorem, ∠PQR=90∘, and diameter PR=2r=2(5)=10.

checks.promptHtml: In Desmos regression (6x_1 + 24)/(x_1^2 + 7x_1 + 10) ~ A/(x_1 + 2) + B/(x_1 + 5), which two numbers must you avoid putting inside your list x_1 = [...]?
checks.answerHtml: Never include -2 or -5 in x_1 = [...], because dividing by (x+2) or (x+5) at those values produces division-by-zero (undefined), breaking the regression!

mathPractice.introHtml:
STRICT SIMULATION RULES (35:00 Countdown Clock — ZERO PAUSING!):

  1. Open desmos.com/calculator in half your screen. Set a strict countdown timer for 35 minutes (35:00).
  2. Hit Your Checkpoints:
    • After MATH-D5-Q10: >= 24:00 remaining
    • After MATH-D5-Q17: >= 12:00 remaining
    • MATH-D5-Q18–Q22 + Flagged Check: final 12:00
  3. All 22 problems below (16 Multiple Choice + 6 SPR) are original SAT-style practice questions matching official Digital SAT Math module weights (8 Algebra · 7 Advanced Math · 4 Data Analysis · 3 Geometry & Trig). Do not view Section 8 until finished!

questions.stemHtml: If 6x−9=27, what is the value of 2x+5?

choices.html: 6
12
17
23

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (12 sec): 6x−9=27⟹6x=36⟹x=6. Boxed target: 2(6)+5=17. (Trap A 6 stops at x!)

questions.stemHtml: During quality-control testing at an electronics plant, 14 out of a random sample of 350 solar micro-inverters failed voltage calibration. At this rate, how many micro-inverters out of a production batch of 2,500 would be expected to fail voltage calibration?

choices.html: 70
100
140
175

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (15 sec): Failure rate =35014​=0.04. Expected failures =0.04×2,500=100.

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, line k passes through the points (0,4) and (3,19). What is the slope of line k?
questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (10 sec): m=3−019−4​=315​=5.

questions.stemHtml: Which expression is equivalent to (2x+5)(x−4)?

choices.html: 2x2−20
2x2−3x−20
2x2+3x−20
2x2−13x−20

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (15 sec): FOIL: 2x2−8x+5x−20=2x2−3x−20. (Trap C flips sign of −3x; Trap A drops middle term.)

questions.stemHtml: A marine instrument technician charges C(h)=45+32h dollars to calibrate sonar transponders for h hours aboard a research vessel. Which is the best interpretation of the number 45 in this context?

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (15 sec): In C(h)=45+32h, C(0)=45 is the fixed one-time service fee before h hours accumulate (Choice A; 32 is the hourly rate in B; 45 + 32 = 77 is the 1-hour total in D).

questions.stemHtml: The two legs of a right triangle have lengths 9 centimeters and 12 centimeters. What is the perimeter, in centimeters, of this right triangle?

choices.html: 15
21
30
36

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (18 sec): 3-4-5 right triangle scaled by 3: legs 9 and 12⟹ hypotenuse =15. Boxed target = perimeter =9+12+15=36! (Trap A 15 stops at hypotenuse!)

questions.stemHtml:
f(x)=3x+7
For the function f defined above, what is the value of f(4)?
questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (12 sec): f(4)=34+7=81+7=88. (Avoid multiplying 3×4=12!)

questions.stemHtml:
3x−2yx+2y​=16=12​
If (x,y) is the solution to the system of equations above, what is the value of y?

choices.html: 2
2.5
5
7

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (20 sec Manual or 12 sec Desmos):
    • Add equations: 4x=28⟹x=7. Plug into x+2y=12: 7+2y=12⟹2y=5⟹y=2.5!
    • Or graph both lines in Desmos and read the y-coordinate of (7, 2.5)! (Trap D 7 enters x instead of y!)

questions.stemHtml:
Salinity Readings Across 19 Intertidal Rock Pools

Salinity (parts per thousand) Number of Pools
30 4

The frequency table above summarizes salinity measurements for 19 intertidal rock pools along a rocky headland. What is the median salinity, in parts per thousand, of the 19 pools?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (25 sec): Total pools N=4+5+6+4=19. Median is the 219+1​=10th ordered pool!
    • Pools 1–4: 30 ppt
    • Pools 5–9: 32 ppt (cumulative =9 pools)
    • Pools 10–15: 34 ppt ⟹ the 10th pool has salinity 34!

questions.stemHtml: Which inequality represents all values of x that satisfy 5−2(x+3)>9?

choices.html: x<−5
x>−5
x<−4
x>−4

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (20 sec): Distribute −2 across (x+3):
    5−2x−6>9⟹−2x−1>9⟹−2x>10⟹x<−5
    (Flipped > to < when dividing by −2! Test x=−6: 5−2(−3)=11>9 ✓.)

questions.stemHtml:
p(x)=3(x−6)2+14
What is the minimum value of the function p defined above?

choices.html: −6
6
14
42

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (10 sec): Vertex form p(x)=3(x−6)2+14 has vertex (6,14) and a=3>0 (opens up). "Minimum value of the function" ALWAYS means the minimum y-output =14! (Trap B 6 is the x-input where the minimum occurs.)

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, line ℓ is defined by 2x−5y=20. Line n is perpendicular to line ℓ and passes through (0,3). Which equation defines line n?

choices.html: y=−25​x+3
y=−52​x+3
y=52​x+3
y=25​x+3

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (20 sec): Rewrite 2x−5y=20⟹5y=2x−20⟹y=52​x−4 (mℓ​=52​). Perpendicular slope =−25​; with y-intercept (0,3), y=−25​x+3.

questions.stemHtml: Snowmelt runoff increased the volume of water stored in a mountain reservoir by 25% during spring. Summer irrigation withdrawals then decreased that spring water volume by 20%. The resulting late-summer water volume was what percent of the original pre-spring water volume?

choices.html: 95%
100%
105%
120%

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (20 sec): Multiply successive percent multipliers on baseline V:
    Vfinal​=V×(1+0.25)×(1−0.20)=V×1.25×0.80=1.00V=100%
    (Trap C 105% adds +25%−20%=+5% additively—classic SAT percent trap!)

questions.stemHtml:
3x+28​=x
What is the real solution to the given equation?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (15 sec Desmos or 25 sec Manual):
    • Square both sides: 3x+28=x2⟹x2−3x−28=(x−7)(x+4)=0.
    • Check in un-squared 3x+28​=x: x=7⟹49​=7 ✓; x=−4⟹16​=+4=−4 (extraneous—reject!). Answer: 7.

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, a circle with equation (x+3)2+(y−5)2=49 is translated 4 units to the right. What are the coordinates of the center of the translated circle?

choices.html: (−7,5)
(−3,9)
(1,5)
(7,−5)

questions.explanationHtml: • Fastest Path (15 sec): Original circle (x+3)2+(y−5)2=49 has center (−3,5). Shifting 4 units right adds +4 to the x-coordinate of the center: (−3+4,5)=(1,5)! (Trap A (-7, 5) shifts left instead of right.)

questions.stemHtml:
6x−9ykx−6y​=15=8​
In the system of equations above, k is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of k?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (25 sec): For no solution, x- and y-coefficients must be proportional while constants are not:
    k6​=−6−9​=23​⟹3k=12⟹k=4
    (Verify constants: 815​=23​, so parallel distinct lines—no solution ✓!)

questions.stemHtml: A medical cyclotron produces 320 milligrams of a short-lived diagnostic radioisotope whose mass decreases by 50% every 18 minutes. How many milligrams of the radioisotope remain 1.5 hours after production? (1 hour=60 minutes)

choices.html: 10
20
40
106.7

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (25 sec): Convert 1.5 hours=90 minutes! Number of 18-minute half-lives =1890​=5:
    M=320×(0.5)5=32320​=10 mg

questions.stemHtml: An analytical chemistry course has two laboratory sections. Section A has 12 students with a mean titration exam score of 78, and Section B has 18 students with a mean titration exam score of 88. What is the combined mean titration exam score across all 30 students?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (25 sec): Total points ÷ Total students (NEVER average 78 and 88 to get 83 because group sizes 12=18!):
    Combined Mean=12+1812(78)+18(88)​=30936+1,584​=302,520​=84

questions.stemHtml:
4x2−12x+c=0
In the given equation, c is a constant. If the equation has no real solutions, which of the following could be the value of c?

choices.html: −9
0
9
11

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (25 sec): No real solutions ⟺D=b2−4ac<0:
    (−12)2−4(4)(c)<0⟹144−16c<0⟹16c>144⟹c>9
    Only 11 (Choice D) is strictly greater than 9! (At Trap C 9, D=0⟹ one real solution.)

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, the parabola y=f(x) has its vertex at (3,5) and passes through the point (0,23). What is the value of f(5)?

choices.html: 9
13
17
33

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (30 sec Manual or 20 sec Desmos):
    1. Write vertex form using vertex (3,5): f(x)=a(x−3)2+5.
    2. Plug in (0,23): 23=a(0−3)2+5=9a+5⟹9a=18⟹a=2.
    3. Evaluate f(5)=2(5−3)2+5=2(4)+5=13!
    • (Symmetry Shortcut: (0,23) is 3 units from x=3; (5,f(5)) is 2 units from x=3, and Desmos slider a on f(x) = a(x - 3)^2 + 5 hitting (0, 23) reads f(5) = 13 in 15 seconds!)

questions.stemHtml: Triangle DEF is inscribed in a circle of radius 8.5 such that side DF is a diameter of the circle. If cosD=178​, what is the area of triangle DEF?

choices.html: 30
34
60
120

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (35 sec):
    1. Thales's Theorem: Because side DF is a diameter of the circle (r=8.5⟹hypotenuse DF=2(8.5)=17), inscribed angle ∠E=90∘!
    2. Use cosD=hypotenuse DFadjacent DE​=178​: since DF=17, leg DE=8.
    3. By the 8-15-17 Pythagorean triple (172−82​=225​=15), perpendicular leg EF=15.
    4. Triangle area =21​(leg1​)(leg2​)=21​(8)(15)=60! (Trap D 120 forgets 21​!)

questions.stemHtml:
x2+7x+106x+24​=x+2A​+x+5B​
The equation above holds for all real numbers x except −2 and −5, where A and B are constants. What is the value of A⋅B?

choices.html: 6
8
12
24

questions.explanationHtml:
• Fastest Path (15 sec Desmos Regression ~!):
    • Line 1: x_1 = [0, 1, 2, 3] (avoids -2 and -5!)
    • Line 2: (6x_1 + 24)/(x_1^2 + 7x_1 + 10) ~ A/(x_1 + 2) + B/(x_1 + 5)
    • Desmos instantly outputs A = 4 and B = 2 ⟹A⋅B=4×2=8!
  • Manual Cover-Up / Clearing Denominators (30 sec): Multiply by (x+2)(x+5)=x2+7x+10:
    6x+24=A(x+5)+B(x+2)
    • Set x=−2: 12=3A⟹A=4.
    • Set x=−5: −6=−3B⟹B=2.
    • Product A⋅B=4×2=8.

answerVault.introHtml:
Post-Simulation Scoring & Cold Re-Solve Rule:

  1. First mark your raw scores (/27 R&W and /22 Math) without reading the explanations of your missed questions!
  2. Re-attempt every missed question untimed on blank paper first—if you solve it right untimed, tag it E10 (Pacing / Clock Rush); if you miss it again untimed, read the full explanation below and tag its exact skill/vocabulary code!

Reading & Writing Checks (CC-D5-RW1 to CC-D5-RW5)

  • CC-D5-RW1: Starting at Q15 lets you harvest 12–13 mechanical Grammar, Transition, and Synthesis points in ~9 minutes while your focus is fresh, eliminating the #1 score-destroying scenario where an international student gets bogged down on Q9–Q14 dense passages and is forced to guess blindly on Q22–Q27 easy points as time expires!
  • CC-D5-RW2: >= 22:00 remaining on the 32:00 clock (<=10 minutes spent on Q15–Q27).
  • CC-D5-RW3: (1) Click the better-supported choice between B and D (never leave blank!), (2) click "Mark for Review", and (3) click "Next" immediately to protect the rest of the module!
  • CC-D5-RW4: Because B (; they), C (, and they), and D (. They) all join two independent clauses, they are grammatically equivalent—eliminating all three at once and confirming that Clause 1 is a dependent clause (Although warm currents..., they... → Choice A)!
  • CC-D5-RW5: Choice C (analyzed) — -ing (analyzing, having analyzed) and to + verb (to analyze) are non-finite verbals that can NEVER serve as the main finite verb of a clause!

Math Checks (CC-D5-M1 to CC-D5-M5)

  • CC-D5-M1: >= 24:00 remaining (<=11 minutes spent on Q1–Q10).
  • CC-D5-M2: Valid entries: improper fraction 27/8 OR exact decimal 3.375. Fatal mistake to avoid: typing 3 3/8 (Bluebook strips spaces or rejects it—33/8 is completely wrong!).
  • CC-D5-M3: Positive SPR answers allow at most 5 characters (1-1-5-/-1-2 is 6 characters!). Divide 115/12 = 9.58333... in Desmos and enter 9.583!
  • CC-D5-M4: By Thales's Theorem, ∠PQR=90∘, and diameter PR=2r=2(5)=10.
  • CC-D5-M5: Never include -2 or -5 in x_1 = [...], because dividing by (x+2) or (x+5) at those values produces division-by-zero (undefined), breaking the regression!

Section 4A: Timed Contextual Recall Across Days 1–4 (SR-D5-Q1 to SR-D5-Q14)

  • SR-D5-Q1: B (attributed) · SR-D5-Q2: C (preclude) · SR-D5-Q3: A (ostensibly) · SR-D5-Q4: C (proliferated) · SR-D5-Q5: B (arrests) · SR-D5-Q6: B (albeit).
  • SR-D5-Q7: tenuous · SR-D5-Q8: ameliorate · SR-D5-Q9: engender · SR-D5-Q10: reciprocity · SR-D5-Q11: underscore · SR-D5-Q12: pragmatic · SR-D5-Q13: reconcile · SR-D5-Q14: scrutinize.

Exercise 4C-1: 48-Second Speed Words in Context (VOC-D5-Q1 to VOC-D5-Q5)

  • VOC-D5-Q1 → B (ephemeral): Unlike perennial [multi-decade] cushions contrasts with germinating, flowering in 10 days, and withering rapidly = short-lived (ephemeral).
  • VOC-D5-Q2 → A (augment): Sundews trap insects to supplement / add to (augment) scarce bog nitrogen.
  • VOC-D5-Q3 → C (discern): Human eyes struggle to detect / perceive (discern) millisecond wingbeat differences without 5,000-fps cameras.
  • VOC-D5-Q4 → B (repudiated): Publicly broke with and renounced (repudiated) austere glass-box functionalism in favor of historical ornament.
  • VOC-D5-Q5 → C (stringent): Strict, rigorous (stringent) double-blind clinical standards exposed weak strains.

Exercise 4C-2: Lookalike & Nuance Discrimination (VOC-D5-Q6 to VOC-D5-Q9)

  • VOC-D5-Q6: salient (most prominent/important archival discovery—contrasted right beside saline = salty lagoons!).
  • VOC-D5-Q7: augment (verb meaning supplement/expand grid capacity; argument is a noun).
  • VOC-D5-Q8: catalyst (spark accelerating trade communication, not a disaster/catastrophe).
  • VOC-D5-Q9: correlate (move together statistically during wildfire smoke spikes).

Exercise 4C-3: Sentence Completion (VOC-D5-Q10 to VOC-D5-Q14)

  • VOC-D5-Q10: discern · VOC-D5-Q11: catalyst · VOC-D5-Q12: stringent · VOC-D5-Q13: ephemeral · VOC-D5-Q14: augment (or augmented).

Exercise 4C-4: Cumulative Sort (VOC-D5-Q15 to VOC-D5-Q16)

  • VOC-D5-Q15: Support / Increase (+): bolster, augment, corroborate · Reject / Block (-): preclude, repudiate · Bypass obstacle: circumvent.
  • VOC-D5-Q16: 1 = ephemeral (fleeting/short-lived), 2 = ubiquitous (present everywhere), 3 = conventional (traditional/established).

Exercise 4C-5: Closed-Notes Rapid Retrieval Quiz (VOC-D5-Q17 to VOC-D5-Q24)

  • VOC-D5-Q17 (ephemeral): Very short-lived; fleeting and temporary.
  • VOC-D5-Q18 (catalyst): Spark or factor accelerating rapid change.
  • VOC-D5-Q19 (repudiate): Firmly reject, disown, or renounce.
  • VOC-D5-Q20 (salient): Most noticeable, prominent, or important.
  • VOC-D5-Q21 (correlate): Vary together in a statistical relationship.
  • VOC-D5-Q22 (discern): Detect, perceive, or distinguish subtle details.
  • VOC-D5-Q23 (stringent): Strict, rigorous, and tightly enforced.
  • VOC-D5-Q24 (augment): Add to, supplement, or make larger.

RW-D5-Q1 → Correct Answer: B (retraced)

  • Why Correct: Goslings followed ultralight planes south in autumn and flew back along that exact same path (retraced it) on their own in spring. A (repudiated) = rejected; C (precluded) = ruled out; D (mitigated) = softened harm.

RW-D5-Q2 → Correct Answer: A (represent)

  • Why Correct: Because palace fires baked soft mud tablets hard, surviving tablets depict / reflect (represent) crisis years disproportionately compared with quiet decades. B (ameliorate), C (circumvent), and D (arrest) make no sense with "crisis years far more heavily."

RW-D5-Q3 → Correct Answer: C (discern)

  • Why Correct: Whereas contrasts satellites easily mapping surface canopies against underwater cameras needed to detect / make out (discern) tiny young kelp beneath murky surf. A (engender) & B (catalyze) mean cause/spark (cameras observe kelp, they don't grow it!); D (concede) = admit.

RW-D5-Q4 → Correct Answer: D (pragmatic)

  • Why Correct: Rather than ideological attacks on commerce + lifted as soon as winter wheat barges arrived defines a practical, temporary real-world fix (pragmatic stabilizers). A (equivocal) = ambiguous; B (ubiquitous) = everywhere; C (perennial) = permanent/year-after-year (contradicts lifting them promptly!).

RW-D5-Q5 → Correct Answer: A (stringent)

  • Why Correct: After the colon, males space flashes exactly 1.4 s apart and females reject deviations of even 0.2 s—an exacting, ultra-strict (stringent) timing rule! B (ephemeral) = short-lived (distractor playing on flashes of light, missing the colon's strict timing precision!); C (tenuous) = weak; D (ostensible) = pretended.

RW-D5-Q6 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Sentence 1 explains how rotational charcoal coppicing kept satoyama floors sunny for violets and butterflies; Sentence 2 traces how post-1960 fossil-fuel adoption closed canopies and prompted conservationists to revive coppicing for biodiversity (Choice B). A invents policy advocacy against propane; C & D invent unmentioned comparisons/diets.

RW-D5-Q7 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Sentence 1 = classical expectation (outer speeds should drop). Sentence 2 (Underlined) = radio-telescope surprise (instead, outer gas orbits at flat constant speeds = observational anomaly). Sentence 3 = dark-matter halo theory proposed to explain Sentence 2! A, C, and D distort surrounding sentences.

RW-D5-Q8 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Look at Text 2's exact 2-step structure (±):
    1. Concession: "confirm that automatic enrollment dramatically boosts initial retirement-plan participation" (rules out A!).
    2. Caveat against extrapolation: Over 3–5 years, higher loans + sticky 4% defaults offset those gains (Choice B, weaving Day 2 concede + Day 3 extrapolate!). C and D invent policy extremes.

RW-D5-Q9 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Henrik boasts "as though he had pardoned winter itself" while "never glanc[ing] toward the soot-streaked iron grate" as old Greta hauls coal at midnight and 4 a.m. (Choice B). A swaps Greta's labor onto Henrik; C & D misread ironic details.

RW-D5-Q10 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Directly matches ashore = >70% bilateral sleep vs. at sea = almost exclusively unihemispheric slow-wave sleep—keeping one eye open and the contralateral brain hemisphere awake (Choice B). A invents total sleep hours; C reverses REM location; D invents social learning.

RW-D5-Q11 → Correct Answer: A

  • Why Correct: Satisfies both halves of the historians' claim: (Half 1) massive engineering preventing river silt from filling Venice's lagoon moat (rerouting the Brenta and Piave rivers outside the lagoon), AND (Half 2) deliberately sacrificing perimeter brackish marsh habitats (ignoring fishermen's petitions about destroying reed-marsh eel fisheries). B, C, and D miss river silt and marshes completely.

RW-D5-Q12 → Correct Answer: C

  • Why Correct: To prove hoverflies drive the vast majority of high-alpine seed set despite looking weak lower down, compare Open-Pollinated (Bees + Hoverflies) vs. Bee-Excluded Mesh (Hoverflies Only): at 1,400 m hoverflies alone manage only 19% (vs. 88% open), whereas at 2,400 m hoverflies alone achieve 72% seed set—nearly matching the 79% open-pollinated total! A cites visit counts without proving seed-set success; B omits hoverfly mesh data; D cites mid-elevation 1,900 m only.

RW-D5-Q13 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Combine premises: Blue-rich white LEDs cut moth pollination by 62%; switching to blue-free amber LEDs (spectral wavelength change) restored pollination to within 5% of unlit baselines (mitigated disruption) while preserving pedestrian obstacle visibility (Choice B). A reverses sodium vs. LED spectra; C invents nectar sweetness; D contradicts the wavelength finding.

RW-D5-Q14 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Combine premises: Deep ocean carbon lacks 14C (looks 300–400 years older) → fish-eating Vikings absorb that older marine carbon into bone collagen → unadjusted bone radiocarbon dates make the skeleton look centuries older (buried earlier) than its true burial year, in proportion to marine fish intake (Choice B). A flips skeleton vs. dated coins; C contradicts "terrestrial grazers reflect contemporary atmospheric 14C"; D is an extreme overclaim.

RW-D5-Q15 → Correct Answer: C (aqueduct)

  • Why Correct: Never place a single comma, semicolon, or dash between grammatical subject (the brick aqueduct) and its main verb (still irrigates)!

RW-D5-Q16 → Correct Answer: D (had debated)

  • Why Correct: "Before Hodgkin determined [past, 1945]" + duration "for over a decade" requires past perfect (had debated) for the earlier ongoing chemical debate.

RW-D5-Q17 → Correct Answer: B (atmosphere; instead,)

  • Why Correct: Left of blank = complete IC (Iceland's Hellisheiði geothermal plant does not vent captured carbon dioxide into the atmosphere). Right of blank = complete IC (engineers dissolve the gas...). Conjunctive adverb instead between two ICs requires IC ; instead, IC (Choice B; A & C are comma splices; D is a fused run-on).

RW-D5-Q18 → Correct Answer: A (portals—exemplifies)

  • Why Correct: (1) Paired Dashes: Must close madrasas—along with... portals— with a matching dash (eliminating C and D). (2) Subject-Verb Agreement: Cross out everything inside the dashes! Singular subject The intricate geometric tilework requires singular verb exemplifies (eliminating plural exemplify in B).

RW-D5-Q19 → Correct Answer: B (Maryam Mirzakhani)

  • Why Correct: Essential title phrase Iranian mathematician (no the or an) restricts Maryam Mirzakhani → zero commas or dashes!

RW-D5-Q20 → Correct Answer: A (birds' courtship calls)

  • Why Correct: Check two clues: (1) plural verb carry and plural comparison those of require plural head noun calls (eliminating singular call in D, and C absurdly makes calls' possessive!); (2) general species statement male Andean cock-of-the-rock birds (matching plural lowland cotingas) uses plural possessive birds', though note male ... birds' vs. singular a bird's (no article a before male, confirming plural birds'!).

RW-D5-Q21 → Correct Answer: C (silica—exhibits)

  • Why Correct: (1) Paired Dashes: Close glassware—formulated... silica— with a dash (eliminating A and D). (2) Finite Parallel Verb: Main clause subject borosilicate laboratory glassware needs finite singular verb exhibits (...exhibits minimal thermal expansion and withstands abrupt temperature shocks), whereas exhibiting (B) leaves a fragment before and withstands!

RW-D5-Q22 → Correct Answer: A (Instead,)

  • Why Correct: [Sea otters lack blubber.] Instead, [they rely on ultra-dense fur.] Direct replacement after a negative statement.

RW-D5-Q23 → Correct Answer: B (consequently,)

  • Why Correct: Because purifying penicillin was dauntingly difficult for one researcher (cause), twelve years elapsed before industrial scaling (effect → consequently,).

RW-D5-Q24 → Correct Answer: D (Even so,)

  • Why Correct: Humanists praised Italian in theory; despite that (Even so,), those very same scholars wrote major works almost exclusively in Neo-Latin in practice!

RW-D5-Q25 → Correct Answer: C (as a result,)

  • Why Correct: Hind-leg crowding triggers a rapid serotonin surge (physiological cause); as a result, within four hours locusts change color and form swarms (behavioral outcome).

RW-D5-Q26 → Correct Answer: B

  • Why Correct: Goal requires both hydraulic AND social functions: Choice B pairs hydraulic (year-round access to receding groundwater between monsoons) with social (cool, shaded pavilions where residents and travelers gathered). A = UNESCO/sculptures only; C = hydraulic only; D = temperature only.

RW-D5-Q27 → Correct Answer: A

  • Why Correct: Goal requires quantitative data from Bhatia's 2021 study showing how iceberg meltwater stimulates phytoplankton abundance. Choice A includes both required quantitative comparisons: higher bioavailable iron (8.4 vs. 0.9 nmol/L) AND resulting higher phytoplankton chlorophyll-a (3.2 vs. 0.6 mg/m3)! B & C include zero data numbers; D omits phytoplankton chlorophyll-a data completely!

MATH-D5-Q1 → Correct Answer: C (17)

  • Fastest Path (12 sec): 6x−9=27⟹6x=36⟹x=6. Boxed target: 2(6)+5=17. (Trap A 6 stops at x!)

MATH-D5-Q2 → Correct Answer: B (100)

  • Fastest Path (15 sec): Failure rate =35014​=0.04. Expected failures =0.04×2,500=100.

MATH-D5-Q3 → Correct Answer (SPR): 5

  • Fastest Path (10 sec): m=3−019−4​=315​=5.

MATH-D5-Q4 → Correct Answer: B (2x^2 - 3x - 20)

  • Fastest Path (15 sec): FOIL: 2x2−8x+5x−20=2x2−3x−20. (Trap C flips sign of −3x; Trap A drops middle term.)

MATH-D5-Q5 → Correct Answer: A

  • Fastest Path (15 sec): In C(h)=45+32h, C(0)=45 is the fixed one-time service fee before h hours accumulate (Choice A; 32 is the hourly rate in B; 45 + 32 = 77 is the 1-hour total in D).

MATH-D5-Q6 → Correct Answer: D (36)

  • Fastest Path (18 sec): 3-4-5 right triangle scaled by 3: legs 9 and 12⟹ hypotenuse =15. Boxed target = perimeter =9+12+15=36! (Trap A 15 stops at hypotenuse!)

MATH-D5-Q7 → Correct Answer (SPR): 88

  • Fastest Path (12 sec): f(4)=34+7=81+7=88. (Avoid multiplying 3×4=12!)

MATH-D5-Q8 → Correct Answer: B (2.5)

  • Fastest Path (20 sec Manual or 12 sec Desmos):
    • Add equations: 4x=28⟹x=7. Plug into x+2y=12: 7+2y=12⟹2y=5⟹y=2.5!
    • Or graph both lines in Desmos and read the y-coordinate of (7, 2.5)! (Trap D 7 enters x instead of y!)

MATH-D5-Q9 → Correct Answer (SPR): 34

  • Fastest Path (25 sec): Total pools N=4+5+6+4=19. Median is the 219+1​=10th ordered pool!
    • Pools 1–4: 30 ppt
    • Pools 5–9: 32 ppt (cumulative =9 pools)
    • Pools 10–15: 34 ppt ⟹ the 10th pool has salinity 34!

MATH-D5-Q10 → Correct Answer: A (x < -5)

  • Fastest Path (20 sec): Distribute −2 across (x+3):
    5−2x−6>9⟹−2x−1>9⟹−2x>10⟹x<−5
    (Flipped > to < when dividing by −2! Test x=−6: 5−2(−3)=11>9 ✓.)

MATH-D5-Q11 → Correct Answer: C (14)

  • Fastest Path (10 sec): Vertex form p(x)=3(x−6)2+14 has vertex (6,14) and a=3>0 (opens up). "Minimum value of the function" ALWAYS means the minimum y-output =14! (Trap B 6 is the x-input where the minimum occurs.)

MATH-D5-Q12 → Correct Answer: A (y = -(5/2)x + 3)

  • Fastest Path (20 sec): Rewrite 2x−5y=20⟹5y=2x−20⟹y=52​x−4 (mℓ​=52​). Perpendicular slope =−25​; with y-intercept (0,3), y=−25​x+3.

MATH-D5-Q13 → Correct Answer: B (100%)

  • Fastest Path (20 sec): Multiply successive percent multipliers on baseline V:
    Vfinal​=V×(1+0.25)×(1−0.20)=V×1.25×0.80=1.00V=100%
    (Trap C 105% adds +25%−20%=+5% additively—classic SAT percent trap!)

MATH-D5-Q14 → Correct Answer (SPR): 7

  • Fastest Path (15 sec Desmos or 25 sec Manual):
    • Square both sides: 3x+28=x2⟹x2−3x−28=(x−7)(x+4)=0.
    • Check in un-squared 3x+28​=x: x=7⟹49​=7 ✓; x=−4⟹16​=+4=−4 (extraneous—reject!). Answer: 7.

MATH-D5-Q15 → Correct Answer: C ((1, 5))

  • Fastest Path (15 sec): Original circle (x+3)2+(y−5)2=49 has center (−3,5). Shifting 4 units right adds +4 to the x-coordinate of the center: (−3+4,5)=(1,5)! (Trap A (-7, 5) shifts left instead of right.)

MATH-D5-Q16 → Correct Answer (SPR): 4

  • Fastest Path (25 sec): For no solution, x- and y-coefficients must be proportional while constants are not:
    k6​=−6−9​=23​⟹3k=12⟹k=4
    (Verify constants: 815​=23​, so parallel distinct lines—no solution ✓!)

MATH-D5-Q17 → Correct Answer: A (10)

  • Fastest Path (25 sec): Convert 1.5 hours=90 minutes! Number of 18-minute half-lives =1890​=5:
    M=320×(0.5)5=32320​=10 mg

MATH-D5-Q18 → Correct Answer (SPR): 84

  • Fastest Path (25 sec): Total points ÷ Total students (NEVER average 78 and 88 to get 83 because group sizes 12=18!):
    Combined Mean=12+1812(78)+18(88)​=30936+1,584​=302,520​=84

MATH-D5-Q19 → Correct Answer: D (11)

  • Fastest Path (25 sec): No real solutions ⟺D=b2−4ac<0:
    (−12)2−4(4)(c)<0⟹144−16c<0⟹16c>144⟹c>9
    Only 11 (Choice D) is strictly greater than 9! (At Trap C 9, D=0⟹ one real solution.)

MATH-D5-Q20 → Correct Answer: B (13)

  • Fastest Path (30 sec Manual or 20 sec Desmos):
    1. Write vertex form using vertex (3,5): f(x)=a(x−3)2+5.
    2. Plug in (0,23): 23=a(0−3)2+5=9a+5⟹9a=18⟹a=2.
    3. Evaluate f(5)=2(5−3)2+5=2(4)+5=13!
    • (Symmetry Shortcut: (0,23) is 3 units from x=3; (5,f(5)) is 2 units from x=3, and Desmos slider a on f(x) = a(x - 3)^2 + 5 hitting (0, 23) reads f(5) = 13 in 15 seconds!)

MATH-D5-Q21 → Correct Answer: C (60)

  • Fastest Path (35 sec):
    1. Thales's Theorem: Because side DF is a diameter of the circle (r=8.5⟹hypotenuse DF=2(8.5)=17), inscribed angle ∠E=90∘!
    2. Use cosD=hypotenuse DFadjacent DE​=178​: since DF=17, leg DE=8.
    3. By the 8-15-17 Pythagorean triple (172−82​=225​=15), perpendicular leg EF=15.
    4. Triangle area =21​(leg1​)(leg2​)=21​(8)(15)=60! (Trap D 120 forgets 21​!)

MATH-D5-Q22 → Correct Answer: B (8)

  • Fastest Path (15 sec Desmos Regression ~!):
    • Line 1: x_1 = [0, 1, 2, 3] (avoids -2 and -5!)
    • Line 2: (6x_1 + 24)/(x_1^2 + 7x_1 + 10) ~ A/(x_1 + 2) + B/(x_1 + 5)
    • Desmos instantly outputs A = 4 and B = 2 ⟹A⋅B=4×2=8!
  • Manual Cover-Up / Clearing Denominators (30 sec): Multiply by (x+2)(x+5)=x2+7x+10:
    6x+24=A(x+5)+B(x+2)
    • Set x=−2: 12=3A⟹A=4.
    • Set x=−5: −6=−3B⟹B=2.
    • Product A⋅B=4×2=8.

errorLab.beforeKeyHtml:
Part A: Morning Pre-Module Cue Card Check (09:00–09:15)

Confirm your 1-page scratchpad header had both checkpoint lines written cleanly before starting today's timed modules:

  • R&W Split-Order Header: Q15–27 (>=22:00 left) → Q1–10 (>=11:00 left) → Q11–14 + Flagged | 75s Bailout!
  • Math Two-Pass Header: Q1–10 (>=24:00 left) → Q11–17 (>=12:00 left) → Q18–22 Scan & Desmos | Box Target!

Part B: Day 5 Timed Module Pacing Audit & Five Pressure Case Studies (EL-D5-CASE-1 to EL-D5-CASE-5)

First fill in your personal Day 5 Simulation Pacing Table:

Timed Module Raw Score Clock at Checkpoint #1 Clock at Checkpoint #2 Any Unanswered / Blind-Guess Rushes? Missed Items Solved Right Untimed (E8)
27-Q R&W (32:00) __ / 27 At Q27: __:__ (Target >=22:00) At Q10: __:__ (Target >=11:00) __ items (Target <=1) __ items
22-Q Math (35:00) __ / 22 At Q10: __:__ (Target >=24:00) At Q17: __:__ (Target >=12:00) __ items (Target <=1) __ items

Now diagnose these 5 realistic Day 5 pacing/pressure errors (E1–E10 + V1–V7 + Fix):
errorLab.caseKeyHtml:
• EL-D5-CASE-1: E8 (Timing problem) + E9 (Wrong strategy — Suboptimal Module Routing) — Fix: Always execute Q15–Q27 FIRST so high-certainty Grammar/Transitions/Synthesis points are banked before touching Q11–Q14.
  • EL-D5-CASE-2: E2 + V4 (Premature Word-Association Trap before Colon) — Fix: Never match a vocabulary choice to a background noun (flashes); read the colon explanation (strict 0.2s tolerance = stringent)!
  • EL-D5-CASE-3: E4 (Misread question) + E7 (Speed-Induced Careless Slip on Easy Item) — Fix: Spend an extra 2 seconds boxing the final noun (perimeter =9+12+15=36)—protecting Module 1 Easy accuracy is worth far more than saving 2 seconds.
  • EL-D5-CASE-4: E1 (Concept gap — Unweighted vs. Weighted Mean Error) — Fix: Whenever group counts differ (n1​=n2​), compute (n1*mean1 + n2*mean2) / (n1 + n2).
  • EL-D5-CASE-5: E9 (Wrong strategy — Skipped 15-sec Desmos Regression on Rational Identity) + E7 (Arithmetic slip) — Fix: Any "holds for all x except..." rational identity is an automatic Desmos ~ problem!

Part C: Mandatory Evening Setup for Tomorrow's Bluebook Practice Test 5 (14:50–14:55)

Before closing Day 5, check off all 4 physical preparation steps so tomorrow morning starts with zero friction:

  • Laptop plugged in to charge to 100% + external mouse ready if preferred.
  • Desk cleared completely except laptop, 3 sharpened pencils/pens, 4 sheets of blank scratch paper, and a closed water bottle.
  • Phone alarm set and charging spot chosen in another room for 09:00–11:40 tomorrow.

lessons.html:
A. Why You Warm Up Your Eyes at 09:05 (Never on Question 1 of the Real Exam!)

Have you ever noticed that during the first 4 minutes of a morning test, you read the same sentence twice because your visual processing speed hasn't shifted into academic English gear yet? Solving 3 easy, familiar-pattern items (RW-D6-Q1..3 + MATH-D6-Q1..3) at 09:05 wakes up your clause-stripping and target-boxing circuits before the Bluebook timer starts—protecting 3–4 precious Module 1 minutes!

B. Scratch-Paper Layout During R&W Modules (2 Sheets)

Fold Sheet 1 into two columns (Module 1 on left, Module 2 on right). Keep notes ultra-minimal:

  • Write your checkpoint targets at the very top the second the module starts: Q27 >= 22:00 | Q10 >= 11:00.
  • ONLY write on R&W scratch paper for three things:
    1. [?] Q# (e.g., ?Q8, ?Q13): Any question where you were below 80% certainty—even if you think you guessed right!
    2. Cross-Text 6-Word Map (Q8): T1: +enrollment / T2: ± loans offset.
    3. Inferences / Hard WIC Elimination (A ✗ B ? C ✗ D ?): Visually crossing out eliminated letters on paper stops your eyes from re-reading dead distractors!

lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 6.2: Sustainable Post-Test R&W Triage — Why We Save Explanations for Tomorrow!
lessons.html:
When you open your Bluebook Practice Test 5 Score Results at 12:40 after lunch, Bluebook gives you two views: (1) Score Overview & Knowledge/Skills Bars and (2) Question-by-Question Review.

Follow This Exact 3-Step Protocol (12:40–13:15 — Zero Burnout!):

  1. Record Macro Scores & Domain Bars First in Section 9A below (R&W Scaled Score, Information & Ideas, Craft & Structure, Expression of Ideas, Standard English Conventions).
  2. Open the Question Table ONLY to Copy Question Numbers & Harvest Vocabulary:
    • Write down every Incorrect Q# (e.g., M1-Q11, M2-Q4, M2-Q12, M2-Q14) and every Correct [?] Guess Q# in Section 9B's Blind Re-Solve Queue.
    • DO NOT CLICK "SHOW EXPLANATION" OR LOOK AT THE CORRECT LETTER! Why? If you see "Correct Answer: C" today while tired after a 2.5-hour exam, your brain nods passively ("Oh yeah, C makes sense") and learns nothing. Tomorrow morning at 09:20 with a fresh brain, re-solving M2-Q12 blind without knowing which letter won forces deep neural rewiring!
  3. Harvest 6–10 Authentic SAT Words from Test 5 Passages & Choices:
    • DO harvest: Reusable academic verbs, tone adjectives, and logical transitions (e.g., corroborate, ostensibly, tenuous, preclude, ameliorate, discrepancy).
    • SKIP harvesting: Proper nouns, Latin species names (Callorhinus ursinus), technical chemistry/geology nouns defined in context (ferrihydrite, pishtaq), or ultra-rare 18th-century archaic literary words unlikely ever to repeat.

Short Comprehension Check — Lessons 6.1 & 6.2 (Check answers in Section 8)

  • CC-D6-RW1: Why should you jot ?Q12 on your scratch paper during the exam even if you end up guessing Q12 correctly?
  • CC-D6-RW2: Why do we forbid reading Bluebook's answer explanations on Day 6 afternoon and save them until after Day 7's morning blind cold re-solve?
  • CC-D6-RW3: On Practice Test 5, you encounter two unfamiliar words: (1) pishtaq (an architectural arch term in a single passage) and (2) vindicate (an answer choice in Words in Context). Which word belongs in your Vocabulary Notebook, and why?
  • CC-D6-RW4: During R&W Module 2, you notice the passages have much denser academic vocabulary than Module 1. What does that tell you about your Module 1 performance, and how should you react emotionally?
