checks.promptHtml: On Practice Test 5 M2-Q11, you picked A under time pressure (wrong). This morning at 09:30, before viewing Bluebook's explanation, you re-solve M2-Q11 untimed and confidently pick D (correct). What does Cold Right prove about your skill vs. your test execution?
checks.answerHtml: Solving M2-Q11 Right Cold without time pressure proves your English comprehension and logic are already intact! Yesterday's error was an execution/pressure leak (E8 timing rush or E4 stem misread), so you should add a 5-second procedural habit trigger rather than wasting time on basic concept videos.

checks.promptHtml: Why is writing "Pay closer attention to answer choices" in Column 7 of your Error Log ineffective compared to writing an IF -> THEN rule?
checks.answerHtml: Vague promises ("pay closer attention") have zero specific visual cue on test day, so your brain reverts to old habits under clock pressure. An IF -> THEN firewall ("IF the conclusion contains whereas, THEN slash the claim into Half 1 / Half 2 and verify both (V7)") triggers automatically the instant that pattern appears on screen.

checks.promptHtml: In the sentence "Vaulted cedar ceilings afford chamber musicians warm acoustic resonance without artificial amplification," what does afford mean?
checks.answerHtml: Here afford means "to provide, supply, or offer" ("terraced timber pavilions provide chamber musicians warm acoustic resonance"), testing secondary academic polysemy (V2) rather than financial cost.

checks.promptHtml: What is Step 3 of the 7-Step Vocabulary Repair Protocol, and why does it build vocabulary independence even for words you never see again?
checks.answerHtml: Step 3 is re-reading the original SAT sentence and circling the exact logical clue (colon, semicolon, although, far from, parallel structure) that dictated the word's meaning. That trains vocabulary independence: even when December 5 introduces an unfamiliar word, you can deduce its polarity and role from sentence architecture.

checks.promptHtml: Is "The excavation uncovered bronze weights, however, no written tablets survived" grammatically valid in Standard English? How do you fix it?
checks.answerHtml: No — it is a comma splice (E6)! However is a conjunctive adverb, NOT a FANBOYS conjunction, so it cannot join two independent clauses with commas alone. Fix: "The excavation uncovered bronze weights; however, no written tablets survived."

subSections.title: A. Day 7 Capstone Precision Vocabulary (Words #55–#60 — Completing Your 60-Word Master Core!)
subSections.titleHtml: A. Day 7 Capstone Precision Vocabulary (Words #55–#60 — Completing Your 60-Word Master Core!)
subSections.html:
Study these final 6 high-precision academic words (#55–#60)—each chosen because it pairs directly with earlier Days 1–6 words to prevent Hard Module 2 confusion traps:

55. circumscribe (verb)

  • Simple English Definition: To draw strict boundaries around something; to restrict or limit power, freedom, or scope.
  • Root Clue & Lookalike Firewall: circum- (around) + scribe (write/draw a line) = draw a limiting circle around! NEVER confuse with circumvent (Day 4 #32 = circum + vent [go around / bypass an obstacle])!
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: restrict, confine, bound, limit · Ant: expand, broaden, liberate.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Venice's Great Council enacted thirteenth-century constitutional statutes specifically designed to circumscribe the Doge's personal treaty-making authority."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: The council passed laws to tightly limit and bound (circumscribe) what the ruler could decide alone.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Mixing up circumscribe ("impose limits on") and circumvent ("cleverly get around limits")—almost exact opposites in institutional passages!
  • Short Application Activity: Choose circumscribed or circumvented: "Strict frost-free growing seasons ______ highland maize cultivation to sheltered valley floors below 2,800 meters." (circumscribed).

56. contentious (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Causing heated disagreement, debate, or controversy among scholars or the public.
  • Lookalike Firewall: Related to the verb contend ("argue/struggle"), NOT the everyday adjective content ("happy/satisfied")!
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: controversial, disputed, debated, polarizing · Ant: uncontroversial, settled, consensus, undisputed.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Whether Clovis stone points represent the earliest human presence in North America—once textbook orthodoxy—became deeply contentious after Monte Verde radiocarbon dates preceded Clovis by a millennium."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Older archaeological dates turned a settled textbook belief into a fiercely debated (contentious) question.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Seeing content- and guessing "peaceful/satisfied" (+), which completely flips the word's true debate/conflict meaning (± / -)!
  • Short Application Activity: If two historians hold contentious views on a treaty, do they agree peacefully or argue sharply? (Argue sharply / disagree!)

57. subordinate (adjective / verb)

  • Simple English Definition: (adj.) Lower in rank, priority, or importance; (verb) to treat something as secondary to a more important goal.
  • Root Clue: sub- (under) + ord (order/rank) = ranked underneath!
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: secondary, lesser, ancillary, subsidiary · Con: primary, paramount, salient (Day 5 #44), overarching.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "In Bauhaus industrial workshops, decorative surface ornament was deliberately subordinated to structural durability and clean geometric function."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Surface decoration was treated as secondary (subordinated) compared to strength and function.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Knowing subordinate clause in grammar but missing the verb "subordinate X to Y" ("make X less important than Y") in art/policy passages.
  • Short Application Activity: In exam-day Math Module 1, should speed be subordinated to accuracy on Q1–Q15, or accuracy subordinated to speed? (Speed subordinated to accuracy—protect those routing points!)

58. immutable (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Unchanging over time; fixed, permanent, and impossible to alter.
  • Root Clue: im- (not) + mut (change, as in mutation) + -able = unable to change!
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: fixed, unchangeable, invariant, permanent · Ant: ephemeral (Day 5 #41), malleable, mutable, tentative (Day 1 #9).
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Before Carl Woese's ribosomal RNA phylogeny, many microbiologists treated bacterial species boundaries as nearly immutable categories rather than fluid lineages shaped by horizontal gene transfer."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Scientists once viewed bacterial species lines as permanently fixed (immutable), before discovering genes jump across species.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Confusing immutable ("unchangeable") with mute ("silent")!
  • Short Application Activity: Does modern neuroscience view adult brain wiring as immutable or adaptable (plastic)? (Adaptable—NOT immutable!)

59. conflate (verb) / conflation (noun)

  • Simple English Definition: To mistakenly blend, mix, or fuse two distinct ideas, measurements, or causes as if they were the exact same thing.
  • Master SAT Contrast Pair: Conflate (blur/lump two different things together — error!) ⟷ Delineate (Day 3 #27) & Discern (Day 5 #46) (clearly separate and distinguish!).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: confuse, fuse, lump together, equate falsely · Ant: distinguish, differentiate, delineate, separate.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Public-health demographers caution against conflating crude hospital admission counts with true disease incidence, since expanded clinic access raises admissions even when infection rates fall."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Analysts warn against falsely treating two distinct metrics as identical (conflating hospital visits with actual new infections).
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Guessing conflate means "inflate/exaggerate" because of the -flate ending (con-flate = blow two separate balloons into one!).
  • Short Application Activity: If a student treats correlation (Day 5 #45) and causation as identical, which verb describes their mistake? (They conflated correlation with causation!)

60. analogous (adjective)

  • Simple English Definition: Comparable or parallel in structure, function, or logic despite belonging to different fields or species.
  • Master SAT Contrast Pair: Analogous (structurally parallel / comparable) ⟷ Disparate (Day 2 #16 = fundamentally different and unrelated).
  • Synonym / Antonym: Syn: comparable, parallel, akin, corresponding · Ant: disparate, dissimilar, divergent, unrelated.
  • Original SAT-Style Contextual Sentence: "Termite-mound ventilation shafts perform a role analogous to mammalian lungs, harnessing wind-driven pressure gradients to exchange underground carbon dioxide for fresh oxygen."
  • Explanation of Contextual Meaning: Mud ventilation shafts and animal lungs look totally different, yet perform a functionally parallel (analogous) gas-exchange job.
  • Common International-Student Misunderstanding: Confusing analogous ("comparable/parallel") with ambiguous ("unclear") or anomalous ("abnormal/outlier")! Watch that trio: analogous (parallel) vs. ambiguous (unclear) vs. anomalous (unusual outlier).
  • Short Application Activity: Are camera lenses and human eye lenses analogous or disparate optical structures? (Analogous!)

subSections.title: B. Official 25-Item Consolidated 7-Day Vocabulary Assessment (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q25)
subSections.titleHtml: B. Official 25-Item Consolidated 7-Day Vocabulary Assessment (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q25)
subSections.html:
Strict Assessment Conditions (11:05–11:25 — 20 Minutes, Closed Notes!):
This cumulative exam tests delayed retention across all 7 days (Words #1–#60) in fresh contexts. Do not peek at your Vocabulary Notebook or Section 8 until all 25 items are answered! Mastery Benchmark: >= 20 / 25 (80%+) (Goal: 22–25 / 25).

Part I: Cumulative SAT-Style Contextual MCQs (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q10)

VOC-D7-Q1 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Far from treating medieval guild charters and rural manor court rolls as ______ legal traditions, historian Sheilagh Ogilvie demonstrates that both institutions enforced remarkably parallel labor-mobility restrictions across central Europe.
A) analogous · B) disparate · C) ubiquitous · D) stringent

VOC-D7-Q2 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Because early seismographs recorded ground motion on smoked-paper drums that had to be swapped manually every twelve hours, nineteenth-century observatories captured ______ tremor archives—preserving major daytime shocks while missing aftershocks during drum changes.
A) immutable · B) unequivocal · C) fragmentary and tentative · D) unprecedented and exhaustive

VOC-D7-Q3 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Critics of single-metric university rankings warn that combining faculty citation counts, alumni salaries, and campus endowment size into one composite score ______ fundamentally distinct educational outcomes that prospective students would be better served evaluating separately.
A) delineates · B) conflates · C) corroborates · D) vindicates

VOC-D7-Q4 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Although municipal building codes ______ mandated fireproof brick party walls between rowhouses after the 1872 blaze, archival insurance maps reveal that speculative builders routinely substituted thin plaster-covered lath whenever inspectors were absent.
A) ostensibly · B) empirically · C) feasibly · D) conversely

VOC-D7-Q5 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Rather than ______ regional dialect diversity as linguistic purists had feared, community-run FM radio stations across highland Oaxaca fostered a surge of Zapotec and Mixtec storytelling broadcasts among younger listeners.
A) augmenting · B) bolstering · C) eroding and precluding · D) catalyzing

VOC-D7-Q6 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
When paleoclimatologists compared Greenland ice-core sulfate spikes against tree-ring frost scars in Irish oaks, the two independent archives closely ______ one another, pinpointing a major northern-hemisphere volcanic veil to 536 CE.
A) refuted · B) circumscribed · C) corroborated · D) exacerbated

VOC-D7-Q7 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Applying crushed basalt dust to weathered tropical croplands serves a dual agronomic purpose: dissolving silicate minerals simultaneously sequesters atmospheric carbon dioxide and ______ chronic soil acidification without synthetic lime.
A) exacerbates · B) ameliorates · C) impedes · D) repudiates

VOC-D7-Q8 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Because fossilized soft gill tissues decay within days unless sealed inside anoxic mudstones, evolutionary links among soft-bodied Cambrian comb jellies remain ______, resting on fewer than a dozen compressed specimens worldwide.
A) compelling · B) tenuous · C) ubiquitous · D) stringent

VOC-D7-Q9 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
By routing insulated district-heating pipes beneath pedestrian sidewalks on its way back to the geothermal plant, Reykjavik's municipal utility ______ the need for chemical de-icing salts during winter snowstorms.
A) entails · B) circumvents · C) underscores · D) attributes

VOC-D7-Q10 [Original SAT-Style Practice — Days 1–7 Synthesis]
Once dismissed as a minor curiosity of desert ecology, biological soil crusts composed of cyanobacteria, lichens, and mosses are now recognized as ______ regulators of arid-land nitrogen cycling whose trampling triggers decades-long dust storms.
A) ephemeral · B) subordinate · C) salient · D) equivocal

Part II: High-Confusion Lookalike & Nuance Duels (VOC-D7-Q11 to VOC-D7-Q18)

Select the single accurate word in parentheses:

  • VOC-D7-Q11 (underscore vs. undermine): "Hospital outbreak audits (underscored / undermined) the lifesaving importance of negative-pressure isolation rooms."
  • VOC-D7-Q12 (circumvent vs. circumscribe): "Emergency constitutional clauses tightly (circumvented / circumscribed) how long martial decrees could remain in force without parliamentary renewal."
  • VOC-D7-Q13 (vindicate vs. vindictive): "High-resolution ALMA telescope rings (vindicated / vindictive) theoretical models of planet-carved dust gaps."
  • VOC-D7-Q14 (feasible vs. plausible): "Tidal heating inside Europa's icy shell offers a (feasible / plausible) geophysical explanation for how a subsurface ocean stays liquid far from the Sun."
  • VOC-D7-Q15 (impede vs. preclude): "Lacking written numerals did not (impede / preclude) Inca administrators from recording complex census tributes on knotted khipu cords."
  • VOC-D7-Q16 (conflate vs. delineate): "Clear zoning maps (conflate / delineate) the exact buffer strip separating tidal salt marshes from upland warehouses."
  • VOC-D7-Q17 (contentious vs. conventional): "Proposed dam removals along salmon rivers sparked (contentious / conventional) public hearings between irrigators and tribal fisheries."
  • VOC-D7-Q18 (exacerbate vs. mitigate): "Paving permeable floodplain meadows into asphalt parking lots (exacerbates / mitigates) downstream flash-flood peaks."

Part III: Closed-Notes Active Recall & Connector Polarity (VOC-D7-Q19 to VOC-D7-Q25)

Write a clear 3–6 word simple English meaning (plus + / - / ± where asked):

  • VOC-D7-Q19: notwithstanding (include logical role) → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q20: albeit (include logical role) → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q21: empirical → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q22: extrapolate → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q23: reciprocity → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q24: immutable → __________________
  • VOC-D7-Q25: caveat → __________________

vocabulary.answerKeyHtml:
Part I (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q10)

  • VOC-D7-Q1: B (disparate) — "Far from treating X and Y as [unrelated/different]..., both enforced parallel restrictions." Disparate (fundamentally different) is negated by Far from, matching parallel in the main clause! (A analogous reverses the Far from negation.)
  • VOC-D7-Q2: C (fragmentary and tentative) — Because smoked-paper drums missed aftershocks during manual 12-hour swaps, records were incomplete and cautious (fragmentary and tentative), not immutable (A), unequivocal (B), or exhaustive (D).
  • VOC-D7-Q3: B (conflates) — Combining fundamentally distinct outcomes into a single composite score falsely fuses/lumps them together (conflates them), the exact opposite of delineates (A = separates clearly).
  • VOC-D7-Q4: A (ostensibly) — Although sets up paper-rule vs. real-practice contrast: codes supposedly on the surface (ostensibly) required brick party walls, yet builders used thin plaster lath whenever uninspected.
  • VOC-D7-Q5: C (eroding and precluding) — "Rather than [-] diversity as purists feared, radio fostered a surge [+]..." Only C carries negative polarity (eroding = undermining, precluding = preventing); A, B, and D are all positive!
  • VOC-D7-Q6: C (corroborated) — Independent Greenland ice cores and Irish oak frost rings confirmed each other with independent evidence (corroborated one another).
  • VOC-D7-Q7: B (ameliorates) — "Serves a dual agronomic purpose" (+ sequesters carbon AND + improves/reduces chronic soil acidification = ameliorates). A (exacerbates), C (impedes), and D (repudiates) are negative.
  • VOC-D7-Q8: B (tenuous) — Resting on fewer than a dozen compressed specimens because soft tissues decay rapidly makes evolutionary links fragile/weakly supported (tenuous).
  • VOC-D7-Q9: B (circumvents) — Warming sidewalks with return geothermal pipes cleverly bypasses/avoids (circumvents) the need for chemical road salt.
  • VOC-D7-Q10: C (salient) — Contrast pivot: "Once dismissed as a minor curiosity... now recognized as [prominent/crucial] regulators" = salient. (A ephemeral = fleeting; B subordinate = secondary; D equivocal = unclear.)

Part II (VOC-D7-Q11 to VOC-D7-Q18)

  • VOC-D7-Q11: underscored (emphasized strongly; undermined = weakened!)
  • VOC-D7-Q12: circumscribed (drew strict legal boundaries around; circumvented = bypassed!)
  • VOC-D7-Q13: vindicated (proved models right; vindictive = spiteful adjective!)
  • VOC-D7-Q14: plausible (believable scientific explanation; feasible = practically doable engineering project!)
  • VOC-D7-Q15: preclude ("did not make impossible" — Inca administrators did record complex censuses on khipu cords!)
  • VOC-D7-Q16: delineate (mark exact boundaries clearly; conflate = blur/confuse!)
  • VOC-D7-Q17: contentious (heatedly debated/controversial; conventional = traditional/routine)
  • VOC-D7-Q18: exacerbates (makes flash-flood peaks worse; mitigates = softens!)

Part III (VOC-D7-Q19 to VOC-D7-Q25)

  • VOC-D7-Q19 (notwithstanding): In spite of / despite (± concession marker that acknowledges an obstacle without cancelling the main claim).
  • VOC-D7-Q20 (albeit): Although / even though (± compact qualifying conjunction introducing a limitation).
  • VOC-D7-Q21 (empirical): Based on real-world observation, measurement, or experiment (not pure theory).
  • VOC-D7-Q22 (extrapolate): To project or estimate unknown values beyond your measured dataset.
  • VOC-D7-Q23 (reciprocity): Mutual two-way exchange that benefits both sides.
  • VOC-D7-Q24 (immutable): Unchanging over time; permanently fixed.
  • VOC-D7-Q25 (caveat): An important warning, caution, or limiting condition attached to a claim.

Consolidated Vocabulary Score Diagnostic:

  • 23–25 / 25 (92–100%): 1400+ Academic Vocabulary Core Locked! Maintain 10-minute spaced reviews every 3 days during Weeks 2–3.
  • 20–22 / 25 (80–88%): Target Met! Move your 3–5 missed words into your Day 8 (Sat, Nov 21) morning sticky deck.
  • < 20 / 25 (<80%): Run the 7-Step Repair Protocol on every missed item before starting Week 2 new words, and re-test Parts I–II on Sunday, Nov 22!

rwPractice.introHtml:
Explicit Origin Notice & Instructions (11:25–11:43 — 18 Minutes, 90 sec/item max):
All 12 items below (RW-D7-Q1–Q12) are original SAT-style practice questions targeting the top Hard-Module score leaks for international students aiming for 650–700+. Apply your IF -> THEN firewalls on every question, and check Section 8 only after finishing all 12! Target: >= 10 / 12 (83.3%+).

questions.stemHtml:
Unlike closed concrete amphitheaters that trap low-frequency street rumble, terraced hillside timber pavilions ______ listeners natural acoustic clarity while allowing summer evening breezes to circulate freely across open seating tiers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: circumvent
afford
circumscribe
conflate

questions.explanationHtml:
• 5-Step Context + Polysemy Check: Contrast Unlike closed concrete amphitheaters that trap rumble (-) ⟷ open timber pavilions give/provide (+) listeners natural acoustic clarity. In academic prose, afford (afford someone X) means "provide or supply" (V2 polysemy).
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (circumvent = bypass), C (circumscribe = restrict), and D (conflate = confuse two things) make zero sense with indirect object listeners + direct object clarity.

questions.stemHtml:
Early twentieth-century foresters treated periodic lodgepole-pine crown fires as purely destructive catastrophes to be suppressed at all costs; subsequent ecological studies of serotinous cones—which remain sealed by resin until intense flame melts the bond to release seeds—revealed that fire exclusion actually ______ forest regeneration by starving sunlit clearings of seedlings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: corroborates
vindicates
impedes
augments

questions.explanationHtml:
• Logical Chain: Lodgepole-pine serotinous cones require intense flame to melt their resin seal and release seeds. Therefore, suppressing fires (fire exclusion) starves clearings of seedlings and hinders/obstructs (C: impedes) forest regeneration!
  • Why Distractors Fail: A (corroborates), B (vindicates), and D (augments = increases) all carry positive polarity, contradicting "starving sunlit clearings of seedlings."

questions.stemHtml:
Because marine radiocarbon reservoirs vary regionally according to deep-water upwelling, archaeologists calibrating shell-midden dates along the Peruvian coast cannot treat a single global ocean correction factor as ______; instead, they measure paired terrestrial twigs and marine shells from identical hearth layers to track local shifts across centuries.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.html: immutable
contentious
ephemeral
tenuous

questions.explanationHtml:
• Context Clue: Semicolon + instead proves contrast: archaeologists track local shifts across centuries using paired twigs and shells because marine radiocarbon reservoirs vary regionally—so a single global correction factor cannot be treated as permanently fixed and unchanging (A: immutable).
  • Why Distractors Fail: Treating a factor as contentious (B), ephemeral (C = short-lived), or tenuous (D = flimsy) would never contrast with needing to track local shifts over time.

questions.stemHtml:
Subglacial Lake Vostok lies buried beneath nearly four kilometers of East Antarctic ice sheet, isolated from surface sunlight for millions of ______ geochemical analyses of accreted basal ice cores indicate that mineral-oxidizing microbes remain metabolically active in its dark, high-pressure waters.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: years, nevertheless,
years; nevertheless,
years, nevertheless
years nevertheless;

questions.explanationHtml:
• Boundary Test (Firewall 1):
    • Left of blank: "Subglacial Lake Vostok lies buried... for millions of years" = Independent Clause 1 (Subject Lake Vostok + finite verb lies).
    • Right of blank: "geochemical analyses... indicate that..." = Independent Clause 2 (Subject analyses + finite verb indicate).
  • Evaluation: Joining two independent clauses via conjunctive adverb nevertheless requires IC ; nevertheless, IC (B). A and C are illegal comma splices (E6); D strands nevertheless without a comma at the end of Clause 1 where it contradicts Clause 1's meaning!

questions.skill: Form, Structure, and Sense (Finite Verb vs. Participial Trap)
questions.stemHtml:
In 1928, Indian physicist C. V. Raman and his colleague K. S. Krishnan—working with focused sunlight, violet glass filters, and sixty purified liquid samples in a Calcutta laboratory—______ that a tiny fraction of scattered photons shifts wavelength upon colliding with vibrating molecular bonds.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: demonstrating
having demonstrated
to demonstrate
demonstrated

questions.explanationHtml: • Clause-Stripping (Firewall 2): Delete the twin-dash participial modifier —working with focused sunlight... laboratory— and introductory phrase In 1928,. Remaining skeleton: "Indian physicist C. V. Raman and his colleague K. S. Krishnan ______ that a tiny fraction..." That main subject requires a finite tense-bearing verb: D (demonstrated)! A (demonstrating), B (having demonstrated), and C (to demonstrate) are non-finite verbals that leave the entire sentence a fragment.

questions.skill: Form, Structure, and Sense (Dangling Introductory Modifier)
questions.stemHtml:
Carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs overlooking desert caravan crossroads in southern Jordan, ______ channeled rare winter flash floods through terracotta wall pipes into covered underground cisterns.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.html: Nabataean hydraulic engineers at Petra

choices.raw: Petra's rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins
choices.html: Petra's rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins

choices.raw: winter rainwater harvested by Nabataean masons
choices.html: winter rainwater harvested by Nabataean masons

choices.raw: subtle two-degree stone gradients designed by Nabataean engineers
choices.html: subtle two-degree stone gradients designed by Nabataean engineers

questions.answerHeadlineHtml: Correct Answer: B (Petra's rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins)
questions.explanationHtml:
• Dangling Modifier Check (Firewall 3): Ask: *Who or what was literally "Carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs"?*
    • Were Nabataean engineers (A) carved into sandstone? No!
    • Was winter rainwater (C) carved into sandstone? No!
    • Were abstract two-degree gradients (D) carved into cliffs overlooking crossroads and channeling floods through wall pipes? No—Petra's physical rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins (B) were literally carved into the rose-red cliffs!

questions.stemHtml:
Literary historian Priya Joshi argues that nineteenth-century Indian circulating-library borrowers did not passively absorb canonical British realist novels promoted by colonial school curricula; rather, Indian readers selectively favored sensational melodramas by authors such as G. W. M. Reynolds—and later adapted melodramatic plot conventions to critique colonial bureaucracy in vernacular Hindi, Bengali, and Marathi fiction.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support both components of Joshi's argument?

choices.raw: Colonial school boards in Bombay and Calcutta purchased thousands of copies of canonical British realist novels by George Eliot and Anthony Trollope between $1860$ and $1890$.
choices.html: Colonial school boards in Bombay and Calcutta purchased thousands of copies of canonical British realist novels by George Eliot and Anthony Trollope between 1860 and 1890.

choices.raw: Surviving loan ledgers from Calcutta public libraries show Reynolds's melodramas checked out four times more often than school-assigned realist novels, while $1880\text{s}$ Bengali serialized novels repurposed Reynolds-style courtroom conspiracy plots to expose corrupt colonial tax collectors.
choices.html: Surviving loan ledgers from Calcutta public libraries show Reynolds's melodramas checked out four times more often than school-assigned realist novels, while 1880s Bengali serialized novels repurposed Reynolds-style courtroom conspiracy plots to expose corrupt colonial tax collectors.

choices.raw: G. W. M. Reynolds's serialized melodramas also outsold canonical realist novels among working-class factory readers in nineteenth-century Manchester and Birmingham.
choices.html: G. W. M. Reynolds's serialized melodramas also outsold canonical realist novels among working-class factory readers in nineteenth-century Manchester and Birmingham.

choices.raw: Several late nineteenth-century Marathi and Hindi novelists translated Sanskrit dramatic treatises before publishing original historical romances.
choices.html: Several late nineteenth-century Marathi and Hindi novelists translated Sanskrit dramatic treatises before publishing original historical romances.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Two-Half Claim Slash: Joshi's thesis has Half 1 (Indian library readers favored sensational melodramas like Reynolds over school-promoted British realist novels) / Half 2 (vernacular Indian writers adapted melodramatic conventions to critique colonial bureaucracy).
  • Evaluation: B proves Half 1 (4× higher Calcutta library checkouts for Reynolds) AND Half 2 (1880s Bengali serials repurposing Reynolds-style plots against corrupt colonial tax collectors). A shows only what school boards bought (not what readers borrowed); C is about British factory cities (E4 wrong geography); D mentions Sanskrit treatises unrelated to Reynolds (V7).

questions.skill: Command of Evidence (Quantitative — Rate vs. Raw Count Trap)
questions.stemHtml:
Pollinator Visits and Seed-Set Efficiency Across Three Alpine Meadow Elevations

Meadow Zone Total Observed Bumblebee Visits Total Open Blossoms Surveyed Visits per 100 Blossoms Flowers Producing Viable Seed (%)
Subalpine (1,900 m) 420 3,000 14.0 74
Treeline (2,400 m) 315 1,500 21.0 79
High Fellfield (2,900 m) 144 1,200 12.0 81

Plant ecologists studying alpine Gentiana populations hypothesized that although raw pollinator counts drop sharply with elevation, high-fellfield plants (2,900 m) compensate physiologically so that viable seed production remains high even when per-blossom visitation intensity falls below subalpine levels.

Which choice best uses data from the table to support the ecologists' hypothesis?

choices.raw: Total observed bumblebee visits fell steadily with elevation, from $420$ at $1{,}900\text{ m}$ to $315$ at $2{,}400\text{ m}$ and $144$ at $2{,}900\text{ m}$.
choices.html: Total observed bumblebee visits fell steadily with elevation, from 420 at 1,900 m to 315 at 2,400 m and 144 at 2,900 m.

choices.raw: Treeline meadows ($2{,}400\text{ m}$) recorded the highest visitation intensity at $21.0$ visits per $100$ blossoms and $79\%$ viable seed production.
choices.html: Treeline meadows (2,400 m) recorded the highest visitation intensity at 21.0 visits per 100 blossoms and 79% viable seed production.

choices.raw: Although high-fellfield meadows ($2{,}900\text{ m}$) received both the fewest total visits ($144$) and fewer visits per $100$ blossoms ($12.0$) than subalpine meadows ($14.0$), $81\%$ of high-fellfield flowers produced viable seed—exceeding the subalpine rate of $74\%$.
choices.html: Although high-fellfield meadows (2,900 m) received both the fewest total visits (144) and fewer visits per 100 blossoms (12.0) than subalpine meadows (14.0), 81% of high-fellfield flowers produced viable seed—exceeding the subalpine rate of 74%.

choices.raw: Subalpine meadows contained $3{,}000$ open blossoms, more than double the $1{,}200$ open blossoms surveyed in high-fellfield meadows.
choices.html: Subalpine meadows contained 3,000 open blossoms, more than double the 1,200 open blossoms surveyed in high-fellfield meadows.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Precision Quantitative Check: Hypothesis = High-fellfield plants (2,900 m) keep viable seed production high even when per-blossom visitation intensity falls below subalpine (1,900 m) levels.
  • Evaluation: C cites both exact comparative metrics: lower per-blossom rate (12.0 vs. 14.0 visits per 100 blossoms, alongside fewest raw visits 144) paired with higher viable seed production (81% vs. 74%). A and D ignore seed production completely (V7); B cites treeline (2,400 m) instead of high fellfield (2,900 m).

questions.stemHtml:
When wild African savanna elephants encounter acoustic playbacks of disturbed honeybee swarms, they emit a distinctive low-frequency "bee-alarm rumble" and retreat rapidly, shaking dust over sensitive ear and trunk membranes. Crucially, elephants played white-noise recordings digitally matched to the exact frequency spectrum and decibel volume of bee swarms show no retreat or head-shaking response, whereas elephants played unaltered bee-alarm rumbles recorded from other elephants retreat even when no bees or bee sounds are present. These results indicate that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.raw: savanna elephants cannot hear acoustic frequencies above white-noise background levels.
choices.html: savanna elephants cannot hear acoustic frequencies above white-noise background levels.

choices.raw: the elephants' defensive retreat is triggered by specific biological acoustic cues in bee buzzing—and can be socially transmitted via conspecific vocalizations—rather than by sheer sound loudness or broad frequency energy alone.
choices.html: the elephants' defensive retreat is triggered by specific biological acoustic cues in bee buzzing—and can be socially transmitted via conspecific vocalizations—rather than by sheer sound loudness or broad frequency energy alone.

choices.raw: honeybee swarms attack savanna elephants more frequently during white-noise playback experiments than during natural foraging.
choices.html: honeybee swarms attack savanna elephants more frequently during white-noise playback experiments than during natural foraging.

choices.raw: young calves must be stung several times before recognizing adult elephants' bee-alarm rumbles.
choices.html: young calves must be stung several times before recognizing adult elephants' bee-alarm rumbles.

questions.explanationHtml:
• 3-Premise Experimental Synthesis:
    1. Bee-swarm sound → alarm rumble + retreat.
    2. Spectrum-and-volume-matched white noise → zero retreat (proving loudness/frequency range alone is NOT the trigger!).
    3. Other elephants' alarm rumble without bees → retreat (proving social vocal transmission!).
  • Evaluation: B integrates all three findings without stretching a single syllable beyond the text. A misreads lack of fear as deafness (E5); C and D invent unmentioned bee stings and calf learning.

questions.stemHtml:
Text 1
Materials scientists developing biodegradable food packaging argue that seaweed-derived alginate films can rapidly replace petroleum-based polyethylene wraps across supermarket supply chains, emphasizing that brown kelp farms require zero freshwater irrigation, zero synthetic fertilizer, and dissolve harmlessly in home compost bins within six weeks.

Text 2
Kelp aquaculture unquestionably avoids the land-and-fertilizer footprint of corn-starch bioplastics, and pure alginate films degrade cleanly at ambient temperatures. Yet unmodified alginate chains are strongly hydrophilic: in humid refrigerated produce aisles, seaweed wraps absorb ambient moisture and lose seventy percent of their tensile tear strength within forty-eight hours unless coated with plant-wax barrier layers that slow home-compost breakdown.

Based on the texts, how would the authors of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's claim about replacing supermarket polyethylene wraps?

choices.raw: By rejecting the claim that brown kelp can be cultivated without synthetic nitrogen fertilizers
choices.html: By rejecting the claim that brown kelp can be cultivated without synthetic nitrogen fertilizers

choices.raw: By acknowledging kelp alginate's agricultural and composting strengths while cautioning that humidity-induced weakening currently creates a performance trade-off between shelf durability and rapid compostability
choices.html: By acknowledging kelp alginate's agricultural and composting strengths while cautioning that humidity-induced weakening currently creates a performance trade-off between shelf durability and rapid compostability

choices.raw: By contending that corn-starch bioplastics outperform polyethylene wraps in humid refrigerated produce aisles
choices.html: By contending that corn-starch bioplastics outperform polyethylene wraps in humid refrigerated produce aisles

choices.raw: By arguing that supermarket supply chains should eliminate refrigerated produce aisles to protect unmodified alginate films
choices.html: By arguing that supermarket supply chains should eliminate refrigerated produce aisles to protect unmodified alginate films

questions.explanationHtml: • 6-Word Cross-Text Map: T1: + seaweed wraps replace polyethylene easily / T2: ± concedes zero-fertilizer + compost perks, BUT 70% humidity tear loss requires wax that slows composting. B captures both the explicit agreement and the shelf-durability vs. rapid-composting trade-off. A contradicts Text 2's first sentence; C and D invent unsupported claims (E5).

questions.stemHtml:
Nineteenth-century Venetian glassblowers on Murano guarded cobalt-and-manganese batch recipes as guild secrets punishable by fines if disclosed abroad. ______ modern X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy allows museum conservators to determine the exact trace-oxide ratios of any Renaissance goblet in ninety seconds without scraping a single microgram of glass.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.html: Today, however,
For this reason,
Likewise,
Specifically,

questions.explanationHtml: • Logical Pivot: Sentence 1 = In the 1800s, Murano glassmakers guarded oxide recipes under strict guild fines (past secrecy). Sentence 2 = Modern X-ray spectroscopy reveals any goblet's exact recipe in 90 seconds without damage (modern transparency). A (Today, however,) marks both the temporal shift and the sharp contrast! B (For this reason,), C (Likewise,), and D (Specifically,) miss the contrast completely.

questions.stemHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Most vertebrate red blood cells rely on iron-rich hemoglobin, which turns bright red when oxygenated and loses oxygen-binding efficiency near 0∘C.
  • Antarctic blackfin icefish (Chaenocephalus aceratus) are the only known vertebrates whose adults completely lack hemoglobin and red blood cells, leaving their blood translucent white.
  • Frigid Southern Ocean waters (−1.8∘C) hold nearly twice as much dissolved oxygen per liter as temperate tropical seas.
  • Blackfin icefish survive without hemoglobin by combining oxygen-rich subzero water with enlarged hearts (4× typical fish size), wide capillary vessels, and low metabolic rates.

The student wants to explain how Antarctic blackfin icefish survive despite lacking oxygen-carrying hemoglobin. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.raw: Unlike most vertebrates whose red blood cells contain iron-rich hemoglobin, adult Antarctic blackfin icefish have translucent white blood with zero red blood cells.
choices.html: Unlike most vertebrates whose red blood cells contain iron-rich hemoglobin, adult Antarctic blackfin icefish have translucent white blood with zero red blood cells.

choices.raw: Cold Southern Ocean water at $-1.8^\circ\text{C}$ holds nearly double the dissolved oxygen of tropical seas, where hemoglobin binds oxygen efficiently.
choices.html: Cold Southern Ocean water at −1.8∘C holds nearly double the dissolved oxygen of tropical seas, where hemoglobin binds oxygen efficiently.

choices.raw: Although adult Antarctic blackfin icefish lack hemoglobin and red blood cells, they survive in oxygen-rich $-1.8^\circ\text{C}$ waters through enlarged hearts, wide capillaries, and low metabolic demand.
choices.html: Although adult Antarctic blackfin icefish lack hemoglobin and red blood cells, they survive in oxygen-rich −1.8∘C waters through enlarged hearts, wide capillaries, and low metabolic demand.

choices.raw: Antarctic blackfin icefish (*Chaenocephalus aceratus*) possess hearts four times larger than those of typical temperate fishes.
choices.html: Antarctic blackfin icefish (Chaenocephalus aceratus) possess hearts four times larger than those of typical temperate fishes.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Goal-First Synthesis Audit: Goal = explain HOW Antarctic blackfin icefish survive despite lacking hemoglobin.
  • Evaluation: Only C states both the challenge (lack hemoglobin and red blood cells) and the complete survival mechanism (oxygen-rich −1.8∘C water + enlarged hearts, wide capillaries, and low metabolic demand). A states only that they lack hemoglobin (not how they survive); B omits icefish altogether; D mentions heart size without connecting it to surviving without hemoglobin.

lessons.title: Lesson 7.3: Deep Math Blind Cold Re-Solve & The 15-Second Desmos Retrofit (12:40–13:45)
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 7.3: Deep Math Blind Cold Re-Solve & The 15-Second Desmos Retrofit (12:40–13:45)
lessons.html:
During your afternoon Math workshop, take your Day 6 Section 9B Math Queue (QS / TR / DM / CU items) and run this strict 2-Pass Protocol on every single item before opening Bluebook's step-by-step explanation:

  1. Pass 1 — Untimed Cold Re-Solve (Scratch Paper + Desmos Open):
    • If you get it right cold in <60 seconds, your math knowledge is already 100% solid! Log the exact trigger that failed yesterday (e.g., E4 forgot to box diameter vs. radius, E8 ran out of clock because I didn't skip Q19 first).
    • If you still get stuck cold (CU), click "Show Explanation", study the theorem, close the explanation, and re-derive the answer from a blank sheet!
  2. Pass 2 — Mandatory 15-Second Desmos Retrofit Check:
    • Even on items you solved algebraically, ask: "Could Desmos have solved or verified this in <15 seconds?"
    • Three High-Yield Desmos Retrofits to Master Today:
      • 3-Point Quadratic/Exponential Table Regression: Click + → Table, enter (x1​,y1​) pairs, and type y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c (or y_1 ~ a b^(x_1)). Desmos hands you exact constants a, b, c in 10 seconds!
      • Equivalent-Expression Graph Overlay: Graph the prompt expression as f(x) = ... and graph Choices A–D; the choice whose curve lies 100% on top of f(x) for all valid x wins instantly!
      • System / Tangency Slider (k): Type y = 4x + k and y = x^2 - 2x + 13, add slider k, and slide until the line barely kisses the parabola at one tangent point—instant visual confirmation of your b2−4ac=0 algebra!

lessons.title: Lesson 7.4: Master High-Leak Math Consolidation Firewall (640 -> 700–750+)
lessons.titleHtml: Lesson 7.4: Master High-Leak Math Consolidation Firewall (640 -> 700–750+)
lessons.html:
Keep these 6 Surgical Rules crystal clear as you enter MATH-D7-Q1–Q12 and Weeks 2–3:

High-Leak Trap Careless Mistake (640 Habit) 1400+ Strategist Firewall (700–750+ Habit)
1. "Increased by P%" when P≥100 Multiplying by 1.50 for "increased by 150%" Multiplier =1+100P​! "Increased by 150%" =1+1.50=2.50×; "is 150% of" =1.50×!
2. Vertex Input x vs. Output y Giving max height/revenue y when asked for time/price x (or vice versa!) Box the noun right after "what...": At what price/time =h=−2ab​; What maximum value =k=f(h)!
3. Removing an Outlier (Mean vs. Median) Assuming median always changes (or never changes) when an extreme value is dropped Write out the middle indices! Mean always shifts away from a removed outlier; median shifts only if the middle slot value(s) change!
4. Similar 2D / 3D Scaling (s,s2,s3) Scaling surface area by volume ratio (or by linear ratio s) Take cube root of volume ratio first (s=3VB​/VA​​), then square s for any area (AB​/AA​=s2)!
5. Circle Diameter Endpoints → Sector/Area Using diameter d directly as radius r! The second you see the word diameter, write r = d / 2 in giant letters inside your scratch box!
6. Survey Generalization Scope Generalizing a commuter-route sample to "all city residents" You can generalize ONLY to the exact population from which the random sample was drawn!

Short Comprehension Check — Lessons 7.3 & 7.4 (Check answers in Section 8)

  • CC-D7-M1: Website traffic was 400 visits/day in May and increased by 200% by October. How many visits/day occurred in October?
  • CC-D7-M2: How do you find a,b,c in 12 seconds in Desmos when given three points (−1,13), (1,1), and (3,5) on y=ax2+bx+c?
  • CC-D7-M3: Solid X and similar solid Y have volumes in the ratio 8:125. What is the ratio of their surface areas?
  • CC-D7-M4: For h(t)=−16(t−3)2+150, what is (a) the time t at maximum height, and (b) the maximum height?
  • CC-D7-M5: On Practice Test 5 Math M2-Q17, you missed the question yesterday (TR), then solved it right cold in 45 seconds today before opening the explanation. Do you need a 20-minute Khan Academy concept lesson on that topic? Why or why not?

outline.text: Short Comprehension Check — Lessons 7.3 & 7.4 (Check answers in Section 8)

checks.promptHtml: Website traffic was 400 visits/day in May and increased by 200% by October. How many visits/day occurred in October?
checks.answerHtml: 1,200 visits/day! "Increased by 200%" means original (100%) + increase (200%) =300%=3.00×⟹400×3=1,200 (never 400×2=800!).

checks.promptHtml: How do you find a,b,c in 12 seconds in Desmos when given three points (−1,13), (1,1), and (3,5) on y=ax2+bx+c?
checks.answerHtml: In Desmos, click + → Table, type -1, 1, 3 under x_1 and 13, 1, 5 under y_1, then on Line 2 type y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c. Desmos immediately outputs a = 2, b = -6, c = 5!

checks.promptHtml: Solid X and similar solid Y have volumes in the ratio 8:125. What is the ratio of their surface areas?
checks.answerHtml: 4 : 25. Take the cube root of the volume ratio first to get the linear ratio (s=38​:3125​=2:5), then square the linear ratio for surface area (s2=22:52=4:25).

checks.promptHtml: For h(t)=−16(t−3)2+150, what is (a) the time t at maximum height, and (b) the maximum height?
checks.answerHtml: In vertex form h(t)=−16(t−3)2+150: (a) time at maximum height t=3; (b) maximum height =150.

checks.promptHtml: On Practice Test 5 Math M2-Q17, you missed the question yesterday (TR), then solved it right cold in 45 seconds today before opening the explanation. Do you need a 20-minute Khan Academy concept lesson on that topic? Why or why not?
checks.answerHtml: No! Solving M2-Q17 cold in 45 seconds proves you have zero E1 concept gap on that math topic. Watching a 20-minute video wastes valuable prep time; instead, enforce your E8 Module 2 two-pass skipping rule so you reach Q17 with plenty of clock left!

mathPractice.introHtml:
Explicit Origin Notice & Instructions (14:00–14:22 — 22 Minutes Timed, then Attempt → Check → Re-solve):
All 12 problems below (MATH-D7-Q1–Q12: 8 Multiple Choice + 4 SPR) are original SAT-style practice questions stress-testing the highest-yield 640 -> 750 traps across all 4 Math domains. Box every target expression, apply your 5-Second Desmos vs. Manual check, and do not view Section 8 until finished! Target: >= 10 / 12 (83.3%+, Goal 11–12 / 12).

questions.skill: Linear Equations with Infinitely Many Solutions
questions.stemHtml:
3(2x−5)=ax−b
In the given equation, a and b are constants. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of a+b?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Distribute Left Side: 3(2x−5)=6x−15.
  • Match Coefficients (Infinitely Many Solutions): Since 6x−15=ax−b for all x, a=6 and −b=−15⟹b=15 (watch the minus sign already printed before b!).
  • Boxed Target: a+b=6+15=21. (Sign trap: writing b=−15 gives −9, wrong!)

questions.stemHtml: A coastal mangrove restoration site covered 80 hectares in 2018. Between 2018 and 2024, the area of the restoration site increased by 150%. How many hectares did the restoration site cover in 2024?

choices.html: 120
150
200
230

questions.explanationHtml:
• Firewall 1 (Increased by P%): An increase of 150% adds 1.50×80=120 hectares on top of the original 80 hectares:
    80×(1+1.50)=80×2.50=200 (C)
  • Trap Alert: Choice A (120) computes 150% of 80 instead of increased by 150%!

questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, line p is defined by 2x+5y=20. Line q is perpendicular to line p and passes through the point (4,3). What is the y-intercept of line q?

choices.html: (0,−7)
(0,−5)
(0,4)
(0,13)

questions.explanationHtml:
• Find Slope of Line p: 2x+5y=20⟹5y=−2x+20⟹y=−52​x+4, so mp​=−52​.
  • Perpendicular Slope mq​: Opposite reciprocal =+25​.
  • Point-Slope Through (4,3): y−3=25​(x−4)=25​x−10⟹y=25​x−7. Thus the y-intercept is (0,−7) (A).

questions.stemHtml:
M(t)=640(0.5)t/12
The function M models the mass, in milligrams, of a diagnostic medical tracer remaining in a patient's bloodstream t hours after injection. How many milligrams of the tracer remain 36 hours after injection?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Substitute t=36: Number of 12-hour half-lives =1236​=3.
  • Compute: M(36)=640(0.5)3=640×81​=80. Type 80.

questions.stemHtml:
x−45​−x+12​
Which expression is equivalent to the given expression for x>4?

choices.html: x2−3x−43​
x2−3x−43x−3​
x2−3x−43x+13​
x2−3x−47x−3​

questions.explanationHtml:
• Common Denominator (x−4)(x+1)=x2−3x−4:
    (x−4)(x+1)5(x+1)−2(x−4)​=x2−3x−45x+5−2x+8​=x2−3x−43x+13​ (C)
  • Desmos 10-Second Verification: Graph f(x) = 5/(x - 4) - 2/(x + 1) and g(x) = (3x + 13)/(x^2 - 3x - 4)—their curves overlap 100%! (Trap B forgets −2(−4)=+8 and writes 5−8=−3.)

questions.skill: Quadratic Vertex Input vs. Output Trap
questions.stemHtml:
R(p)=−4p2+120p−200
The function R models a community theater's weekly ticket revenue, in dollars, when tickets are priced at p dollars each. At what ticket price p, in dollars, does the theater achieve its maximum weekly ticket revenue?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Firewall 2 (Box Input vs. Output!): The question asks *"At what ticket price p"* (x-coordinate of vertex), NOT "What is the maximum weekly revenue" (y-coordinate =700)!
  • Vertex Formula (or Desmos Click): p=−2ab​=−2(−4)120​=8120​=15. Type 15.

questions.skill: Quadratic Function from Three Points (Desmos Table Regression)
questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, the graph of the quadratic function y=f(x) is a parabola that passes through the points (−1,13), (1,1), and (3,5). What is the value of f(4)?

choices.html: 9
11
13
17

questions.explanationHtml:
• Desmos Regression Winner (12 Seconds):
    1. Insert Table (x_1, y_1) with rows (-1, 13), (1, 1), (3, 5).
    2. On Line 2, type y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c → Desmos outputs a = 2, b = -6, c = 5.
    3. Evaluate f(4)=2(4)2−6(4)+5=32−24+5=13 (C).
  • Bonus Parabolic Symmetry Shortcut: Vertex is at x=−2(2)−6​=1.5. Since x=4 is 2.5 units right of 1.5 and x=−1 is 2.5 units left of 1.5, f(4)=f(−1)=13 immediately!

questions.stemHtml:
yy​=x2−2x+13=4x+k​
In the given system of equations, k is a constant. If the system has exactly one real solution (x,y), what is the value of k?
questions.explanationHtml:
• Set Equal for Intersection: x2−2x+13=4x+k⟹x2−6x+(13−k)=0.
  • Exactly One Real Solution ⟹ Discriminant =0:
    b2−4ac=(−6)2−4(1)(13−k)=36−52+4k=0⟹4k=16⟹k=4
  • Desmos Check: Graph y = x^2 - 2x + 13 and y = 4x + 4; they touch at the single tangent point (3,16)!

questions.stemHtml: A regional transit authority surveyed a random sample of 400 weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B and found that 68% supported adding a 6:15 a.m. express sailing, with an associated margin of error of 4.5%. To which population can these survey results most appropriately be generalized?

choices.raw: All residents of the harbor metropolitan area
choices.html: All residents of the harbor metropolitan area

choices.raw: All ferry passengers across all regional routes and days of the week
choices.html: All ferry passengers across all regional routes and days of the week

choices.raw: All weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B
choices.html: All weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B

choices.raw: Only the $400$ passengers who responded to the survey
choices.html: Only the 400 passengers who responded to the survey

questions.explanationHtml: • Firewall 6 (Sampling Frame = Inference Scope): Because the random sample was drawn exclusively from weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B, results generalize validly to all weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B (C)—neither broader to all city residents/weekend routes (A, B) nor restricted only to the 400 respondents (D).

questions.skill: Outlier Removal Effect on Mean vs. Median
questions.stemHtml:
Dataset P consists of the 9 values listed below in ascending order:

12,14,15,20,20,22,24,26,63
Dataset Q is formed by removing the single value 63 from Dataset P. How do the mean and median of Dataset Q compare to the mean and median of Dataset P?

choices.raw: Both the mean and the median of Dataset $Q$ are less than those of Dataset $P$.
choices.html: Both the mean and the median of Dataset Q are less than those of Dataset P.

choices.raw: The mean of Dataset $Q$ is less than the mean of Dataset $P$, and the medians are equal.
choices.html: The mean of Dataset Q is less than the mean of Dataset P, and the medians are equal.

choices.raw: The means are equal, and the median of Dataset $Q$ is less than the median of Dataset $P$.
choices.html: The means are equal, and the median of Dataset Q is less than the median of Dataset P.

choices.raw: The mean of Dataset $Q$ is less than the mean of Dataset $P$, and the median of Dataset $Q$ is greater than the median of Dataset $P$.
choices.html: The mean of Dataset Q is less than the mean of Dataset P, and the median of Dataset Q is greater than the median of Dataset P.

questions.explanationHtml:
• Check Mean: Removing the high outlier 63 (which sits well above Dataset P's mean of 216/9=24) pulls the mean down to 153/8=19.125. Thus mean decreases.
  • Check Median (Firewall 3 — Write Middle Slots!):
    • Dataset P (9 values): 5th value =20.
    • Dataset Q (8 values: 12,14,15,20,20,22,24,26): average of 4th and 5th values =220+20​=20!
    • Because both middle slots equal 20, the medians are equal (B)! (Trap A blindly assumes dropping the max always lowers the median!)

questions.stemHtml: Right circular cylinder A has a volume of 54π cm3, and right circular cylinder B has a volume of 128π cm3. Cylinder A is similar to cylinder B. If the lateral surface area of cylinder A is 36π cm2, what is the lateral surface area, in cm2, of cylinder B?

choices.html: 48π
64π
85π
96π

questions.answerHeadlineHtml: Correct Answer: B (64π)
questions.explanationHtml:
• Firewall 4 (s3→s→s2):
    1. Volume ratio: VA​VB​​=54π128π​=2764​.
    2. Linear scale factor: s=32764​​=34​.
    3. Surface-area scale factor: s2=(34​)2=916​.
    4. Lateral surface area of B=36π×916​=4π×16=64π (B).
  • Trap Alert: A (48π) multiplies by s=4/3; C (85π) multiplies by s3=64/27.

questions.skill: Circle Diameter Endpoints & Radian Sector Area
questions.stemHtml: In the xy-plane, line segment PQ is a diameter of a circle, with endpoints P(−2,1) and Q(6,7). What is the area of a sector of this circle formed by a central angle of 52π​ radians?

choices.html: 2π
5π
10π
20π

questions.answerHeadlineHtml: Correct Answer: B (5π)
questions.explanationHtml:
• Step 1 (Distance Formula for Diameter PQ):
    d=(6−(−2))2+(7−1)2​=82+62​=100​=10
  • Step 2 (Firewall 5 — Halve Diameter Immediately!): r=210​=5.
  • Step 3 (Radian Sector Area Formula):
    Asector​=21​r2θ=21​(52)(52π​)=225​⋅52π​=5π (B)
  • Trap Alert: D (20π) plugs d=10 into 21​r2θ without dividing by 2!

Any item missed on VOC-D7-Q1..25, RW-D7-Q1..12, or MATH-D7-Q1..12 must be added to your Sticky Weekend Deck (Day 8 / Saturday, Nov 21) and re-solved from a blank page before moving on!

subSections.title: A. Lesson Comprehension Checks (CC-D7-RW1–RW5 & CC-D7-M1–M5)
subSections.titleHtml: A. Lesson Comprehension Checks (CC-D7-RW1–RW5 & CC-D7-M1–M5)
subSections.html:
• CC-D7-RW1: Solving M2-Q11 Right Cold without time pressure proves your English comprehension and logic are already intact! Yesterday's error was an execution/pressure leak (E8 timing rush or E4 stem misread), so you should add a 5-second procedural habit trigger rather than wasting time on basic concept videos.
  • CC-D7-RW2: Vague promises ("pay closer attention") have zero specific visual cue on test day, so your brain reverts to old habits under clock pressure. An IF -> THEN firewall ("IF the conclusion contains whereas, THEN slash the claim into Half 1 / Half 2 and verify both (V7)") triggers automatically the instant that pattern appears on screen.
  • CC-D7-RW3: Here afford means "to provide, supply, or offer" ("terraced timber pavilions provide chamber musicians warm acoustic resonance"), testing secondary academic polysemy (V2) rather than financial cost.
  • CC-D7-RW4: Step 3 is re-reading the original SAT sentence and circling the exact logical clue (colon, semicolon, although, far from, parallel structure) that dictated the word's meaning. That trains vocabulary independence: even when December 5 introduces an unfamiliar word, you can deduce its polarity and role from sentence architecture.
  • CC-D7-RW5: No — it is a comma splice (E6)! However is a conjunctive adverb, NOT a FANBOYS conjunction, so it cannot join two independent clauses with commas alone. Fix: "The excavation uncovered bronze weights; however, no written tablets survived."
  • CC-D7-M1: 1,200 visits/day! "Increased by 200%" means original (100%) + increase (200%) =300%=3.00×⟹400×3=1,200 (never 400×2=800!).
  • CC-D7-M2: In Desmos, click + → Table, type -1, 1, 3 under x_1 and 13, 1, 5 under y_1, then on Line 2 type y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c. Desmos immediately outputs a = 2, b = -6, c = 5!
  • CC-D7-M3: 4 : 25. Take the cube root of the volume ratio first to get the linear ratio (s=38​:3125​=2:5), then square the linear ratio for surface area (s2=22:52=4:25).
  • CC-D7-M4: In vertex form h(t)=−16(t−3)2+150: (a) time at maximum height t=3; (b) maximum height =150.
  • CC-D7-M5: No! Solving M2-Q17 cold in 45 seconds proves you have zero E1 concept gap on that math topic. Watching a 20-minute video wastes valuable prep time; instead, enforce your E8 Module 2 two-pass skipping rule so you reach Q17 with plenty of clock left!

subSections.title: B. Official 25-Item Consolidated 7-Day Vocabulary Assessment (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q25)
subSections.titleHtml: B. Official 25-Item Consolidated 7-Day Vocabulary Assessment (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q25)
subSections.html:
Part I (VOC-D7-Q1 to VOC-D7-Q10)

  • VOC-D7-Q1: B (disparate) — "Far from treating X and Y as [unrelated/different]..., both enforced parallel restrictions." Disparate (fundamentally different) is negated by Far from, matching parallel in the main clause! (A analogous reverses the Far from negation.)
  • VOC-D7-Q2: C (fragmentary and tentative) — Because smoked-paper drums missed aftershocks during manual 12-hour swaps, records were incomplete and cautious (fragmentary and tentative), not immutable (A), unequivocal (B), or exhaustive (D).
  • VOC-D7-Q3: B (conflates) — Combining fundamentally distinct outcomes into a single composite score falsely fuses/lumps them together (conflates them), the exact opposite of delineates (A = separates clearly).
  • VOC-D7-Q4: A (ostensibly) — Although sets up paper-rule vs. real-practice contrast: codes supposedly on the surface (ostensibly) required brick party walls, yet builders used thin plaster lath whenever uninspected.
  • VOC-D7-Q5: C (eroding and precluding) — "Rather than [-] diversity as purists feared, radio fostered a surge [+]..." Only C carries negative polarity (eroding = undermining, precluding = preventing); A, B, and D are all positive!
  • VOC-D7-Q6: C (corroborated) — Independent Greenland ice cores and Irish oak frost rings confirmed each other with independent evidence (corroborated one another).
  • VOC-D7-Q7: B (ameliorates) — "Serves a dual agronomic purpose" (+ sequesters carbon AND + improves/reduces chronic soil acidification = ameliorates). A (exacerbates), C (impedes), and D (repudiates) are negative.
  • VOC-D7-Q8: B (tenuous) — Resting on fewer than a dozen compressed specimens because soft tissues decay rapidly makes evolutionary links fragile/weakly supported (tenuous).
  • VOC-D7-Q9: B (circumvents) — Warming sidewalks with return geothermal pipes cleverly bypasses/avoids (circumvents) the need for chemical road salt.
  • VOC-D7-Q10: C (salient) — Contrast pivot: "Once dismissed as a minor curiosity... now recognized as [prominent/crucial] regulators" = salient. (A ephemeral = fleeting; B subordinate = secondary; D equivocal = unclear.)

Part II (VOC-D7-Q11 to VOC-D7-Q18)

  • VOC-D7-Q11: underscored (emphasized strongly; undermined = weakened!)
  • VOC-D7-Q12: circumscribed (drew strict legal boundaries around; circumvented = bypassed!)
  • VOC-D7-Q13: vindicated (proved models right; vindictive = spiteful adjective!)
  • VOC-D7-Q14: plausible (believable scientific explanation; feasible = practically doable engineering project!)
  • VOC-D7-Q15: preclude ("did not make impossible" — Inca administrators did record complex censuses on khipu cords!)
  • VOC-D7-Q16: delineate (mark exact boundaries clearly; conflate = blur/confuse!)
  • VOC-D7-Q17: contentious (heatedly debated/controversial; conventional = traditional/routine)
  • VOC-D7-Q18: exacerbates (makes flash-flood peaks worse; mitigates = softens!)

Part III (VOC-D7-Q19 to VOC-D7-Q25)

  • VOC-D7-Q19 (notwithstanding): In spite of / despite (± concession marker that acknowledges an obstacle without cancelling the main claim).
  • VOC-D7-Q20 (albeit): Although / even though (± compact qualifying conjunction introducing a limitation).
  • VOC-D7-Q21 (empirical): Based on real-world observation, measurement, or experiment (not pure theory).
  • VOC-D7-Q22 (extrapolate): To project or estimate unknown values beyond your measured dataset.
  • VOC-D7-Q23 (reciprocity): Mutual two-way exchange that benefits both sides.
  • VOC-D7-Q24 (immutable): Unchanging over time; permanently fixed.
  • VOC-D7-Q25 (caveat): An important warning, caution, or limiting condition attached to a claim.

Consolidated Vocabulary Score Diagnostic:

  • 23–25 / 25 (92–100%): 1400+ Academic Vocabulary Core Locked! Maintain 10-minute spaced reviews every 3 days during Weeks 2–3.
  • 20–22 / 25 (80–88%): Target Met! Move your 3–5 missed words into your Day 8 (Sat, Nov 21) morning sticky deck.
  • < 20 / 25 (<80%): Run the 7-Step Repair Protocol on every missed item before starting Week 2 new words, and re-test Parts I–II on Sunday, Nov 22!

subSections.titleHtml: C. Targeted Reading & Writing Consolidation Set (RW-D7-Q1 to RW-D7-Q12)
subSections.html:
Question Answer Domain & Skill Firewall Applied
RW-D7-Q1 B C&S · Words in Context Secondary polysemy (V2): afford = provide/supply acoustic clarity
RW-D7-Q2 C C&S · Words in Context Blocking flame-triggered seed release impedes (hinders) regeneration
RW-D7-Q3 A C&S · Words in Context Regional upwelling shifts → correction factor is NOT immutable (unchanging)
RW-D7-Q4 B SEC · Boundaries IC ; conjunctive adverb, (years; nevertheless,) prevents comma splice (E6)
RW-D7-Q5 D SEC · Finite Verb Strip —working... laboratory— → subject needs finite verb demonstrated
RW-D7-Q6 B SEC · Dangling Modifier Subject after comma must literally be carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs!
RW-D7-Q7 B I&I · Textual Evidence Proves BOTH halves: 4× Reynolds loan rate + Bengali anti-colonial plot adaptation
RW-D7-Q8 C I&I · Quant Evidence Compares BOTH rate (12.0<14.0 per 100) AND higher seed set (81%>74%)
RW-D7-Q9 B I&I · Inferences Accounts for all 3 controls: bee cue + white-noise null + social alarm rumble
RW-D7-Q10 B C&S · Cross-Text Qualified response (±): concedes eco perks, highlights humidity vs. compost trade-off
RW-D7-Q11 A EOI · Transitions Past guarded secrecy ⟷ modern 90-sec X-ray disclosure = Today, however,
RW-D7-Q12 C EOI · Rhetorical Synthesis Explains how icefish survive without hemoglobin (cold O2​-rich water + 4× heart)

Detailed Distractor-by-Distractor Teaching Explanations

  1. RW-D7-Q1 — Correct Answer: B (afford)

    • 5-Step Context + Polysemy Check: Contrast Unlike closed concrete amphitheaters that trap rumble (-) ⟷ open timber pavilions give/provide (+) listeners natural acoustic clarity. In academic prose, afford (afford someone X) means "provide or supply" (V2 polysemy).
    • Why Distractors Fail: A (circumvent = bypass), C (circumscribe = restrict), and D (conflate = confuse two things) make zero sense with indirect object listeners + direct object clarity.

  2. RW-D7-Q2 — Correct Answer: C (impedes)

    • Logical Chain: Lodgepole-pine serotinous cones require intense flame to melt their resin seal and release seeds. Therefore, suppressing fires (fire exclusion) starves clearings of seedlings and hinders/obstructs (C: impedes) forest regeneration!
    • Why Distractors Fail: A (corroborates), B (vindicates), and D (augments = increases) all carry positive polarity, contradicting "starving sunlit clearings of seedlings."

  3. RW-D7-Q3 — Correct Answer: A (immutable)

    • Context Clue: Semicolon + instead proves contrast: archaeologists track local shifts across centuries using paired twigs and shells because marine radiocarbon reservoirs vary regionally—so a single global correction factor cannot be treated as permanently fixed and unchanging (A: immutable).
    • Why Distractors Fail: Treating a factor as contentious (B), ephemeral (C = short-lived), or tenuous (D = flimsy) would never contrast with needing to track local shifts over time.

  4. RW-D7-Q4 — Correct Answer: B (years; nevertheless,)

    • Boundary Test (Firewall 1):
      • Left of blank: "Subglacial Lake Vostok lies buried... for millions of years" = Independent Clause 1 (Subject Lake Vostok + finite verb lies).
      • Right of blank: "geochemical analyses... indicate that..." = Independent Clause 2 (Subject analyses + finite verb indicate).
    • Evaluation: Joining two independent clauses via conjunctive adverb nevertheless requires IC ; nevertheless, IC (B). A and C are illegal comma splices (E6); D strands nevertheless without a comma at the end of Clause 1 where it contradicts Clause 1's meaning!

  5. RW-D7-Q5 — Correct Answer: D (demonstrated)

    • Clause-Stripping (Firewall 2): Delete the twin-dash participial modifier —working with focused sunlight... laboratory— and introductory phrase In 1928,. Remaining skeleton: "Indian physicist C. V. Raman and his colleague K. S. Krishnan ______ that a tiny fraction..." That main subject requires a finite tense-bearing verb: D (demonstrated)! A (demonstrating), B (having demonstrated), and C (to demonstrate) are non-finite verbals that leave the entire sentence a fragment.

  6. RW-D7-Q6 — Correct Answer: B (Petra's rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins)

    • Dangling Modifier Check (Firewall 3): Ask: *Who or what was literally "Carved directly into rose-red sandstone cliffs"?*
      • Were Nabataean engineers (A) carved into sandstone? No!
      • Was winter rainwater (C) carved into sandstone? No!
      • Were abstract two-degree gradients (D) carved into cliffs overlooking crossroads and channeling floods through wall pipes? No—Petra's physical rock-cut facades and rock-hewn aqueduct basins (B) were literally carved into the rose-red cliffs!

  7. RW-D7-Q7 — Correct Answer: B

    • Two-Half Claim Slash: Joshi's thesis has Half 1 (Indian library readers favored sensational melodramas like Reynolds over school-promoted British realist novels) / Half 2 (vernacular Indian writers adapted melodramatic conventions to critique colonial bureaucracy).
    • Evaluation: B proves Half 1 (4× higher Calcutta library checkouts for Reynolds) AND Half 2 (1880s Bengali serials repurposing Reynolds-style plots against corrupt colonial tax collectors). A shows only what school boards bought (not what readers borrowed); C is about British factory cities (E4 wrong geography); D mentions Sanskrit treatises unrelated to Reynolds (V7).

  8. RW-D7-Q8 — Correct Answer: C

    • Precision Quantitative Check: Hypothesis = High-fellfield plants (2,900 m) keep viable seed production high even when per-blossom visitation intensity falls below subalpine (1,900 m) levels.
    • Evaluation: C cites both exact comparative metrics: lower per-blossom rate (12.0 vs. 14.0 visits per 100 blossoms, alongside fewest raw visits 144) paired with higher viable seed production (81% vs. 74%). A and D ignore seed production completely (V7); B cites treeline (2,400 m) instead of high fellfield (2,900 m).

  9. RW-D7-Q9 — Correct Answer: B

    • 3-Premise Experimental Synthesis:
      1. Bee-swarm sound → alarm rumble + retreat.
      2. Spectrum-and-volume-matched white noise → zero retreat (proving loudness/frequency range alone is NOT the trigger!).
      3. Other elephants' alarm rumble without bees → retreat (proving social vocal transmission!).
    • Evaluation: B integrates all three findings without stretching a single syllable beyond the text. A misreads lack of fear as deafness (E5); C and D invent unmentioned bee stings and calf learning.

  10. RW-D7-Q10 — Correct Answer: B

    • 6-Word Cross-Text Map: T1: + seaweed wraps replace polyethylene easily / T2: ± concedes zero-fertilizer + compost perks, BUT 70% humidity tear loss requires wax that slows composting. B captures both the explicit agreement and the shelf-durability vs. rapid-composting trade-off. A contradicts Text 2's first sentence; C and D invent unsupported claims (E5).

  11. RW-D7-Q11 — Correct Answer: A (Today, however,)

    • Logical Pivot: Sentence 1 = In the 1800s, Murano glassmakers guarded oxide recipes under strict guild fines (past secrecy). Sentence 2 = Modern X-ray spectroscopy reveals any goblet's exact recipe in 90 seconds without damage (modern transparency). A (Today, however,) marks both the temporal shift and the sharp contrast! B (For this reason,), C (Likewise,), and D (Specifically,) miss the contrast completely.

  12. RW-D7-Q12 — Correct Answer: C

    • Goal-First Synthesis Audit: Goal = explain HOW Antarctic blackfin icefish survive despite lacking hemoglobin.
    • Evaluation: Only C states both the challenge (lack hemoglobin and red blood cells) and the complete survival mechanism (oxygen-rich −1.8∘C water + enlarged hearts, wide capillaries, and low metabolic demand). A states only that they lack hemoglobin (not how they survive); B omits icefish altogether; D mentions heart size without connecting it to surviving without hemoglobin.

subSections.html:
Question Answer Format Fastest Method Leak Shield Verified
MATH-D7-Q1 21 SPR Manual (20 sec) ∞ solutions: match 6x−15=ax−b⟹a=6,b=15 (watch −b sign!)
MATH-D7-Q2 C (200) MC Manual (15 sec) "Increased by 150%" =×(1+1.50)=×2.50, NOT ×1.50!
MATH-D7-Q3 A ((0, -7)) MC Manual/Desmos (25 sec) Perpendicular slope −52​→+25​ through (4,3)
MATH-D7-Q4 80 SPR Manual/Calc (15 sec) Half-life exponent 36/12=3⟹640×(0.5)3=80
MATH-D7-Q5 C MC Manual/Desmos (25 sec) Distribute minus sign carefully: 5(x+1)−2(x−4)=3x+13
MATH-D7-Q6 15 SPR Manual/Desmos (15 sec) Box Target: asks for ticket price p (x-vertex =15), NOT max revenue 700!
MATH-D7-Q7 C (13) MC Desmos Table (12 sec) y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c gives 2x2−6x+5⟹f(4)=13
MATH-D7-Q8 4 SPR Manual/Desmos (25 sec) Tangency x2−6x+(13−k)=0⟹D=36−4(13−k)=0⟹k=4
MATH-D7-Q9 C MC Manual (15 sec) Generalize ONLY to exact sampled population (weekday morning Route B)
MATH-D7-Q10 B MC Manual (30 sec) Mean drops (24→19.125); 4th & 5th values are both 20⟹ median stays 20!
MATH-D7-Q11 B (64π) MC Manual (30 sec) VB​/VA​=64/27⟹s=4/3⟹Area scales by s2=16/9⟹64π
MATH-D7-Q12 B (5π) MC Manual (35 sec) Diameter d=10⟹r=5⟹Sector=21​(52)(52π​)=5π

Step-by-Step + Desmos Teaching Solutions

  1. MATH-D7-Q1 — Correct Answer: 21 (SPR)

    • Distribute Left Side: 3(2x−5)=6x−15.
    • Match Coefficients (Infinitely Many Solutions): Since 6x−15=ax−b for all x, a=6 and −b=−15⟹b=15 (watch the minus sign already printed before b!).
    • Boxed Target: a+b=6+15=21. (Sign trap: writing b=−15 gives −9, wrong!)

  2. MATH-D7-Q2 — Correct Answer: C (200)

    • Firewall 1 (Increased by P%): An increase of 150% adds 1.50×80=120 hectares on top of the original 80 hectares:
      80×(1+1.50)=80×2.50=200 (C)
    • Trap Alert: Choice A (120) computes 150% of 80 instead of increased by 150%!

  3. MATH-D7-Q3 — Correct Answer: A ((0, -7))

    • Find Slope of Line p: 2x+5y=20⟹5y=−2x+20⟹y=−52​x+4, so mp​=−52​.
    • Perpendicular Slope mq​: Opposite reciprocal =+25​.
    • Point-Slope Through (4,3): y−3=25​(x−4)=25​x−10⟹y=25​x−7. Thus the y-intercept is (0,−7) (A).

  4. MATH-D7-Q4 — Correct Answer: 80 (SPR)

    • Substitute t=36: Number of 12-hour half-lives =1236​=3.
    • Compute: M(36)=640(0.5)3=640×81​=80. Type 80.

  5. MATH-D7-Q5 — Correct Answer: C

    • Common Denominator (x−4)(x+1)=x2−3x−4:
      (x−4)(x+1)5(x+1)−2(x−4)​=x2−3x−45x+5−2x+8​=x2−3x−43x+13​ (C)
    • Desmos 10-Second Verification: Graph f(x) = 5/(x - 4) - 2/(x + 1) and g(x) = (3x + 13)/(x^2 - 3x - 4)—their curves overlap 100%! (Trap B forgets −2(−4)=+8 and writes 5−8=−3.)

  6. MATH-D7-Q6 — Correct Answer: 15 (SPR)

    • Firewall 2 (Box Input vs. Output!): The question asks *"At what ticket price p"* (x-coordinate of vertex), NOT "What is the maximum weekly revenue" (y-coordinate =700)!
    • Vertex Formula (or Desmos Click): p=−2ab​=−2(−4)120​=8120​=15. Type 15.

  7. MATH-D7-Q7 — Correct Answer: C (13)

    • Desmos Regression Winner (12 Seconds):
      1. Insert Table (x_1, y_1) with rows (-1, 13), (1, 1), (3, 5).
      2. On Line 2, type y_1 ~ a x_1^2 + b x_1 + c → Desmos outputs a = 2, b = -6, c = 5.
      3. Evaluate f(4)=2(4)2−6(4)+5=32−24+5=13 (C).
    • Bonus Parabolic Symmetry Shortcut: Vertex is at x=−2(2)−6​=1.5. Since x=4 is 2.5 units right of 1.5 and x=−1 is 2.5 units left of 1.5, f(4)=f(−1)=13 immediately!

  8. MATH-D7-Q8 — Correct Answer: 4 (SPR)

    • Set Equal for Intersection: x2−2x+13=4x+k⟹x2−6x+(13−k)=0.
    • Exactly One Real Solution ⟹ Discriminant =0:
      b2−4ac=(−6)2−4(1)(13−k)=36−52+4k=0⟹4k=16⟹k=4
    • Desmos Check: Graph y = x^2 - 2x + 13 and y = 4x + 4; they touch at the single tangent point (3,16)!

  9. MATH-D7-Q9 — Correct Answer: C

    • Firewall 6 (Sampling Frame = Inference Scope): Because the random sample was drawn exclusively from weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B, results generalize validly to all weekday morning ferry passengers aboard Harbor Route B (C)—neither broader to all city residents/weekend routes (A, B) nor restricted only to the 400 respondents (D).

  10. MATH-D7-Q10 — Correct Answer: B

    • Check Mean: Removing the high outlier 63 (which sits well above Dataset P's mean of 216/9=24) pulls the mean down to 153/8=19.125. Thus mean decreases.
    • Check Median (Firewall 3 — Write Middle Slots!):
      • Dataset P (9 values): 5th value =20.
      • Dataset Q (8 values: 12,14,15,20,20,22,24,26): average of 4th and 5th values =220+20​=20!
      • Because both middle slots equal 20, the medians are equal (B)! (Trap A blindly assumes dropping the max always lowers the median!)

  11. MATH-D7-Q11 — Correct Answer: B (64π)

    • Firewall 4 (s3→s→s2):
      1. Volume ratio: VA​VB​​=54π128π​=2764​.
      2. Linear scale factor: s=32764​​=34​.
      3. Surface-area scale factor: s2=(34​)2=916​.
      4. Lateral surface area of B=36π×916​=4π×16=64π (B).
    • Trap Alert: A (48π) multiplies by s=4/3; C (85π) multiplies by s3=64/27.

  12. MATH-D7-Q12 — Correct Answer: B (5π)

    • Step 1 (Distance Formula for Diameter PQ):
      d=(6−(−2))2+(7−1)2​=82+62​=100​=10
    • Step 2 (Firewall 5 — Halve Diameter Immediately!): r=210​=5.
    • Step 3 (Radian Sector Area Formula):
      Asector​=21​r2θ=21​(52)(52π​)=225​⋅52π​=5π (B)
    • Trap Alert: D (20π) plugs d=10 into 21​r2θ without dividing by 2!

errorLab.caseKeyHtml:
• EL-D7-CASE-1: Primary Code: E8 (Timing problem). Because Tariq solved M2-Q13 Right Cold in 75 seconds, he has zero inference deficit! His real leak happened earlier in Module 2 when he failed to jump straight to Q15–Q27 first (Split-Order) or stalled >75 seconds on a hard Words in Context item. Hitting Q27 -> Q15 in 10 minutes (>=22:00 remaining) gives him 95+ calm seconds for Q13 on Practice Test 6.
  • EL-D7-CASE-2: Codes: E2 (Vocabulary gap) + V2 (Knew word but selected wrong everyday meaning). 7-Step Repair: Step 2 (Simple English): qualify = limit, soften, or add conditions to a broad claim (±). Step 5 (Polysemy Trap): Everyday qualify for a race = academic qualify a sweeping thesis! Clue in sentence: "sweeping thesis" contrasted with "northern valleys remained wet" (partial exception). Step 6 (Own Sentence): "New coral cores qualified the global cooling model by showing equatorial lagoons stayed warm."
  • EL-D7-CASE-3: Code: E9 (Wrong strategy). 10-Second Desmos Retrofit: Type y = abs(3x - 6) on Line 1 and y = x + 6 on Line 2 (or type |3x - 6| = x + 6 directly to plot two vertical solution lines). Click the intersections at (0,6) and (6,12)—giving x=0 and x=6 (positive difference = 6) in 10 seconds with zero extraneous-root or case-sign risk!
  • EL-D7-CASE-4: Concession-Marker Blindness (V4, 4 occurrences across domains) triggers the 3+ Priority Escalation Tracker! Her 4 Craft and Structure misses had three unrelated root causes (V1, E4, E8), whereas missing albeit / notwithstanding / granted four times across different domains is one single high-return underlying mechanism.
  • EL-D7-CASE-5: Leaving "Exclude Active Questions" unchecked exposes Kenji to live questions drawn directly from Bluebook Practice Tests 6–11! cases.promptHtml: On Test 5 R&W M2-Q3 (Words in Context), Elena picked B) substantiate yesterday AND picked D) corroborate cold again this morning—both wrong—because the correct answer was A) qualify in "Subsequent isotope measurements helped **qualify** the sweeping monsoon-collapse thesis by showing northern valleys remained wet." Step 5 (Polysemy Trap): Everyday qualify for a race = academic qualify a sweeping thesis! Clue in sentence: "sweeping thesis" contrasted with "northern valleys remained wet" (partial exception). cases.promptHtml: On Test 5 Math M2-Q18, Min-jun missed ∣3x−6∣=x+6 yesterday (CU) and spent 4 minutes checking two algebraic sign cases this morning before getting the positive difference between the solutions (6). Click the intersections at (0,6) and (6,12)—giving x=0 and x=6 (positive difference = 6) in 10 seconds with zero extraneous-root or case-sign risk!

cases.promptHtml: Across Days 1–6, Sofia missed 4 questions in Craft and Structure: one was an unknown literary adjective (E2+V1), one was misreading "Text 2 would agree" as "disagree" (E4), and two were 75+ second stalls (E8). Her 4 Craft and Structure misses had three unrelated root causes (V1, E4, E8), whereas missing albeit / notwithstanding / granted four times across different domains is one single high-return underlying mechanism.
