mastery.introHtml: Instructions (14:45–14:55 — 10 Minutes, Closed Notes): Complete this final 10-question Week-1 Graduation Check from memory, verify against the Answer Key, and lock in your Weeks 2–3 launch schedule!

masteryItems.promptHtml: Distinguish circumscribe from circumvent, and conflate from delineate.
State the academic SAT meaning of (a) qualify, (b) check, (c) arrest, and (d) afford.
Fix the punctuation error in: "High-altitude telescopes escape lower-troposphere water vapor, consequently, infrared astronomers prize arid Chilean peaks."
Why is "Forged from meteoritic iron around 1350 BCE, archaeologists discovered Tutankhamun's dagger in 1925" grammatically broken?
What is the exact difference in study follow-up between a Test 5 question answered Right Cold vs. Wrong Cold on Day 7?
Battery energy density was 120 Wh/kg in 2010 and increased by 125% by 2025. What was the 2025 energy density in Wh/kg?
Two similar pyramids have volumes of 27 m3 and 64 m3. If the smaller pyramid has base area 18 m2, what is the base area of the larger pyramid?
Segment AB is a diameter of length 12 in a circle. What is the area of a sector with central angle 3π​ radians?
What exact equation do you type in Desmos after entering a 3-point table (x_1, y_1) to recover quadratic constants a, b, c?
Which two official Bluebook Practice Tests are scheduled during Weeks 2–3 (Nov 21 – Dec 4), and what happens to study volume during Days 19–21 (Dec 2–4) right before the December 5 SAT?

mastery.keyHtml:
• MA-D7-Q1: Circumscribe = draw strict limits/restrictions around; circumvent = cleverly bypass/get around an obstacle. Conflate = mistakenly fuse/confuse two distinct things as one; delineate = trace or mark exact boundaries clearly.
  • MA-D7-Q2: (a) qualify = limit or add conditions to a claim (±); (b) check = restrain/slow down; (c) arrest = stop/halt a process; (d) afford = provide/supply.
  • MA-D7-Q3: Replace the first comma with a semicolon (or period): "vapor;* consequently, infrared astronomers..."* (E6 conjunctive adverb comma-splice fix).
  • MA-D7-Q4: Archaeologists were not forged from meteoritic iron in 1350 BCE! The noun immediately after the comma must be Tutankhamun's dagger: "Forged from meteoritic iron around 1350 BCE, Tutankhamun's dagger was discovered by archaeologists in 1925."
  • MA-D7-Q5: Right Cold = skill is intact, fix pacing/careless execution via a 5-second IF -> THEN habit trigger (E4/E7/E8); Wrong Cold = true concept/vocabulary gap, run 7-Step Vocab Repair or targeted CB Question Bank skill repair (E1/E2/E3/E5/E6).
  • MA-D7-Q6: 270 Wh/kg — Multiplier =1+1.25=2.25⟹120×2.25=270 (never 120×1.25=150!).
  • MA-D7-Q7: 32 m2 — Volume ratio 64/27⟹ linear ratio s=364/27​=4/3⟹ area ratio s2=16/9⟹18×916​=32.

vocabStudio.howToUseHtml:
1. Daily Selection Target: Record 8–12 high-value academic words or expressions per day discovered in official SAT practice, your Error Log, or your daily workbook lessons (aim for 8 words on full-test or heavy passage-analysis days so quality stays high; 40–60 words mastered deeply by Day 7).
  2. Write Definitions in Simple English: Explain the word as if teaching a younger student in clear, everyday English. Use first-language (L1) translation only for a 5-second check if an abstract concept is still unclear—then immediately write and practise in English.
  3. Record the Logical Clue: Underline the contrast, cause-and-effect, colon, or parallel structure in the SAT sentence that proves the word's meaning.
  4. Complete Spaced Retrieval Without Looking: Cover Columns 2–6 when reviewing on scheduled dates. Test whether you can:
    • Recognize the word immediately in print.
    • Explain its meaning in simple English.
    • Identify its contextual meaning (especially secondary academic meanings, such as qualify = "limit a claim," not "meet requirements").
    • Spot logical clues around it.
    • Distinguish it from close synonyms or trap distractors.
    • Apply it accurately in a brand-new sentence or passage.
vocabStudio.wordPartsHtml:
Do not memorize dozens of obscure Latin/Greek roots. Focus only on directional prefixes and part-of-speech suffixes that help you judge positive/negative polarity and grammatical role under time pressure:

Word Part Core Signal Academic SAT Examples How It Helps Under Time Pressure
sub- under, beneath, supporting from below substantiate, subordinate, subtle Signals either foundational support (substantiate) or lower rank (subordinate).
cor- / con- / com- together, with corroborate, concur, compelling, reconcile Signals agreement, alignment, or bringing ideas together.
ambi- / equiv- both ways, equal weight ambiguous, ambivalent, equivocal Signals uncertainty, mixed feelings, or two possible meanings (never extreme certainty).
un- / in- / im- / ir- / dis- not, opposite of undermine, implausible, indifferent, disparate Flips sentence polarity immediately—watch for double negatives (not implausible = reasonable).
re- back, again reconcile, refute, resilient, retract Signals restoring harmony (reconcile) or pushing back against a claim (refute).
-ate / -ify / -ize verb ("to make or do") substantiate, scrutinize, corroborate Tells you the blank requires an action/relationship between subject and object.
-ous / -ive / -able / -ible adjective ("having the quality of") ambiguous, tentative, plausible, compelling Tells you the word modifies a noun's tone, strength, or certainty.
-tion / -ity / -ance / -ence abstract noun substantiation, ambiguity, plausibility Helps convert a familiar verb/adjective into a noun without treating it as a brand-new word.

words.simpleMeaning: To prove or support a claim with solid facts or evidence
words.satContextHtml: "Although the historian's theory was intriguing, newly uncovered trade ledgers failed to substantiate her claim."
words.satContextRaw: Although the historian's theory was intriguing, newly uncovered trade ledgers failed to substantiate her claim.
words.modelSentence: The lab team must substantiate its hypothesis with three independent trials before publishing.

words.simpleMeaning: To weaken a system, argument, or authority gradually or indirectly
words.satContextHtml: "Contradictory sensor readings from deep-sea vents undermined confidence in the original climate model."
words.satContextRaw: Contradictory sensor readings from deep-sea vents undermined confidence in the original climate model.
words.modelSentence: Relying on a tiny, biased survey undermines the credibility of the economist's conclusion.

words.simpleMeaning: To confirm or give independent evidence that another report or finding is true

words.satContextRaw: Ice-core chemical data corroborated the volcanic eruption date recorded in medieval chronicles.
words.modelSentence: Satellite images corroborated the field biologists' report of rapid glacier retreat.

words.simpleMeaning: Reasonable and believable enough to possibly be true (though not yet 100% proven)
words.satContextHtml: "Because Mars once had liquid water, researchers consider ancient microbial life a plausible hypothesis."
words.satContextRaw: Because Mars once had liquid water, researchers consider ancient microbial life a plausible hypothesis.
words.modelSentence: Delayed monsoon winds offered a plausible explanation for the sudden drop in harvest yields.

words.simpleMeaning: Open to two or more valid interpretations; unclear or not decisive
words.satContextHtml: "The treaty's ambiguous phrasing allowed both neighboring states to claim fishing rights."
words.satContextRaw: The treaty's ambiguous phrasing allowed both neighboring states to claim fishing rights.
words.modelSentence: Because the fossil layer's age remained ambiguous, paleontologists postponed naming a new species.

words.simpleMeaning: To reach a logical conclusion from evidence rather than from a direct statement
words.satContextHtml: "From microscopic wear patterns on the stone tools, archaeologists inferred that villagers harvested wild grain."
words.satContextRaw: From microscopic wear patterns on the stone tools, archaeologists inferred that villagers harvested wild grain.
words.modelSentence: Readers can infer from the narrator's hesitation that he doubts his brother's promise.

words.simpleMeaning: To make two seemingly conflicting facts, ideas, or groups fit together without contradiction
words.satContextHtml: "Quantum physicists continue working to reconcile general relativity with subatomic particle behavior."
words.satContextRaw: Quantum physicists continue working to reconcile general relativity with subatomic particle behavior.
words.modelSentence: The accountant had to reconcile the company's bank statement with its internal expense log.

words.simpleMeaning: Showing subtle, careful distinctions rather than a simple black-and-white view
words.satContextHtml: "Instead of praising or condemning urbanization outright, the sociologist offered a nuanced assessment."
words.satContextRaw: Instead of praising or condemning urbanization outright, the sociologist offered a nuanced assessment.
words.modelSentence: Our teacher gave a nuanced explanation of why trade tariffs help some local workers while hurting others.

words.simpleMeaning: Provisional, cautious, and subject to change when more evidence arrives

words.satContextRaw: Given the small patient sample, the medical team described its conclusions as strictly tentative.
words.modelSentence: We set a tentative study-group schedule for Saturday morning until exam room assignments are confirmed.

words.simpleMeaning: In spite of; nevertheless (signals concession/contrast without cancelling the main fact)

words.satContextRaw: The solar rover exceeded its mission lifespan by four years, notwithstanding severe dust storms.
words.modelSentence: Notwithstanding his limited lab budget, the graduate student designed an accurate optical sensor.

words.simpleMeaning: To strengthen, reinforce, or support an argument or institution

words.satContextRaw: Newly translated customs registries from Aden bolstered the historian's argument about family partnerships.
words.modelSentence: Independent lab replications bolstered confidence in the room-temperature sensor design.

words.simpleMeaning: To examine closely, critically, and thoroughly in detail

words.satContextRaw: Paleographers scrutinized the charter's parchment fibers and ink chemistry under ultraviolet magnification.
words.modelSentence: Before submitting my SAT Math module, I scrutinize every boxed target phrase for unit traps.

words.simpleMeaning: Powerfully convincing and persuasive due to strong evidence or logic

words.satContextRaw: Matching volcanic glass shards to an Alaskan caldera provided compelling evidence for the eruption's date.

eCodes.label: Concept gap
eCodes.description: Did not know the underlying math formula, theorem, or rhetorical principle.

eCodes.label: Vocabulary gap
eCodes.description: Unfamiliar academic word or secondary word meaning blocked comprehension or answer selection.

eCodes.label: Complex sentence misunderstanding
eCodes.description: Lost track of the main subject-verb-object because of long modifiers, appositives, dashes, or inverted syntax.

eCodes.label: Misread question
eCodes.description: Solved for x instead of 2x + 3, missed *EXCEPT / NOT / LEAST*, or misread *weakens* as *supports*.

eCodes.label: Incorrect inference
eCodes.description: Chose an answer that stretched beyond the text ("too extreme," "unsupported causal leap," or outside assumption).

eCodes.label: Grammar rule forgotten
eCodes.description: Misapplied sentence boundaries (comma splice), subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, pronouns, or modifiers.

eCodes.label: Careless mistake
eCodes.description: Sign flip (-3² vs (-3)²), copying error, misreading axis units/scale, or clicking the wrong option letter.

eCodes.label: Timing problem
eCodes.description: Spent >2.5 minutes stalling on one hard question or rushed the final 4–5 questions in a module.

eCodes.label: Wrong strategy
eCodes.description: Expanded messy algebra by hand for 3 minutes when plugging in a point or graphing in Desmos took 20 seconds.

eCodes.label: Calculator or Desmos misuse
eCodes.description: Parentheses typo, radians vs. degrees mismatch, zoomed-out window hiding a second intersection, or misreading vertex coordinates.

vCodes.label: Did not know word meaning
vCodes.description: Target word in the stem, passage, or correct answer was completely unfamiliar.

vCodes.label: Knew word but selected the wrong meaning
vCodes.description: Fell for a common everyday meaning when the SAT tested a secondary academic sense (e.g., *check* = restrain; *qualify* = limit; *arrest* = stop).

vCodes.label: Misunderstood sentence structure
vCodes.description: Knew the individual words, but modifiers, participial phrases, or double negatives scrambled who did what to whom.

vCodes.label: Missed a contrast or cause-and-effect clue
vCodes.description: Overlooked a pivot signal (*nevertheless, notwithstanding, albeit, conversely, consequently, whereas*) that dictated the blank's logic.

vCodes.label: Confused similar answer choices
vCodes.description: Narrowed to 2 choices with similar positive/negative tone (e.g., *tentative* vs. *ambiguous*, or *corroborate* vs. *assert*) and picked the imprecise match.

vCodes.label: Misunderstood the author's tone
vCodes.description: Confused neutral analytical description with strong praise/attack, or missed hedged academic caution (*suggests, may, plausible*).

vCodes.label: Failed to connect evidence to the claim
vCodes.description: Read the passage and quote accurately at the surface level, but chose data/text that proved the *wrong* part of the hypothesis.

errorLogStudio.escalationHtml:
Essential Rule

Distinguish an Underlying Root Weakness from Broad Domain Coincidence:

  • NOT a single recurring pattern: Missing 3 questions in Craft and Structure where one was an unknown noun (V1), one was a cross-text main-claim misread (E4), and one was running out of time (E8). Those are three separate issues.
  • TRUE priority recurring pattern (Flag Immediately!): Missing 3 questions across different topics (e.g., 1 Words in Context, 1 Transitions, 1 Inferences) because all three times you missed a concession pivot (V4) such as nevertheless, albeit, or regardless.

Action Rule: Whenever the exact same error code or underlying mechanism appears 3 or more times, add it to the Priority Escalation Table below and dedicate the first 15 minutes of your next topic block to targeted repair before attempting mixed sets.

modelEntries.whyMissed: `E2` + `V4`: Missed "Although" at the start of the sentence and picked a synonym of the first clause instead of a contrast.
modelEntries.correctMethod: "Although Clause A (+), Clause B (-)" requires opposite polarity between clauses.
modelEntries.nextTimeRule: Circle concession markers (`although, despite, notwithstanding, whereas`) and write `+` or `-` above the blank before reading A–D.

modelEntries.whyMissed: `E4` + `E7`: Solved correctly for `x = 4`, `y = 7`, then entered `4` when the prompt asked for `x + y`.
modelEntries.correctMethod: Substitute `(4, 7)` into both equations (or check intersection in Desmos) and underline the exact target expression.
modelEntries.nextTimeRule: Before typing any SPR answer, box the final phrase after "what is the value of..." and re-read it once.
